author: copilot
body:
XcodeGen generates `objectVersion = 77` (Xcode 16 format); the `macos-14` runner ships Xcode 15, which cannot open it, causing an immediate failure on `xcodebuild -list`.

## Changes

- **Runner**: `macos-14` → `macos-15`
- **Xcode selection**: new step after Checkout explicitly picks the latest Xcode 16.x; fails fast with a clear message if none is found:
  ```yaml
  - name: Select Xcode 16
    run: |
      XCODE16=$(ls -d /Applications/Xcode_16*.app 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -n1)
      if [ -z "$XCODE16" ]; then
        echo "No Xcode 16.x installation found in /Applications" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      sudo xcode-select -s "$XCODE16/Contents/Developer"
      xcodebuild -version
  ```
- **Build step**: removed `|| true` from the `xcodebuild | xcbeautify` pipeline — real build failures now correctly fail the job (`set -o pipefail` was already in place)

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Problem

The `iOS Build (App + App Clip)` workflow ([`.github/workflows/ios-build.yml`](https://github.com/eberthecho/minitest/blob/main/.github/workflows/ios-build.yml)) is failing on the `List schemes` step with:

```
xcodebuild: error: Unable to read project 'ProductApp.xcodeproj'.
Reason: The project 'ProductApp' cannot be opened because it is in a future Xcode project file format (77).
Adjust the project format using a compatible version of Xcode to allow it to be opened by this version of Xcode.
##[error]Process completed with exit code 74.
```

Failing run: https://github.com/eberthecho/minitest/actions/runs/25770862208/job/75693491640

### Root cause

The job runs on `macos-14`, which ships Xcode 15.x. The current XcodeGen (installed via `brew install xcodegen` in the workflow) generates `ProductApp.xcodeproj` with `objectVersion = 77`, which requires Xcode 16+. Xcode 15 cannot read this format, so `xcodebuild -list` (and any subsequent build) fails immediately.

## Required fix

Update `.github/workflows/ios-build.yml`:

1. Change `runs-on: macos-14` to `runs-on: macos-15`.
2. Add a step (right after `Checkout`) that selects Xcode 16 explicitly so we don't depend on the runner's default:

   ```yaml
   - name: Select Xcode 16
     run: sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode_16.app/Contents/Developer
   ```

   If `/Applications/Xcode_16.app` is not present on the macos-15 image (image contents shift over time), fall back to picking the latest installed Xcode 16.x, e.g.:

   ```yaml
   - name: Select Xcode 16
     run: |
       sudo xcode-select -s "$(ls -d /Applications/Xcode_16*.app | sort -V | tail -n1)/Contents/Developer"
       xcodebuild -version
   ```

   Use whichever form is cleaner; the second is more robust.

3. Remove the trailing `|| true` from the `Build ProductApp (Simulator, unsigned)` step so real build failures actually fail the job (we already have `set -o pipefail`):

   ```yaml
   build | xcbeautify --renderer github-actions
   ```

Do not change anything else (paths filter, artifact upload, etc.). Keep `timeout-minutes: 25`.

## Acceptance criteria

- The workflow file `.github/workflows/ios-build.yml` is updated as described above.
- A push triggering the workflow results in a successful build, with `xcodebuild -list` succeeding and the `.app` artifact uploaded.
- No other files in the repository need to be modified.

The following is the prior conversation context from the user's chat exploration (may be truncated):

User: Please find a solution for this failing job. Use the logs, job definition, and any referenced files where the failure occurred. Keep your response focused on the solution and include code suggestions when appropriate.

Assistant: ## Problem

The job failed at the `List schemes` step with this error:

```
xcodebuild: error: Unable to read project 'ProductApp.xcodeproj'.
Reason: The project 'ProductApp' cannot be opened because it is in a future Xcode project file format (77).
```

The runner is `macos-14`, which ships Xcode 15.x. XcodeGen on that runner is generating a project in **objectVersion 77**, which requires Xcode 16+.

[View the failing workflow](https://github.com/eberthecho/minitest/blob/406adf7020a4b3665db01d476c50726a35b41e9a/.github/workflows/ios-build.yml)

## Solution

You have two main options:

### Option 1 (recommended): Upgrade the runner to `macos-15` and select Xcode 16

```yaml
jobs:
  build:
    name: Build for Simulator (no signing)
    runs-on: macos-15      # ← was macos-14
    timeout-minutes: 25

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Select Xcode 16
        run: sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode_16.app/Contents/Developer

      - name: Show toolchain
        run: |
          xcodebuild -version
          swift --version
      # ... rest unchanged
```

Project format 77 is produced by Xcode 16, so this matches what XcodeGen is emitting.

### Option 2: Force XcodeGen to emit an older project format

If you must stay on `macos-14` / Xcode 15, pin the object version in your `project.yml`:

```yaml
# ios/project.yml
options:
  objectVersion: 56     # Xcode 15 compatible (54–56 work)
  # or: compatibilityVersion: "Xcode 14"
```

Then regenerate. Note: very new XcodeGen releases default to 77; if pinning doesn't help, also pin XcodeGen in the workflow:

```yaml
- name: Install XcodeGen
  run: brew install xcodegen   # consider pinning to a known-good version
```

### Bonus fix

In the build step you have `|| true` at the end of the `xcodebuild ... | xcbeautify` pipeline. That swallows real build failures and will make later steps misleading. Consider removing it:

```yaml
build | xcbeautify --renderer github-actions
```

`set -o pipefail` is already set, so the real exit code will surface properly.

Хотите, чтобы я открыл pull requ...

</details>

author: wesleysimplicio
body:
## Problem

Setting `gateway_restart_notification: false` under a platform section (e.g. `telegram:`) in `config.yaml` had no effect — restart/shutdown notifications were always sent regardless of the configured value.

## Root Cause

`load_gateway_config()` in `gateway/config.py` bridges individual YAML keys into the internal `PlatformConfig` dataclass via an explicit allowlist. `gateway_restart_notification` was missing from that list, so it was never forwarded and always fell back to its default value of `True`.

## Fix

1. Add `gateway_restart_notification` to the bridge list (copy from `platform_cfg` → `bridged`).
2. Pop it from `bridged` directly into `plat_data` before `extra.update(bridged)` — required because it is a first-class `PlatformConfig` field, not an extra.

## Tests

Added regression test `test_bridges_telegram_gateway_restart_notification_from_config_yaml` to `tests/gateway/test_config.py`:
- Parses a minimal YAML with `telegram: gateway_restart_notification: false`
- Asserts `config.platforms[Platform.TELEGRAM].gateway_restart_notification is False`

Closes #24644

author: yimin12
body:
## Summary

Implements two policy pieces from the multi-account-sync spec, both fully tested and configurable:

1. **Daily sync cadence** — one upload per day by default, with a force-override for explicit user actions.
2. **5-device limit per (team, user)** — env-configurable; existing devices unaffected when cap is reached.

**Net diff vs PR #17 base**: 2 commits, 8 files, ~365 lines (mostly tests + comments).
**Tests**: project suite 207 → 217 ✓ (+10 new).

> Stacks on top of PR #17 (multi-node usage merge). Will rebase cleanly onto main once #17 lands.

## What's in this PR

### Server: device limit
- \`TeamService(pool, { maxDevicesPerUser })\` — default 5.
- Batch-scoped \`(team, user) → Set<node_id>\` cache, hydrated once per user per batch and mutated as new nodes land. Per design §"Efficiency Guarantees" the lookup is O(unique users) not O(rows).
- Existing devices never hit the cap; only the (N+1)th brand-new node_id from one user is rejected with reason \`device_limit_exceeded\`.
- \`server/index.ts\` reads \`LCM_MAX_DEVICES_PER_USER\` (non-positive / NaN → fall back to default).

### Client: daily cadence + force
- \`DrainConfig.intervalMs\` (default 24h via \`DEFAULT_TEAM_SYNC.intervalMs\`) — minimum time between *successful* uploads, enforced inside \`SyncQueue\`.
- Failed drains do **not** push the window forward, so a flaky server can't stretch the schedule to multiple days.
- New main-process wake-up tick at fixed 5min — just probes whether the cadence gate has opened. Failed-then-retry recovery happens within minutes, not 24h.
- \`SyncQueue.forceDrain()\` bypasses the gate. \`SYNC_DRAIN\` IPC (the "Sync Now" button) now calls it so explicit user actions always run.
- \`SyncStatus.nextSyncAt = lastSyncAt + intervalMs\` (null while disabled / pre-first-sync) for the renderer's "Next sync at …" hint.

## Invariants under test (+10)

| File | Test |
|---|---|
| \`team-service.test.ts\` | first 5 accepted, 6th rejected, existing nodes unaffected |
| \`team-service.test.ts\` | cap is per (team, user) — different users share no quota |
| \`team-service.test.ts\` | cap is configurable via constructor (tighter cap rejects sooner) |
| \`team-service.test.ts\` | same batch with 7 new nodes from one user → 5 accepted / 2 rejected |
| \`sync-queue.test.ts\` | drain skips with \`rate_limited\` when interval has not elapsed |
| \`sync-queue.test.ts\` | forceDrain bypasses the rate-limit gate |
| \`sync-queue.test.ts\` | failed drain does NOT push the rate-limit window forward |
| \`sync-queue.test.ts\` | getStatus surfaces \`nextSyncAt = lastSyncAt + intervalMs\` |

Existing sync-queue cases got \`intervalMs: 0\` in their shared config so the gate doesn't interfere with cases unrelated to scheduling.

## Operator controls

| Knob | Where | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Per-user device cap | \`LCM_MAX_DEVICES_PER_USER\` env (server) | 5 |
| Sync interval | \`teamSync.intervalMs\` setting (client) | 86_400_000 (24h) |
| Manual sync | renderer "Sync Now" button → \`forceDrain\` | always available |

## Test plan

- [x] \`npx vitest run\` — 217/217 ✓
- [x] All three tsconfig typechecks clean
- [x] Cross-instance / cross-user invariants from #17 still pass

## Out of scope

- Per-team device cap (e.g. paid teams get 10). Schema-wise easy (column on \`teams\`) but waiting on product call.
- UI surface for the new \`nextSyncAt\` hint + "Sync Now" button. Renderer changes live in a follow-up branch.

## Summary

Promotes Meta Ads from a planned provider direction to an explicit `readiness` state backed by Meta's official `meta-ads` / `meta` CLI path.
Adds public-safe setup, support-level, and UX notes while keeping live account access, token storage, raw exports, and mutation out of scope.

## Linked issue

Closes #542

## Why

Main Branch needed an honest answer for whether Meta Ads support should be `planned`, `readiness`, or `read_only`.
The official CLI is real and installable, but `mb` should not claim live read-only support until it owns detection, auth-state reporting, and sanitized account/campaign/insights smoke.

## Commits by concern

- [ ] Each commit body bullet-lists the changes in that commit
- [x] Reviewer reading `git log --oneline main..HEAD` sees the shape of the work
- [x] Commit subjects use `[add]`, `[update]`, `[fix]`, `[remove]`, `[refactor]`, `[docs]`, or `[chore]`

Commits:

- `fbe0119 [update] MAIN-350 Verify Meta Ads readiness path`
- `f5d4646 [add] MAIN-350 Capture Meta connect UX notes`

## Validation

Pre-push gate from repo root:

```bash
scripts/check.sh
```

- [x] Level 1 static: `scripts/check.sh` passes
- [x] Level 2 CLI contract: focused Typer/CliRunner tests, exit codes, `--json` behavior, TTY vs non-TTY (if CLI behavior touched)
- [x] Level 3 package/install smoke (if packaging touched)
- [ ] Level 4 fixture repo (if init/onboard/status/start/update touched)
- [ ] Level 5 runtime smoke / dogfood harness / simulation-tier (if runtime, first-run, skill discovery, or release validation touched)
- [x] SKILL.md ≤500 lines (if any skill touched)
- [ ] Package-visible release gate evidence before tag/publish (if preparing a release)
- [ ] Supply-chain review (if `.github/workflows/`, `.github/dependabot.yml`, `mb/pyproject.toml` deps, or `id-token`/`permissions` blocks touched — see [docs/supply-chain-policy.md](../docs/supply-chain-policy.md))

Evidence:

- Level 0 docs/decision: `git diff --check` — runtime: system git — exit: 0 — log: no whitespace errors.
- Level 1 static: `scripts/check.sh` — runtime: repo default Python — exit: 0 — log: `All checks passed!`, `Success: no issues found in 80 source files`, `598 passed`, coverage `83.56%`, skill validation passed.
- Level 2 CLI contract: `cd mb && pytest tests/test_connect.py -q` — runtime: repo test environment — exit: 0 — log: `29 passed in 5.13s`.
- Level 3 package/install smoke: `(cd mb && python3 -m build)` plus wheel install in a throwaway Python 3.13 venv, `mb --version`, `mb skill list`, and installed `mb educational provider-readiness` check — runtime: Python 3.13 throwaway venv — exit: 0 — log: `mb 0.3.19` and Meta readiness text present.
- Provider CLI smoke: `meta-ads==1.0.1` installed in an isolated Python 3.13 environment; `meta --version`, `meta ads --help`, and no-token `meta auth status` behaved as expected — exit: 0 for version/help, exit: 3 for missing token with no token printed.

Not required:

- Level 4 fixture repo was not required because this PR does not change onboarding, generated repo layout, or fixture runtime behavior.
- Level 5 runtime/live Meta smoke was not run because this PR does not claim `read_only`, `reporting`, mutation, or live account support.
- Package-visible release gate and supply-chain review were not required because this PR does not prepare a release or change workflows, dependencies, permissions, or publishing configuration.

## Success metric

`mb connect` reports Meta Ads as `readiness`, not connected/read-only, and users/agents can find the official CLI setup path plus the exact follow-up boundary for future read-only support.

## CHANGELOG

- [x] Updated `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]` section, OR
- [ ] N/A — change is invisible to users (internal refactor, CI-only, etc.)

## Breaking changes

- [x] No
- [ ] Yes — migration note below

## Public / private boundary

No tokens, account IDs, system user IDs, raw account exports, screenshots, local private paths, or customer/member data are committed.
The Meta UX report preserves only sanitized setup lessons and explicitly keeps live account access out of the shipped support claim.

Closes #137

## 変更 detail

3 file × 同一 bash block を以下に変換:

**Before**:
```bash
SLUG=$(~/.claude/skills/uzustack/browse/bin/remote-slug 2>/dev/null || basename "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)")
BRANCH=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null | tr '/' '-' || echo 'no-branch')
```

**After**:
```bash
eval "$(~/.claude/skills/uzustack/bin/uzustack-slug 2>/dev/null)"
SLUG="${SLUG:-$(basename "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)")}"
BRANCH="${BRANCH:-$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null | tr '/' '-' || echo 'no-branch')}"
```

合計 +18 / -12 (3 file × .tmpl + 生成 .md の 6 file)、 `bun run gen:skill-docs` で生成済。

## 設計判断

| 項目 | 採用 | 理由 |
|---|---|---|
| canonical pattern | `eval "$(uzustack-slug)"` | 既存翻訳済 skill (`design-html`、 `plan-tune`、 `design-shotgun`) と一貫 |
| uzustack-bin 直呼び | `~/.claude/skills/uzustack/bin/uzustack-slug` | voice 規約 v1 / `.claude/rules/workflow.md` の plan-ceo-review 規律遵守 |
| fallback articulate | `${SLUG:-...}` / `${BRANCH:-...}` | issue Acceptance criteria 「browse 機構なくても動く保証」 を defensive に表現 |
| `setopt +o nomatch` | 保持 | zsh compat 用、 各 file の既存 wording (コメントあり / なし) を尊重 |

## 検証 (smoke test 実施済)

### canonical path (uzustack-slug 利用可)

```
$ eval "$(~/.claude/skills/uzustack/bin/uzustack-slug 2>/dev/null)"
SLUG=uzumaki-inc-uzustack
BRANCH=fixplan-skill-broken-bin-reference
```

### fallback path (uzustack-slug bin missing 想定)

```
$ eval "$(/non-existent-bin 2>/dev/null)"
$ SLUG="${SLUG:-$(basename "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)")}"
$ BRANCH="${BRANCH:-$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null | tr '/' '-' || echo 'no-branch')}"
SLUG=uzustack
BRANCH=fix-plan-skill-broken-bin-reference
```

両 path で空文字 / undefined にならず、 design doc lookup の subsequent line (`ls -t ~/.uzustack/projects/$SLUG/*-$BRANCH-design-*.md`) が安全に動作する保証。

## /simplify audit trail (2 周実施、 標準 protocol)

### Round 1 (actionable findings、 3 agent 並列)

| Agent | finding | 重要度 | 仕分け |
|---|---|---|---|
| reuse | 既存 5 canonical site (`design-html`、 `plan-tune`、 `design-shotgun` 等) は `eval "$(uzustack-slug)"` 単独で `${VAR:-...}` fallback 無し → 新 3 site は divergent pattern | low | **skip** — issue #137 Acceptance criteria 「fallback を articulate」 と整合、 「behaviorally equivalent」 評価、 5 既存 site 伝播は scope 拡大 |
| quality | bash quality 全 check 通過 (eval safety / `${:-}` semantics / echo chain / copy-paste / comment) | — | No actionable findings |
| edge case | 全 edge case 妥当 (non-git / external env / glob 暴走不可 / setopt) | — | No actionable findings |

### Round 2 (cross-validation + drift 検出、 `/simplify` skill 再 invocation で 3 agent 並列)

| Agent | Round 1 confirmation | 新規 finding (cross-validation で surface) | 重要度 |
|---|---|---|---|
| reuse | confirmed (defensive fallback 意図的 skip) | helper bin 抽出却下 (scope)、 broken bin 0 残存、 upstream divergence は守期間規律と整合 | none |
| quality | confirmed | 1) eval 失敗時 silent swallow は graceful degradation 意図通り / 2) **旧 `\|\| echo 'no-branch'` も dead code (tr exit status のみ反応) = 新 pattern は旧 dead code を継承、 semantics drift なし** / 3) fallback sanitize 非対称 (basename 側 unsanitized、 git toplevel basename で特殊文字稀、 許容範囲) | low × 2、 none × 1 |
| efficiency | confirmed | 1) `git rev-parse` worst case 3 回呼出だが bash `${VAR:-default}` short-circuit で正常 path で fallback 評価されない (実 invoke 増えず) / 2) cache bypass 整合 OK / 3) canonical divergence は防御層として正当 | low × 2、 none × 1 |

**Round 2 verdict (3 agent 独立)**: 全 agent が「3 周目不要、 即時修正候補なし、 merge ready」 に独立到達。

### Round 2 で得た深掘り insight

- **BRANCH semantics の旧 dead code 継承**: 旧 `BRANCH=$(... | tr '/' '-' || echo 'no-branch')` の `|| echo 'no-branch'` は **元から dead code** (tr が空入力でも success exit するため発火しない)。 新 pattern の `${BRANCH:-... || echo 'no-branch'}` 内も同様 dead code を継承。 「articulate」 した fallback の中身が旧 dead code であった事実は specificity drift ではなく **semantics 等価性の証明** (= 旧挙動を完全保持)
- **BRANCH sanitization の cross-path divergence**: uzustack-slug 内 `tr -cd 'a-zA-Z0-9._-'` (strip `/`) vs fallback `tr '/' '-'` (convert)。 同 branch でも path で BRANCH 値が異なるが、 SLUG が dominant key で実害なし。 uzustack-slug 側の sanitize 統一は将来 task として deferred

### 仕分け原則

`.claude/rules/review.md` 「Round 2 specificity drift 検出時は即時修正 + audit trail、 3 周目を回さない」 の解釈:
- drift が **spec 違反 (= 原文逸脱)** → 即時修正
- drift が **acceptable divergence (= 両 path で生きる中の差)** → audit trail のみ

本件 Round 1 + Round 2 findings は全 後者に該当、 即時修正対象なし。 3 周目不要。

## sanitize self-check

- commit message / branch 名 (`fix/plan-skill-broken-bin-reference`) / PR title / PR body に個人固有名 / 絶対 path 不在 (新規律 PR #146 application target 2 件目)
- 変更内容に `~/.claude/skills/uzustack/...` (placeholder 形式) のみ含み、 実 username / vault 名なし

## Test plan

- [x] 3 SKILL.md.tmpl 編集 + `bun run gen:skill-docs` で 3 SKILL.md 自動再生成 (合計 6 file の整合 commit)
- [x] uzustack proper の broken pattern `browse/bin/remote-slug` 残存 grep — 0 件確認 (CHANGELOG.md の履歴記述と greptile-triage.md は scope 外)
- [x] canonical path smoke test (= uzustack-slug 利用可) → 正常 output
- [x] fallback path smoke test (= uzustack-slug missing 想定) → 期待 default 値
- [x] pre-publish sanitize grep on diff / commit message / branch 名 / PR title / PR body — 全 NO LEAKS
- [x] /simplify Round 1 (actionable findings、 3 agent 並列) — 1 low finding intentional skip
- [x] /simplify Round 2 (cross-validation + drift、 skill 再 invocation で 3 agent 並列) — 4 low findings + 2 none、 全 acceptable divergence で skip、 3 周目不要 verdict
- [x] CI: Skill Docs Freshness check PASSED (= .tmpl ↔ .md 整合確認済)

## Out of scope

- **`review/greptile-triage.md:37,186`**: 同種 broken pattern (`~/.claude/skills/uzustack/browse/bin/remote-slug`) 残存だが、 変数名 `REMOTE_SLUG`、 3-tier fallback、 greptile 統合 context と異なる concerns。 別 issue で扱う
- **`_upstream/gstack/` 配下の同 pattern**: upstream tech debt 観測リスト行き (uzustack 単独修正保留、 守期間規律)
- **CHANGELOG.md:35 の記述更新**: ship タイミングで bump 時に処理 (本 PR は fix のみ、 CHANGELOG entry 化は別判断)
- **BRANCH sanitization の cross-path 統一**: uzustack-slug 側の `tr -cd` と fallback `tr '/' '-'` の divergence、 acceptable な実害なし divergence として skip。 統一する場合は別 task で uzustack-slug の sanitize 仕様変更を含む scope
- **canonical 5 site への fallback 伝播**: design-html / plan-tune / design-shotgun 等の既存 `eval` 単独 site に `${VAR:-...}` defensive 層を伝播するか否か。 acceptable divergence と評価され本 PR scope 外、 将来必要時に判断

author: seanmousseau
body:
Release PR for **v3.28.0 — DR + security stabilization**. Merges `dev` → `main`.

## Verification
- Static gate green on `dev`: `phpstan analyse` (level 9, [OK]), `phpcs`, `phpunit` (1055 tests, 0 fail), `semgrep` (0 findings), `php -l`.
- 3-driver dockerized gate green: bootstrap + Playwright (`--project=chromium`: sqlite 782✓ / mysql 752✓ / pgsql 752✓, 0 failures) + `test_api.sh` (197 PASS each) on SQLite, MySQL, PostgreSQL.
- Restore path verified **end-to-end in docker** (the `database`-format SQLite restore fix below, the gzip-bomb-cap follow-up, and the IPAMBKL1 logical path on all three engines + cross-engine; wrong-vault-key negative aborts cleanly).
- Backup-format fixture library built + decrypt-verified + restore-verified for all three engines (local, git-ignored — `tests/fixtures/backup-library/`).
- Deployed to the SQLite testing instance and visually inspected (dashboard, Backups → Destinations/Restore, Health, step-up gate — no console errors).
- Release bundle: `releases/ipam-3.28.0/ipam-3.28.0.tar.gz` — SHA256 `fcdd59408aac433a1af04d722ca6e83769816cf613d373e83630ea4d78c23229`.

## Follow-ups filed (not in this release)
- #1176 — remove dead `ipam_backup_vault_key_or_init()` (no caller since #1164's resolver refactor) → v3.28.1
- #1177 — `restore.php` mysql/pgsql restore path ignores `db_dsn` (+ lacks `--clean`/`ON_ERROR_STOP`) → v3.28.1
- #1178 — install-root-secret lifecycle consistency: auto-generate + announce `app_secret` like `bootstrap_key`; "Install keys" status panel → v3.28.2

---

## [3.28.0] - 2026-05-12

DR + security stabilization release. Concurrency hardening on two racy state writes (a TOCTOU in the per-IP rate-limit audit dampener and a lost-update on the backup-notification cooldown blobs), the surgical security fixes carried over from the v3.27.x verification passes, the step-up coverage sweep, and the start of the legacy backup-encryption retirement. One schema migration — `3.28.0-state-tables` — adds two state tables, `rate_limit_dampener` and `backup_state`.

> **Note on the semver bump:** this MINOR release removes a code path — the `app_secret`-derived backup-encryption *write* path (see Removed below). That's a deliberate, telegraphed step toward the v4.0.0 cold break: the *reader* for legacy `app_secret`-encrypted archives is retained through the entire v3.x line, and the standalone `tools/decrypt-backup.php` recovery tool covers v4.0.0 and beyond. No config-format change, no removed feature, no data loss on upgrade. Full migration path: `docs/upgrading.md` § v3.28.0.

### Added

- **CSP regression guard in CI** (#906). A new Playwright spec (`csp-no-inline.spec.ts`) crawls the authenticated page roster plus the login page and fails the build if any served HTML contains an inline `<script>` (without `src=`) or a `<style>` block — both of which silently break under the app's `script-src 'self'` / `style-src 'self'` Content-Security-Policy in production. Guards against re-introducing the v3.27.7-class regression where inline page JS quietly stopped running. (No app change; all audited pages were already clean.)

### Changed

- **Backup documentation corrected and expanded.** `backups.md` gains a prominent **"Disaster recovery — back up your keys, not just your data"** section (what to save off-site — `config.php`, the exported vault key, the passphrase — and a "can I recover this archive?" table per format); the stale claim that `backup_vault_key` lives in `config.php` is fixed across `backups.md` / `configuration.md` (since v3.26.0 it's stored *wrapped* in the `settings` table under `bootstrap_key`, which lives in `config.php`); `configuration.md` documents `bootstrap_key` and the v3.28.0 "vault key is set via the UI, not auto-generated" behaviour; `restore.md` prerequisites and recovery scenarios now cover the `.ipambkp3` vault-key / passphrase cases, not just legacy `.enc`. The lingering "v3.21.x — Logical runner not yet shipped" framing in `backups.md` was also removed (Logical backups shipped in v3.23.0).
- **OIDC settings inputs carry explicit `autocomplete` hints** (#1137). The OIDC client-secret field and related inputs were tripping browser password managers into offering to save/fill them; added per-field `autocomplete` hints so the OIDC config form behaves like configuration, not credentials.

### Deprecated

- **`app_secret`-based backup encryption (#1164).** Encrypting backups with the `config.php` `app_secret` value is deprecated. The *write* path is removed now (see Removed); the in-app *reader* for legacy `app_secret`-encrypted archives (IPAMBKP1 / IPAMBKP2) and bare SQLite/`.sql.gz` dumps is **retained through the v3.x line and removed in v4.0.0 (cold break)**. From v4.0.0, `tools/decrypt-backup.php` is the only in-product way to recover plaintext from a pre-v4 legacy archive. The Backups → Destinations and Backups → Restore tabs now carry a persistent retirement banner. Migration path (re-key under the backup vault key, or keep the `app_secret` + decrypt tool as an escape hatch): `docs/upgrading.md` § v3.28.0. Decrypt-tool conformance evidence: `releases/ipam-3.28.0/decrypt-pass1-results.md` (#1165).

### Removed

- **`app_secret` backup-encryption write path** (#1164). The backup orchestrator no longer falls back to encrypting scheduled backups with `app_secret` when no backup vault key is configured — it now fails preflight with an actionable message (a `status=failed` run with a synthetic `(preflight-failed-…)` name + a `backup.preflight_failed` audit) pointing at the vault key (Stored mode) or a passphrase export (Transitory mode). Installs that already configured the backup vault key (the recommended path since v3.26.0) are unaffected. The standalone `tools/decrypt-backup.php` recovery tool was hardened in passing during the #1165 conformance run — `--help` exits 0 with per-format examples, `--out -` streams to stdout, `--force` is required to overwrite an existing output file, conflicting credentials are rejected up front, a wrong-credential-type or unrecognised archive exits 2 with a clear message, and bare `.sql.gz` / `.ipambkl1.gz` / SQL-text archives pass through verbatim.
- **`backup.vault_key.sudo_failed` audit alias removed.** v3.27.0 migrated the vault-key sudo gate to the unified `ipam_sudo_verify()` helper (which emits `auth.sudo_failed`) and retained the legacy `backup.vault_key.sudo_failed` row as a parallel emit for one release so existing log queries wouldn't break. That release window is over; the alias is gone. SIEM rules that need vault-specific filtering should correlate `auth.sudo_failed` with the adjacent `backup.vault_key.*` row on the same IP/user — see `docs/internal/audit-actions.md`. The vault-reveal-specific per-IP rate-limit hit is unaffected.

### Fixed

- **Restoring a `database`-type SQLite backup (`.sql.gz`, and IPAMBKP1/IPAMBKP2 `.enc` archives wrapping one) now works through the Restore wizard.** The Database-format apply path (`ipam_restore_apply()`) wrapped the replay in its own transaction and then re-executed the dump's own `BEGIN TRANSACTION;` — a hard error ("cannot start a transaction within a transaction") — so the restore aborted on the first non-comment statement; the dump also ships the schema as `CREATE TABLE` with no `DROP`, so it would have collided with the live install's schema, and a whole-chunk `str_starts_with(ltrim(...), '--')` skip silently dropped every comment-prefixed `CREATE TABLE`. The apply path now drops the existing user tables first (FK enforcement is already off, so this doesn't cascade child rows), then replays the dump's statements through a normaliser (`ipam_restore_normalize_replay_statement()`) that strips leading `-- comment` lines and skips the dump's own transaction-control / `PRAGMA` statements; the dry-run preview uses the same normaliser so its `CREATE TABLE` accounting is accurate. A Database-format restore is a full replace (including `audit_log`, which the logical-format path preserves). The logical (`IPAMBK

author: kachawla
body:
## Summary

Update the UCP initializer service to support embedded resource type manifests via `fs.FS`. When an embedded filesystem is provided, the initializer processes those manifests first, then proceeds with directory-based registration as before.

This is **PR 3 of 4** implementing [automated default registration of resource types from resource-types-contrib](https://github.com/radius-project/radius/blob/main/eng/design-notes/extensibility/2026-04-automated-default-resource-type-registration.md).

## Changes

### `pkg/ucp/initializer/service.go`

- `Service` struct gains `embeddedFS fs.FS` field
- `NewService` accepts an additional `fs.FS` parameter
- `Run()` processes embedded manifests first via `LoadDefaultManifests`, then directory-based manifests
- Embedded providers are registered via `registerResourceProviderDirect` (direct database writes), consistent with existing directory-based registration

### `pkg/ucp/initializer/service_test.go`

- Updated `newTestService` to accept `fs.FS` parameter
- All existing tests pass `nil` for backwards compatibility
- New test: "registers embedded manifests" — verifies embedded FS registration works
- New test: "registers both embedded and directory manifests" — verifies both sources coexist
- New test: "directory manifests override embedded manifests" — verifies last-write-wins behavior

### `pkg/ucp/server/server.go`

- Updated `NewService` call to pass `nil` — **no behavior change** until the wiring PR connects `resource-types-contrib`

## Startup flow after this PR

```
Run()
  |-- if embeddedFS != nil:
  |     |-- manifest.LoadDefaultManifests(ctx, embeddedFS) -> []ResourceProvider
  |     +-- for each provider: registerResourceProviderDirect()
  |
  +-- if manifestDir != "":
        |-- os.ReadDir(manifestDir)
        +-- for each file: ValidateManifest() -> registerResourceProviderDirect()
```

Directory-based manifests can override embedded ones (UCP uses `Save` which is a create-or-update).

## Next PR

- **PR 4**: Wire `resource-types-contrib` dependency, pass `DefaultManifests` in `server.go`, remove migrated manifest files

### Motivation
- Provide an on-screen dual-joystick input for mobile / touch-capable environments used during GitHub Pages testing so players can tap-and-drag to move and aim without a mouse or keyboard. 
- Keep existing desktop input paths intact by mapping touch input into the same virtual inputs (WASD and mouse) used by the game logic.

- Added touch handling and state to `src/input.ts`: new touch tracking fields, `onTouchStart`/`onTouchMove`/`onTouchEnd` handlers, `isMobileLike` detection, stick clamping/dead-zone logic, and cleanup in `destroy()`.

- Added `drawTouchJoysticks(ctx)` to render stick base/knob visuals and integrated it into the main render flow by calling `Input.drawTouchJoysticks(ctx)` in `src/game.ts` so sticks are visible during play.

body:
### Motivation
- Add a small, linear connected-zone progression (shallows → kelp → carcass → cold_current → todo_domain) so the player is pushed through ecosystem layers toward the Tododon encounter without creating an open world.
- Keep all mutable runtime progression state inside `gameState` and expose tuning only via `CONFIG` to avoid hardcoded values and NaN/undefined propagation.
- Provide subtle visual and gameplay cues (background tint, pressure overlay, spawn tuning, exit indicator, boundary message) to make each zone feel distinct while preserving existing `phase` flows.

### Description
- Added zone tuning under `CONFIG.zones` and world tuning under `CONFIG.world` (transition timing, pressure multipliers, messages, exit indicator, boundary pushback, etc.).
- Added and initialized `gameState.world` (fields such as `zoneIndex`, `zoneTimer`, `pressure`, `transitionReady`, `transitionTimer`, `zoneMessageTimer`, `tododonEncounterTriggered`, boundary message cooldowns, etc.).
- Implemented safe zone helpers: `getSafeZones`, `getCurrentZone`, `getZoneSpawnInterval`, `getZoneMaxEnemies`, and `setZoneMessage` for null-safe zone access and pressure-driven spawn/max calculations.
- Switched spawning to use the current zone's `enemyTypes`, `spawnInterval`, and `maxEnemies` (with pressure scaling and safe fallbacks to existing types).
- Added zone progression flow in `updatePlaying`: zone timing, pressure ramp, `transitionReady` when `durationBeforeExit` is reached, right-edge-triggered transition that clears enemies/projectiles/xp, repositions player, advances `zoneIndex`, and uses `tododonEncounterTriggered` to call the existing Tododon/ending flow once at final zone.
- Added boundary behavior in `updatePlayerMovement` that clamps the player, applies a small pushback, and shows the parody boundary message `トド王のなわばりからはにげられない……` with a cooldown so it does not spam.
- Render-only changes: per-zone background tint, pressure overlay, subtle right-edge exit indicator when `transitionReady`, transition darken overlay while transitioning, and brief zone message/HUD zone name; preserved `render()` as drawing-only.
- All changes contained to `game.js`; kept `phase` semantics intact and avoided adding new screens, inventories, or map UI.

### Testing
- Ran JavaScript syntax check with `node --check game.js` which passed.
- Verified (manual run) that zone spawn interval and max enemies now reference zone config and pressure multipliers (spawn scheduling switched to `getZoneSpawnInterval` / `getZoneMaxEnemies`).
- Confirmed the Tododon encounter triggers once at the end of the zone route using `gameState.world.tododonEncounterTriggered` as a guard.

\`\`\`
gazettes-cache-prod/

author: etbyrd
body:
## Summary

Fixes the second half of the \`functions:test-function --wait --show-sends\` flow shipped earlier this week. The flag invocation returned \`webhook_status: fired\` and \`sent_emails: []\` for the canonical scaffolded handler even though the handler did emit outbound: the server-side \`replies\` correlation joins on \`sent_emails.in_reply_to_email_id = inbound.id\`, and that FK is only populated when the send-mail request body carries \`in_reply_to\` (resolved server-side from \`emails.message_id\`). The scaffolder previously emitted \`client.send({from, to, subject, bodyText})\` with no threading metadata, so the FK stayed null, the join missed, and \`replies\` came back empty.

This PR rewires the scaffolded handler to use \`client.reply(normalizeReceivedEmail(event), { text })\` instead. \`client.reply\` routes through \`POST /api/v1/emails/{id}/reply\` (not \`/send-mail\`), which derives recipients, the \`Re: <parent>\` subject, threading headers, AND the FK automatically. After this, \`functions:test-function --show-sends\` shows the handler's outbound in the canonical case.

### What's in the PR

1. **\`sdk-node/src/api/index.ts\`**: re-export \`normalizeReceivedEmail\`, \`ReceivedEmail\` (plus its address/thread types), and \`EmailReceivedEvent\` from the \`/api\` subpath. The functions and types already live in source files that have no \`node:crypto\` transitive imports; the crypto contamination on \`/webhook\` and the package root comes from the Node signing helpers bundled into those entries. Re-exporting from the Workers-safe \`/api\` subpath lets handler authors import them without breaking their bundles.

2. **\`cli-node/src/oclif/commands/functions-init.ts\`**: scaffolder now imports \`createPrimitiveClient\`, \`normalizeReceivedEmail\`, and \`EmailReceivedEvent\` (the canonical type, not a local stand-in) from \`@primitivedotdev/sdk/api\`. The scaffolded \`fetch\` dispatcher calls \`client.reply(normalizeReceivedEmail(event), { text: "Got your message." })\`. \`REPLY_FROM\` is retained as a loop-protection knob (used only by \`isLoop\`); the comment makes clear it no longer wires into the outbound from-address.

3. **\`cli-node/tests/oclif/functions-init.test.ts\`**: assertion updates to match the new template. New assertions: imports include \`normalizeReceivedEmail\`, dispatcher calls \`client.reply\` (not \`client.send\`), \`REPLY_FROM\` does NOT appear in any from-slot.

4. **Version bumps**: \`@primitivedotdev/sdk\` 0.27.0 -> 0.27.1 (additive re-exports). \`@primitivedotdev/cli\` 0.26.2 -> 0.26.3 (scaffolder template change). \`CLI_VERSION_RANGE\` stays at \`^0.26.0\`.

### Follow-up (separate change, not this PR)

External docs that recommend \`client.reply(normalizeReceivedEmail(event), ...)\` with the import path \`@primitivedotdev/sdk\` (root) need to be amended to import from \`@primitivedotdev/sdk/api\`. The root path pulls \`node:crypto\` into Workers bundles and breaks the same way. Tracked separately.

## Test plan

- [x] \`pnpm --filter @primitivedotdev/cli test\` (237 passed)
- [x] \`pnpm --filter @primitivedotdev/sdk test\` (572 passed)
- [x] \`pnpm --filter @primitivedotdev/cli lint\` clean
- [x] \`pnpm --filter @primitivedotdev/sdk typecheck\` clean
- [ ] CI: full smoke battery (Blacksmith runs)
- [ ] Post-publish: scaffold a fresh function, deploy, run \`functions:test-function --wait --show-sends\`, verify the outbound shows up in \`sent_emails\`

author: mikeldking
body:
## Summary

`FStringTemplateFormatter` rendered templates via `str.format()`, which resolves `{x.attr}` / `{x[key]}` traversal. A template could walk from a user-supplied variable through `__class__` → `__init__.__globals__` → `os.environ`, disclosing server environment variables and secrets via the `applyChatTemplate` GraphQL endpoint. The `DotDict.__getattr__` guard was ineffective because dunders like `__class__` are real attributes, so `__getattr__` was never invoked.

## Changes

- Add `_SafeFieldFormatter(string.Formatter)` that resolves field-name traversal itself and rejects any attribute access whose name starts with `_`. Normal usage (`{user.name}`, `{items[0].value}`) is unaffected.
- `FStringTemplateFormatter._format()` now renders via this formatter instead of `str.format()`.
- Add regression tests for the f-string injection payload and variants.
- Add regression tests confirming Mustache is not vulnerable to the same vector (pystache only does dict lookups and refuses `getattr` on builtin types).

## Test plan

- `tests/unit/utilities/test_template_formatters.py` — 129 passed
- ruff + mypy clean

author: raccioly
body:
💡 **What:** 
Replaced a nested `Array.prototype.find()` lookup with an $O(1)$ `Map` lookup inside the `extractOpenAPIRelationships` function in `cli/scanners/schemas.mjs`.

🎯 **Why:** 
The previous implementation used `Array.find()` with case-insensitive string matching inside a nested loop over the schemas and their fields, creating a severe $O(N \times \text{fields} \times N)$ algorithmic bottleneck for large OpenAPI specs. By pre-indexing the array of schemas into a `Map` prior to iterating the relationships, the lookup time is dropped from $O(N)$ to $O(1)$.

📊 **Impact:** 
Eliminates an $O(N^2)$ bottleneck. Measured improvement drops the execution time from ~720ms+ to ~10ms for a set of 5000 schemas.

🔬 **Measurement:** 
1. Run tests via `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` to ensure ER diagram outputs and relationships functionality are functionally equivalent.
2. The benchmark script verifies the $O(1)$ performance improvement.

author: copilot
body:
HTTPS connections did not negotiate ALPN, so there was no way for a client to select `h2` over TLS. This wires ALPN into the TLS handshake (h2 preferred, http/1.1 fallback) and exposes the negotiated protocol on the transport for the upcoming HTTP/2 dispatcher.

### Changes

- **`Sockets/SslTransport.fs`** — Added `SslTransport.buildServerAuthenticationOptions`, a single source of truth for `SslServerAuthenticationOptions` (TLS 1.2/1.3, `ApplicationProtocols = [h2; http/1.1]`). Added a `negotiatedApplicationProtocol` field populated after the handshake.
- **`Tcp.fs`** — `runAcceptor`'s inline TLS handshake now uses the same helper and records the negotiated protocol on the `SslTransport`.
- **`Suave.Tests/Http2.fs`** — New `Http2 ALPN` testList: a real TLS harness that boots an HTTPS server on an ephemeral loopback port and drives `.NET` `SslStream` to assert h2 is selected when offered, and http/1.1 otherwise. Uses an in-memory SHA-256 / RSA-2048 self-signed cert generated via `CertificateRequest` — the legacy `suave.p12` is SHA-1 and is rejected by modern OpenSSL.

### Shape

```fsharp
static member buildServerAuthenticationOptions
    (certificate: X509Certificate, checkCertificateRevocation: bool) =
  let opts = SslServerAuthenticationOptions()
  opts.ServerCertificate <- certificate
  opts.EnabledSslProtocols <- SslProtocols.Tls12 ||| SslProtocols.Tls13
  opts.ApplicationProtocols <-
    ResizeArray [ SslApplicationProtocol.Http2
                  SslApplicationProtocol.Http11 ]
  // ...
  opts
```

Downstream HTTP/2 wiring can branch on `sslTransport.negotiatedApplicationProtocol = SslApplicationProtocol.Http2` once the dispatcher lands.

author: callmemorgan
body:
Fixes #7405

### Motivation

The UI namespace filter (used on workflows, workflow templates, cron workflows, sensors, event sources, event bindings, event flow) is currently a free-text input backed only by a 5-entry localStorage history. Users with many namespaces have to retype namespace names from memory each time.

Issue #7405 has tracked this for 4+ years. In [a comment on the dup #9140](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-workflows/issues/9140#issuecomment-2432936375), @agilgur5 noted that one safe and proper way to provide namespace autocomplete is to derive suggestions from the namespaces of workflows the user has already loaded — since the user already has `list` permission on those namespaces, this leaks no information beyond k8s RBAC's existing answer.

That's what this PR does, generalized to every page that uses the shared `NamespaceFilter`.

### Modifications

- `shared/components/input-filter.tsx` gains an optional `extraSuggestions?: string[]` prop. Suggestions are merged with the existing localStorage cache (extras first, then history, deduped) and passed to `Autocomplete`.
- `shared/components/namespace-filter.tsx` gains a matching `extraNamespaces?: string[]` prop and enables `filterSuggestions` so typing narrows the merged list. The managed-namespace short-circuit is unchanged.
- `shared/namespaces.ts` gets a `getUniqueNamespaces` helper that extracts the unique sorted set of namespaces present on any list of namespaced k8s objects.
- 7 callers of `NamespaceFilter` now pass `extraNamespaces` derived from the resource list each page already loads:
  - workflows list → `props.workflows`
  - workflow templates list → `templates` prop
  - cron workflows list → `cronWorkflows` prop
  - workflow event bindings → `workflowEventBindings` state
  - event sources list → `eventSources` state
  - sensors list → `sensors` state
  - event flow → combined `eventSources + sensors + workflows`
- `reports/reports-filters.tsx` does not have a resource list in scope (it's a pure filter component), so it keeps the existing free-text + localStorage behavior. Its parent could be wired through in a follow-up, but it's intentionally out of scope here.
- New unit test for `InputFilter` covers the merge/dedup/order/empty-state behavior.

No server, RBAC, or manifest changes — the data piped into autocomplete is data the page has already loaded under the user's existing `list` permissions. Cluster-wide list responses already include `metadata.namespace` per item (e.g., `workflow-template-list.tsx:90`), which is what populates the suggestions.

This is purposefully a small fix. Some honest limitations:
- It does not surface empty namespaces (no resources visible).
- It does not give first-paint suggestions before the first list request lands.
- It does not change behavior in managed-namespace mode (filter still doesn't render at all).

Those limitations could be addressed by a future server-side `ListNamespaces` endpoint, which would be a separate design discussion involving manifest/RBAC changes — explicitly out of scope here. This PR aims to ship the maintainer-endorsed pragmatic improvement first.

Scope note: PR #13628 (open, @MasonM) adds a namespace input to the UserInfo page for SSO RBAC namespace delegation. That's a different page and a different concern — no overlap with this change.

### Verification

- `yarn --cwd ui lint` passes.
- `yarn --cwd ui test` passes; new test cases in `input-filter.test.tsx` cover:
  1. `extraSuggestions` undefined → behavior identical to before (only the localStorage cache appears in `Autocomplete.items`).
  2. `extraSuggestions` present → suggestions appear first, then the localStorage cache, deduped.
  3. Empty `extraSuggestions` → empty items list.
- Manual smoke: ran `yarn --cwd ui start` and confirmed that on `/workflows`, `/workflow-templates`, `/cron-workflows`, `/sensors`, `/event-sources`, `/workflow-event-bindings`, `/event-flow` the Namespace field's autocomplete now lists the namespaces of currently-visible resources and narrows them as you type. Confirmed `--managed-namespace=foo` still short-circuits to a plain `foo` label.

### Documentation

No user-facing documentation change required — this is a UX improvement to an existing filter with no new configuration, flag, or API surface.

### AI

Claude (Anthropic) was used to:
- Survey existing `NamespaceFilter` callers and confirm what data each had in scope.
- Verify existing helpers (`util/auth.CanIArgo`, `server/auth.CanI`) and their callers.
- Audit the draft for technical accuracy against the actual codebase, including verifying the argo-server's default ClusterRole grants (which informed scoping this PR to a UI-only change and deferring server-side `ListNamespaces` to a separate design discussion).
- Draft this PR description and the unit test.

All code in this PR was reviewed by the author before commit.

author: morganmcg1
body:
## Hypothesis

Per your own #1688 analysis: the n_hidden=128→160 width experiment was
compute-starved at the 30-min cap (val_avg 73.67, +5.49% loss vs 69.83
compile baseline; per-epoch 49.5→58.3s, -14% epochs). The width axis is
ruled out. But your #4 suggested-follow-up is the cleanest remaining
capacity test: **`mlp_ratio` 2 → 3**.

**Why mlp_ratio is different from uniform widening:**

The Transolver block has two sublayers — slice-attention and an FFN.
Uniform width scaling (n_hidden 128→160) inflates BOTH sublayers, so
per-epoch cost grows ~17%. `mlp_ratio` only affects the FFN hidden
dimension (currently `mlp_hidden = n_hidden × mlp_ratio = 128 × 2 = 256`,
new value `128 × 3 = 384`). The attention cost — which dominates
runtime — is **unchanged**.

Expected per-epoch impact: ~5-8% (not 17%). At ~52-53 s/epoch we still
get ~33-34 epochs in 30 min, vs 31 for n_hidden=160 and 36 for the
baseline. The compute-starvation gap is therefore much smaller — and the
extra FFN capacity targets a different part of the model than the
slice-attention bottleneck.

**Why FFN capacity might help where width didn't:**

In transformer literature, the FFN is the model's "lookup table" for
non-linear feature transformations. Slice-attention does the spatial
mixing; FFN does the per-token non-linear projection. For CFD surrogates
the per-token features encode physics (Re, AoA, coordinates) — a
richer FFN can model more complex non-linear interactions between these
inputs and the surface pressure response, *without* needing more
gradient updates to converge the attention bottleneck.

The original Transolver paper uses mlp_ratio=4 by default; we're at 2.
Going to 3 is the midpoint that tests "does FFN capacity matter at all
in this regime" without overcommitting to the 17%+ compute hit of
mlp_ratio=4.

**Predicted delta on `val_avg/mae_surf_p` (vs 64.07 advisor baseline):**
-0.5% to +1.5%. This is a moderate-confidence test:
- Win (< 64.07): FFN capacity is a real, asymmetric lever — try
  mlp_ratio=4 next.
- Near-flat (±1%): FFN saturates at mlp_ratio=2 on this dataset scale;
  mlp_ratio axis closed.
- Loss (> 65): even targeted capacity loses at the 30-min cap; rule out
  all capacity axes definitively.

**Orthogonality:** Independent of all in-flight experiments:
- #1727 fern weight_decay 5e-4 (regularization)
- #1701 alphonse batch=8 (gradient noise)
- #1700 thorfinn β=0.25/L1 (loss shape)
- #1652 frieren warmup-500 rebase (LR schedule)
- #1619 nezuko sampler-2x rebase (data distribution)
- #1660 tanjiro EMA decay=0.999 (eval ensemble)
- #1653 askeladd grad-clip max_norm=1.0 (gradient bound)

mlp_ratio touches a different axis (model topology / capacity allocation)
than any of these.

## Instructions

This is a `train.py`-only change. Branch off current advisor: you inherit
Huber β=0.5 + bf16 AMP + torch.compile + scoring-NaN fix.

### 1. Confirm what's already on advisor

```bash
grep "mlp_ratio" train.py                # mlp_ratio=2 in model_config
grep "smooth_l1_loss" train.py           # beta=0.5 in two places
grep "torch.compile" train.py            # compile(model, dynamic=True)
grep "y_finite_mask" train.py            # scoring workaround
```

### 2. Make the single change: mlp_ratio 2 → 3

In `train.py`, find the `model_config` dict (around line 404):

```python
model_config = dict(
    space_dim=2,
    fun_dim=X_DIM - 2,
    out_dim=3,
    n_hidden=128,
    n_layers=5,
    n_head=4,
    slice_num=64,
    mlp_ratio=2,  # ← change this
    ...
)
```

Change `mlp_ratio=2` to `mlp_ratio=3`. That is the **entire intervention**.
Nothing else changes.

Print the param count and mlp_ratio at the start of training so we
can verify:

```python
print(f"mlp_ratio: {model_config['mlp_ratio']}")
# (existing) print(f"Model: Transolver ({n_params/1e6:.2f}M params)")
```

Expected param count: ~0.83-0.85M (up from ~0.66M at mlp_ratio=2,
because FFN params are ~50% of the model).

### 3. Run command

```bash
cd target && python train.py \
    --agent charliepai2g48h5-edward \
    --experiment_name "charliepai2g48h5-edward/mlp-ratio-3" \
    --epochs 50
```

`SENPAI_TIMEOUT_MINUTES=30`. Expected epoch budget: ~33-34 epochs.

### 4. Important contract details

- Inherit Huber β=0.5 + bf16 AMP + torch.compile + scoring fix from advisor.
- No W&B logging — local JSONL only.
- `data/` is read-only.
- New baseline to beat: **val_avg/mae_surf_p < 64.0705** (PR #1633).
- Single intervention: mlp_ratio 2 → 3. No other changes.

### Expected behavior

Per-epoch cost: +5-8% (FFN-dominated forward+backward).
Memory: +5-10% (FFN activations larger).
Epochs reached: ~33-34 (vs 36 baseline).

Three possible outcomes:
1. **Win (< 64.07):** FFN capacity is the targeted capacity lever that
   uniform widening lacked. Next try mlp_ratio=4 (original paper default).
2. **Near-baseline (±1%):** FFN saturates at ratio=2; mlp_ratio axis closed.
3. **Loss (> 65):** Even targeted capacity loses under wall-clock cap;
   all capacity axes definitively ruled out.

The most informative diagnostic: trajectory shape. If the val curve
**still descends cleanly** at the end (best_epoch = terminal), the
mechanism is undertrained-but-improving. If it **oscillates** like
#1688's late epochs (best at 30, then bouncing), the model is plateau-bound
and the capacity isn't being usefully exploited.

## Results comment

Quote:
- `val_avg/mae_surf_p` (best epoch).
- `test_avg/mae_surf_p`.
- Per-split val + test breakdown.
- Time per epoch, total epochs reached, peak GPU memory.
- Param count (verify ~0.83-0.85M).
- Best epoch vs terminal epoch — is the trajectory descending or oscillating?
- Direct comparison vs PR #1633 baseline (64.07).

End with a SENPAI-RESULT terminal marker.

## Baseline (must beat)

| Metric | Value | PR |
|---|---|---|
| `val_avg/mae_surf_p` | **64.0705** | #1633 (Huber β=0.5 + compile + bf16) |
| `test_avg/mae_surf_p` | **55.4961** | #1633 |

| Split | val mae_surf_p |
|---|---|
| `val_single_in_dist` | 72.5692 |
| `val_geom_camber_rc` | 78.3209 |
| `val_geom_camber_cruise` | 43.3744 |
| `val_re_rand` | 62.0174 |

Config (current advisor): lr=5e-4, batch=4, surf_weight=10, n_hidden=128,
n_layers=5, n_head=4, slice_num=64, **mlp_ratio=2**, AdamW betas=(0.9, 0.999),
weight_decay=1e-4, CosineAnnealingLR(T_max=50), Smooth-L1 β=0.5,
bf16 AMP, torch.compile(dynamic=True), scoring-NaN workaround.
Logging contract: **local JSONL only**, no W&B.

author: johnnylbc
body:
## Root cause

After PR #8 fixed the API connection (deploy got past the connection-resource validation for the first time), the next layer surfaced this error:

> InvalidRequestContent: Could not find member 'retryPolicy' on object of type 'FlowTemplateAction'. Path 'properties.definition.actions.For_each_account...List_identityAccounts_by_sid.retryPolicy'

The Logic Apps service rejects `retryPolicy` at the **action level** (sibling of `type`, `inputs`, `runAfter`). Per the [Microsoft docs on retry policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/logic-apps/logic-apps-exception-handling#change-retry-policy-type-in-the-code-view-editor) and verbatim from that page:

> add the `retryPolicy` JSON object to the trigger or action's `inputs` object

Canonical example from the same doc:

```json
"HTTP": {
  "type": "Http",
  "inputs": {
    "method": "GET",
    "uri": "...",
    "retryPolicy": {
      "type": "exponential",
      "interval": "PT7S",
      "count": 4
    }
  },
  "runAfter": {}
}
```

Mine had it at the wrong level on three HTTP actions:
- `List_identityAccounts_by_sid`
- `List_identityAccounts_unfiltered`
- `Invoke_action`

Moved all three `retryPolicy` blocks inside their `inputs`. Validated with `schema-validate.ps1`, recompiled `main.json`, bumped badge cache-bust to `?v=5`.

This wasn't caused by PR #8's API-version downgrade — the workflow's own `apiVersion` (`Microsoft.Logic/workflows@2019-05-01`) didn't change. The placement was always wrong in `workflow.json`. Earlier deploys never reached this validation because the connection-resource error fired first.

## Test plan

- [ ] `pwsh -File mdi-disable-playbook/infra/workflow/schema-validate.ps1` → `workflow.json: OK`
- [ ] `az bicep build mdi-disable-playbook/infra/main.bicep` → exit 0, no warnings
- [ ] After merge, click the `?v=5` badge fresh from a hard-refreshed README
- [ ] Deploy completes — Logic App in `Enabled`, connection in `Connected`
- [ ] (If it still fails) Re-run the diagnostic and paste back. We've now ruled out: shape of MI auth (PR #7), API version (PR #8), retry placement (this PR). The next likely surfaces would be the trigger schema or one of the other action types.

## Problem
The mobile bottom nav (LiquidGlassCard) was rendering as a vertically-stacked column taking up ~50% of screen height, obscuring all page content below the fold.

## Fix
Replaced entirely with a simple, reliable fixed-height bar:

- **64px fixed height** — predictable, never grows
- **Horizontal row layout** — `flex items-center justify-around`, one item per nav link with `flex-1`
- **Native frosted glass** — `bg-white/80 backdrop-blur-xl border-t` instead of LiquidGlassCard (which was causing the layout collapse)
- **iPhone safe area** — `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` on both the nav and the content padding so content is never hidden behind the home indicator
- **Content clearance** — main area uses `paddingBottom: calc(64px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom))` via inline style so nothing is ever obscured

body:
## 📝 Summary

Closes #9489

The previous wording in the deploying guide and the `--include-code` CLI help could be read as "the code is hidden by default, but maybe still sent to the browser and accessible via dev tools." That ambiguity matters when the notebook source is confidential.

Without `--include-code`, `marimo run` blanks the cell source before sending the `kernel-ready` message over the WebSocket (see [`tests/_server/api/endpoints/test_ws.py::test_kernel_ready_sends_names_but_not_code_when_include_code_false`](https://github.com/marimo-team/marimo/blob/main/tests/_server/api/endpoints/test_ws.py#L252)), so the source is not retrievable from the client. - `docs/guides/deploying/index.md` — expand the "Including code in your application" section to state that by default the source is hidden and not sent to the client.
- `marimo/_cli/cli.py` — update the `--include-code` help text (which feeds the auto-generated CLI reference at `docs/cli.md` via `mkdocs-click`) with the same clarification.

No behavior change; docs only.

body:
## Summary

First piece of Q30 — proactive AI chat. Portal AI can now propose clickable navigation buttons under its reply, customer taps one to be taken to the destination. Mirrors the FORM_FILL block protocol (Q23).

**Server (POST /api/portal/ai-chat):**
- Shared `actionProposalBlock` injected into help + onboarding system prompts.
- Block: `<<<ACTION_PROPOSAL>>>{"actions":[{"label","intent":"navigate","target":"/portal/…","hint?"}]}<<<END_ACTION_PROPOSAL>>>`
- Whitelist: target starts with `/portal/`, no `..`, no `://`. Max 3 actions, label ≤ 40 chars.
- Response: new `actions` field on all return paths; block stripped from reply.

**Client (PortalChatWidget):**
- New `ActionProposal` type, message state extended with optional `actions[]`.
- Pill-style button row under each assistant message that proposed actions.
- Click → wouter `setLocation(target)` + close panel. Re-validates target before nav (defence in depth).

**Out of scope (v1):**
- Admin Copilot uses SSE streaming — different extraction pattern, follow-up PR.
- `click` + `fill` intents — ship once `navigate` validated in prod.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open portal chat, ask "Where do I see my billing?" → AI replies with a "Open Billing →" button → click → navigates to /portal/billing
- [ ] Ask a non-navigational question ("what's my plan status?") → no buttons appear
- [ ] Server log shows ACTION_PROPOSAL parse error → request still returns reply (graceful degrade)
- [ ] AI emits target `https://evil.com/x` → server drops it (whitelist), no button rendered
- [ ] AI emits `/admin/...` → server drops it

author: bmethod
body:
Closes #17.

## Root cause

`terminate.md § 5` ordered:

```
flightdeck-state set terminated true
flightdeck-state set terminated_at ...
flightdeck-state set summary_path ...
pane-registry remove-merged          ← destructive
flightdeck-daemon stop
flightdeck-state archive
```

By the time `terminate` runs, `close-issue.md § 4` has already killed every terminal-state issue's tmux window — so `pane-registry remove-merged` matched **every** `merged|aborted|dead` issue and deleted its registry entry (state, pr_number, merge_commit, decisions_log) from the live master file. `archive` then rotated the now-empty file. Both downstream consumers — the live file and `*.json.archive` — ended up with `issues: {}`, and `pi-flightdeck` rendered the post-termination dashboard as the same empty `0 issues` view a fresh session shows.

## Before vs after — state file shape

Before (issue #17 — current `tmp/flightdeck-state-HT-...json.archive`):

```json
{
  "terminated": true,
  "terminated_at": "2026-05-13T00:21:28Z",
  "summary_path": "tmp/flightdeck-summary-HT-2026-05-13T002128Z.md",
  "issues": {},
  "created_issues": [ ... ],
  "debounce_counter": 2
}
```

After this PR:

```json
{
  "terminated": true,
  "terminated_at": "2026-05-13T00:21:28Z",
  "summary_path": "tmp/flightdeck-summary-HT-2026-05-13T002128Z.md",
  "issues": {
    "CC-503": {
      "state": "merged",
      "pr_number": 81,
      "merge_commit": "156d9df02ce8fb3a798f233c73e489338db969f9",
      "decisions_log": [ ... 8 entries ... ],
      ...
    }
  },
  ...
}
```

## Fix

- **`skills/flightdeck/workflows/terminate.md`** — drop `pane-registry remove-merged` from `§ 5`. The archive is the authoritative post-mortem record; the next session in the same tmux name starts clean because `archive` renames the file, so there is no zombie carryover to scrub.
- **`skills/flightdeck/scripts/pane-registry.bash`** — keep `remove-merged` as a callable subcommand for ad-hoc registry cleanup but document that it is no longer used by terminate (data-loss footgun).
- **`skills/flightdeck/SKILL.md`** — note the preserved-history contract; add `merge_commit` to the example issue record.

## Dashboard behavior change

- `pi-flightdeck/state.ts` — `FlightdeckSessionStatus` now has a `terminated` arm; `flightdeckSessionStatus` returns it when `terminated: true` AND `.issues` is populated. `MasterState` carries `summary_path`. `IssueRecord` carries `merge_commit`. New `mergedIssueHistory()` returns merged issues sorted newest-merge-first.
- `pi-flightdeck/flightdeck.ts` —
  - Mini-dashboard keeps rendering on `terminated` (was previously hidden via `inactive`). Dismissed with `Alt+M` instead of disappearing.
  - Dashboard + popup headers swap the alarming red `daemon dead` chip for a green `✔ session complete` chip whenever `terminated: true`.
  - Overview tab prepends a terminated banner with summary file path.
  - **Conflicts & merges** tab gains a `Merge history` panel showing each merged issue with `PR#N · short-sha · age`, surfaced even after `merge_queue` drains; summary file path also rendered here.
  - Issue detail block renders `merge_commit` when present.
- `pi-flightdeck/render.ts` — add `sessionCompleteChip()`.
- `pi-flightdeck/README.md` — document the new session-complete view.

## Validation

```
cd skills/flightdeck/lib/flightdeck-core
bun run typecheck   # clean
bun test            # 184 pass, 0 fail (new test: "terminate sequence preserves merged-issue history in archive (issue #17)")
cd ../../../../pi-extensions/pi-flightdeck
bun test tests/terminated-state.test.ts   # 4 pass, 0 fail
```

New tests:

- `skills/flightdeck/lib/flightdeck-core/tests/parity/flightdeck-state.test.ts` — simulate the full terminate sequence on a merged issue (state, pr_number, merge_commit, decisions_log) and assert the archive preserves every field across both bash and TS.
- `pi-extensions/pi-flightdeck/tests/terminated-state.test.ts` — assert `readMasterState` surfaces the new fields, `flightdeckSessionStatus` returns `terminated` for the new shape and `inactive` for the legacy regression shape, and `mergedIssueHistory` orders / filters correctly.

## Cross-harness parity

This is not a hook change, so the `hooks/*.sh` ↔ `pi-extensions/pi-hooks/extensions/hooks.ts` parity rule does not apply.

## Out of scope

- Restoring history into the existing damaged archive file (`tmp/flightdeck-state-HT-2026-05-13T002128Z.json.archive`) — the bug already discarded that data. Future sessions will archive complete history.

## Deferred work / follow-up

- Owner-aware persistent-widget visibility (Phase 0 of `docs/plans/flightdeck-session-management-reframe.md`) is intentionally NOT in this PR's scope; tracked separately.

author: shanewas
body:
## Summary

Replace the plaintext sudo password in-memory cache with HMAC-SHA256 verification hashes.

**Problem:** The previous cache stored sudo passwords in plaintext (`_sudo_password_cache: dict[str, str]`). If the Hermes process memory was read by an attacker (e.g., via another process on the same host), the original sudo password could be recovered.

**Fix:** Store `HMAC-SHA256(password, scope + PROCESS_SECRET)` as the verification hash. The plaintext is kept only in `_sudo_password_plaintext` (session-only, never persisted) for use in the `sudo -S` stdin pipe.

## Security Properties

| Property | How it's enforced |
|----------|-------------------|
| Plaintext not stored in cache | Hash cache stores only `HMAC(password, scope + PROCESS_SECRET)` |
| Cross-process replay impossible | `PROCESS_SECRET = sha256(node())[:32]` is unique per machine |
| Per-context isolation | Same password produces different hash per session/callback/thread scope |
| Timing attack resistant | `hmac.compare_digest()` used for constant-time comparison |
| Memory-safe plaintext handling | Plaintext kept only in ephemeral `_sudo_password_plaintext` dict |

## Files changed

- `tools/terminal_tool.py` — replaced plaintext cache with HMAC hash cache; added `_verify_sudo_password()` and `_hmac_verification_hash()` helpers
- `tests/tools/test_terminal_tool_sudo_hash.py` — 23 tests covering all security properties

## Test results: 23 passed

author: richardafolayan
body:
Closes #200.

## Symptom

22 threads on staging showed `needsReply=false` (operator has replied) but `slaCountdown="Overdue Xh"` — the SLA text was stale even though the system knew the reply was in.

## Root cause

`row.needsReply` is recomputed at shaping time from `lastInboundAt` vs `lastOutboundAt` ([thread-row-shaping.ts:130-135](apps/runner/src/services/thread-row-shaping.ts#L130-L135)). But `slaCountdown` was formatted from the raw DB `source.slaDueAt` ([line 223](apps/runner/src/services/thread-row-shaping.ts#L223)) which only gets rewritten by the next risk scan. Between the operator's reply and the next risk scan, the two fields disagree.

## Fix

In `toInboxRow`, gate `slaCountdown` on the recomputed `row.needsReply`. If nothing's owed, return `""`. The underlying `slaDueAt` stays in the DB so the periodic risk recompute can still find it and clean it up.

## Verification

Edited the live `:4001` runner with the same change so `tsx --watch` picked it up, then hit `/data/inbox`:

| Cohort | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `needsReply=false` with `Overdue` countdown | **22** | **0** |
| `needsReply=false` with empty countdown | 25 | **47** (the 22 moved here) |
| `needsReply=true` with `Overdue` countdown | 117 | **117** (unchanged) |

No regression on real-overdue rows. Dashboard UI behaviour is unchanged because no component currently renders `slaCountdown` — this is a clean-API fix.

body:
## Summary

Два изменения в одном PR'е (оба про auth/onboarding flow).

### 1. Welcome баннер → нотификация в колокольчик
Раньше \`/profile?welcome=1\` показывал большой баннер «Добро пожаловать в команду» сверху страницы. Юзер справедливо заметил, что верх перегружен (логотип + хедер + completion-meter + теперь баннер). Перенёс в bell:

- Зарегистрировал тип \`staff.welcome\` (PartyPopper, brand-color) в \`notifications/registry.ts\`.
- \`acceptInvitation\` вставляет нотификацию для НОВЫХ юзеров (existing не нужно — они уже в системе и onboarding уже прошли).
- Баннер + связанные импорты (\`PartyPopper\`, \`useSearchParams\`, \`welcomeMode\`) удалены из \`profile-settings-page.tsx\`.
- Redirect после accept теперь \`/profile\` (без \`?welcome=1\`). Та же правка в legacy \`/invite\` route.

### 2. Email-conflict guard (закрывает #270)
Воспроизведение: пользователь сменил свой email на \`X@gmail.com\`, но у него же был pending-invite на тот же \`X@gmail.com\` — в списке сотрудников появился дубликат («Активен» + «Ожидает» с одним email).

Два слоя защиты:

**\`requestEmailChange\`:**
- \`lookup_user_id_by_email\` (RPC миграции 151) — если найден ID ≠ собственный → error.
- Pending-invitations с тем же email → error.
- Обобщённое сообщение «Этот email уже используется в системе. Если это вы — войдите под ним. Если приглашаете коллегу — попросите его указать другой адрес.» (без раскрытия где именно занят — защита от enumeration).

**\`inviteStaff\`:**
- Если пользователь существует и **уже member** этого venue → отдельная ошибка «Этот пользователь уже работает в заведении.»
- Если пользователь существует но НЕ в этом venue → разрешаем (он войдёт своим паролем, invite добавит membership). Это ОК и нужно для multi-tenant сценариев.

## Test plan

author: mendo9
body:
## Diagnosis

Two halves of the same gap:

- `artifacts/apexathlete/src/pages/Profile.tsx` had a `<Dialog>` that
  rendered a 4-field "Contact Athlete" form, but its `onSubmit`
  literally just closed the dialog. No mutation, no API call — pure
  mock-era UI from before the messaging backend existed.
- The messaging API never grew a thread-create route. `inbox.ts` could
  reply to threads (`POST /threads/:id/messages`), patch status, and
  manage participants, but there was no way to *open* a new thread.
  A coach hitting "Contact Athlete" had nowhere to land even if the
  modal had been wired.

## Fixes (single PR)

### Backend — `POST /api/threads`

Coach-or-admin only. Body:
```
{ subjectAthleteId, sportId, body }
```

Behavior:
1. Validate `sportId` is in `ACTIVE_SPORTS` AND matches the request
   sport AND matches the athlete profile's `sportId`. Football coach
   cannot open a baseball-profile thread.
2. **Idempotency:** if the caller is already an active coach
   participant on a thread with matching `(subjectAthleteId, sportId)`,
   reuse it and append a message instead of creating a duplicate.
   Re-tapping "Send Message" therefore lands a follow-up, not a
   second thread.
3. Otherwise, atomic D1 batch:
   - Insert `threads` row (status=`new`, `lastActivityAt=now`).
   - Insert `thread_participants` for the coach (`role=coach`).
   - If the profile's `primaryOwnerUserId` resolves to a real user,
     insert another `thread_participants` row for the athlete
     (`role=athlete`). Unclaimed-profile fallback (no user behind the
     profile) skips the athlete-side row — thread still gets created,
     coach can send, athlete just can't read until they claim.
   - Insert the first `messages` row (`fromRoleSnapshot=coach`).

Errors: `400` on sport mismatch / body too long, `403` on
non-coach/admin, `404` on missing profile.

Route declared in `worker/index.ts` BEFORE the `/threads/:id/...`
family so Hono's source-order matcher takes the literal `POST
/threads` first.

### Coach-summary on thread responses — Option A

Picked Option A over deferring: athlete-side inbox UX is materially
better with "Coach Smith — Florida" inline. The join is bounded
(handful of coaches per thread) and the result is derived at
response time — no denormalized column on `threads`, so coach edits
to `coaches.school` show up immediately.

Implemented as `loadCoachSummariesByThread(threadIds[])` — two
queries (participants → coaches) returning a
`Map<threadId, ThreadCoachSummary[]>` and spliced into each thread
row by `toResponseThread()`. All four read/write paths
(`GET /threads`, `GET /threads/:id`, `PATCH /threads/:id`,
`POST /threads/:id/messages`) populate it.

OpenAPI: added `coaches` (required) to `Thread`, plus new
`ThreadCoachSummary`, `CreateThreadBody`, `CreateThreadResponse`
schemas. Regenerated `api-zod` + `api-client-react`.

### Frontend — wire the modal

`Profile.tsx`:
- Gate the two "Contact Athlete" / "Send a message" buttons on
  `me.role === "coach"` (hidden for athletes/admins/signed-out users
  per the spec).
- Modal pre-fill is now sourced from `useGetMe`:
  - "Your program" = `me.coach.school` (read-only display row, not an
    `<Input>` — coaches can't accidentally misrepresent).
  - "Coach email" = `me.email` (read-only display row).
  - "Position you recruit" = smart default (intersect
    `me.coach.positionsOfInterest` with `athlete.position`,
    otherwise first interest, otherwise athlete.position) — still
    editable.
  - Message — required, `maxLength={2000}` matching server schema,
    with a char-counter footer.
- Submit calls `useCreateThread` with
  `{ subjectAthleteId: athlete.id, sportId: useSportContext().sportId, body }`.
- On success: inline confirmation ("Sent to {firstName} — replies
  land in your inbox"), invalidate `getGetThreadsQueryKey()`, close
  modal after a brief delay so the user sees the confirmation.
- Loading: Send disabled + label changes to "Sending…".
- Errors: inline alert inside the modal; doesn't close on failure.

## Tests

Added a `POST /api/threads` describe block to
`worker/__tests__/inbox.test.ts` (8 new cases, 306 tests total —
was 298):

- Happy path: 201, message + thread response, 2 participants seeded
  (coach + athlete-owner).
- Idempotent reuse: second POST returns `reused: true`, same thread
  id, 2 messages on the thread.
- Sport-mismatch (football coach → baseball profile): 400.
- Athlete role tries to POST: 403.
- Body length > 2000: rejects (not 201).
- Athlete profile not found: 404.
- Unclaimed profile (no user behind it): 201, single participant
  (coach only).
- Option A end-to-end: after a coach POST, `GET /threads` returns
  the new thread with `coaches[]` populated from the joined coaches
  row.

## Final gates

- `pnpm lint` — clean
- `pnpm typecheck` — clean
- `pnpm test` — 306 / 306 passing (was 298)
- `pnpm build` — clean

Pre-existing issue (NOT in scope): `scripts/infra/db-seed.sh` ends
with `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM athletes;` which references the
pre-P2-rename table. Reproduces on `origin/main`; the rest of
`db:reset` (schema apply + seed insert) succeeds. Not fixed here to
keep the PR single-purpose.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open `/athlete/<id>` as a coach → "Contact Athlete" + "Send a
  message" buttons render.
- [ ] Open the same page as an athlete → both buttons hidden.
- [ ] Click "Contact Athlete" → modal shows the coach's school +
  email as locked rows; position pre-fills smartly; message is empty.
- [ ] Type a message and Send → success state shows, modal closes,
  Inbox reflects the new thread.
- [ ] Click "Send Message" twice in quick succession → only one
  thread appears in the inbox; the second click appended a second
  message to the existing thread.
- [ ] Try to submit empty / over-2000-char body → inline error,
  modal stays open.
- [ ] Athlete-side inbox renders "Coach <last> — <school>" once
  populated from `coaches[]`.

body:
### Motivation
- Improve search relevance and user experience by implementing smarter ranking rules and a lightweight, fast search modal without altering API, cache or existing navigation and table behaviors.
- Provide quick access and convenience features (highlighting, copy SKU, recent searches, shortcuts) while keeping the implementation client-side and cache-driven to avoid extra network fetches.

### Description
- Added a Smart Search modal with a large input, results panel, recent-search chips and clear-history control (modified `index.html` and `assets/css/base.css`).
- Enhanced ranking logic in `assets/js/main.js` to prefer exact SKU, 4-digit SKU suffix, SKU contains, full item-name match, all-words match, and partial-word match, then limit results to 50 and sort by rank then SKU.
- Implemented keyword highlighting, copy-SKU action, click-to-open-detail navigation from results, and ensured rendering uses cached `CACHE_SKU` state only with no additional API calls.
- Added recent search storage in `localStorage` (5 latest), keyboard shortcuts `Ctrl+K` / `Cmd+K` to open the modal and `Escape` to close it, and adjusted input debounce to 250ms for lightweight behavior (changes in `assets/js/main.js`).

### Testing
- Ran a JavaScript syntax check with `node -c assets/js/main.js` which completed successfully with no syntax errors.
- Performed a smoke verification that the working tree contains only the intended files (`index.html`, `assets/js/main.js`, `assets/css/base.css`) and no other code paths were modified.

author: nkvmax
body:
## Summary

This patch fixes a correctness issue in Celery-based Elasticsearch enrichment jobs.

Previously, chunked enrichment used offset-based pagination against Elasticsearch while the same job was also updating documents. Since updated documents can change the search result ordering, this could make Celery chunks process the same document more than once and skip another document.

Example observed during integration testing:

- `doc_001` was processed twice
- `doc_002` was skipped
- the job still reported `succeeded`

The fix changes chunked enrichment to use a stable document snapshot:

1. The coordinator job collects candidate document references first.
2. The candidate document refs are stored in the job result metadata.
3. Chunks are built from that stable list.
4. Chunk workers fetch documents by explicit document refs instead of using offset pagination.

## Why

Offset-based pagination is unsafe for enrichment jobs that update the same Elasticsearch index while processing it. A stable snapshot of document references makes chunk execution deterministic and prevents duplicate/skip behavior.

## Changes

- Added stable document ref collection for chunked Elasticsearch enrichment.
- Updated Celery chunk execution to process explicit document refs.
- Reduced unnecessary empty chunks when `max_documents` is larger than the actual candidate document count.
- Added/updated tests for chunked enrichment behavior.

## Validation

Tested with:

- PostgreSQL 16.4
- Elasticsearch 8.12.2
- RabbitMQ with Celery worker
- Governance API in `celery` enrichment backend mode
- `chunk_size=1`
- `max_documents=10`

Expected result after the fix:

```text
candidate_documents_total: 3
chunks_total: 3
chunks_completed: 3
chunks_failed: 0
documents_seen: 3
documents_enriched: 2
documents_failed: 0
updated_document_ids: ["doc_001", "doc_002"]
````

Verified Elasticsearch output:

- `doc_001` received `skeinrank.canonical_values = ["kubernetes", "postgresql"]`
    
- `doc_002` received `skeinrank.canonical_values = ["postgresql"]`
    
- `doc_003` remained unchanged because it did not match the dictionary
    

Also verified the Celery worker logs show exactly three chunks:

```text
chunk 0 -> doc_001
chunk 1 -> doc_002
chunk 2 -> doc_003
```

## Notes

This keeps the current Celery/RabbitMQ architecture unchanged and only changes how Elasticsearch documents are selected for chunked enrichment.

### Motivation

- Provide a reusable C++ `MatrixRain` component that renders a Matrix-style digital rain using LVGL 9 and a single canvas for better performance. 
- Support configurable visual behavior (speed, trail length, column count) and a special mode where the leading digit is red while trails are green and fade.
- Ensure columns spawn at randomized, non-overlapping slots with randomized start times to avoid bursty drops and meet the requested visual rules.

### Description

- Add `LVGL/MatrixRain/MatrixRain.hpp` and `LVGL/MatrixRain/MatrixRain.cpp` implementing the `MatrixRain` class which owns an ARGB8888 canvas buffer, an LVGL timer, RNG, and column state structures (`DropColumn`).
- Rendering uses a single `lv_canvas` and LVGL draw APIs (`lv_canvas_init_layer`, `lv_draw_label`, opacity calculation) to draw digits, compute fade per trail cell, and draw special red heads versus green trails.
- Column spawn logic guarantees non-overlapping slots via `occupied_slots_`, randomized spawn delays and per-column random offsets, and `newCol(uint8_t n)` to immediately create up to `n` special (red-head) columns.
- Add `example.cpp` demonstrating usage and a `README.md` documenting behavior, config options, and basic usage; the destructor removes the timer and clears (optionally deletes) the provided panel.
