author: wallscaler
body:
## Summary

Two production bugs blocking the first real scored card on Cathedral — both surfaced end-to-end tonight from an RTX 4090 miner box.

### Bug 1 — tilde expansion in install verify

`SshHermesRunner._verify_hermes_install` was building `test -d $(shlex.quote("~/.hermes"))` which renders as `test -d '~/.hermes'`. Bash does **not** expand `~` inside single quotes, so the test always failed and every miner with the default `hermes_home=~/.hermes` hit `hermes_install_invalid` with empty stderr on the first visit.

Worse, the same `~/.hermes` prefix flowed through `_profile_path` into:
- the sqlite3 backup one-liner (`sqlite3.connect('file:~/.hermes/profiles/.../state.db?mode=ro')` — Python's sqlite3 doesn't expand `~` either)
- SFTP `get` / `listdir` calls (SFTP performs no shell expansion at all)
- `test -f` / `tar -czf -C` shell commands wrapped in `shlex.quote`

**Fix:** resolve `hermes_home` to an absolute path **once** at session start by querying remote `$HOME` via `printf "%s" "$HOME"`. Thread the resolved path through every downstream consumer. Absolute paths still go through `shlex.quote` for shell-injection safety (covered by new no-regression test).

### Bug 2 — multi-turn agentic loop produces prose, not Card JSON

`hermes -z` without a turn cap runs the full agentic loop. DeepSeek-V3.1 (and similar models) then drift into conversational research replies ("I don't have any recent local information about...") instead of single-turn Card JSON. Tonight 4/5 evals failed this way.

**Fix:** new `eval_max_turns: int | None = 1` config field. When set, `hermes -z` is invoked with `--max-turns N`. Orchestrator reads it from `CATHEDRAL_HERMES_MAX_TURNS` env (default `1`; set to `0` or empty to omit the flag).

Profile content also being tightened upstream in `cathedral-baseline-agent/soul.md` to force JSON-only output.

## Test plan

- [x] New: `test_verify_command_resolves_tilde_to_absolute_path` — asserts rendered command does NOT contain `'~/.hermes'` and DOES contain the absolute resolved path
- [x] New: `test_absolute_hermes_home_still_shlex_quoted` — no shell-injection regression on absolute paths with unusual chars (space)
- [x] New: `test_hermes_z_passes_max_turns_1_by_default` — invocation contains `--max-turns 1`
- [x] New: `test_hermes_z_max_turns_can_be_disabled_via_config` — `eval_max_turns=None` omits the flag
- [x] All 20 existing `test_ssh_hermes_runner.py` tests updated to stub the new `$HOME` resolve step — still pass
- [x] Full suite: `321 passed, 8 skipped` (skips pre-existing)
- [x] `ruff check` clean, `ruff format` clean, `mypy --strict` clean on changed files

## Operational notes

- Default behavior changes: `hermes -z` now runs with `--max-turns 1`. Operators who want the old multi-turn behavior set `CATHEDRAL_HERMES_MAX_TURNS=0`.
- No on-chain or signing changes. Bundle shape unchanged.
- Cuts v1.1.3 after merge — unblocks first real scored cards.

author: realunstoppable
body:
🚨 **Severity:** HIGH
💡 **Vulnerability:** The `escapeHTML` function in `admin.html` silently returned non-string inputs (like Arrays) unmodified (`if (typeof str !== 'string') return str;`).
🎯 **Impact:** This allowed XSS payloads to bypass the sanitization filter. By passing a payload as an array (e.g., `["<script>alert(1)</script>"]`), it would not be sanitized. When inserted into the DOM via template literals, JavaScript implicitly coerces the array into a string, injecting the unescaped payload directly into `innerHTML`, resulting in a DOM-based XSS attack.
🔧 **Fix:** Updated `escapeHTML` in `admin.html` to explicitly coerce non-string inputs into strings (using `str.toString()`) before processing them through the `.replace()` sanitization chain.
✅ **Verification:** Verified syntax correctness using `pnpm test` and `node --check`. No new regressions introduced. Documented the pattern in `.jules/sentinel.md`.

author: sebkister
body:
Adds support for the **JedEye** cave-survey instrument (https://sebkister.github.io/JedEye-Documentation) as a recognised BLE device in TopoDroid.

JedEye is an Arduino-based handheld instrument (Nano RP2040 Connect / NINA-W102 radio) that measures azimuth, clino, roll and distance. Its firmware uses the same 17-byte shot frame as the SAP6 (sequence byte + four little-endian `float32`: bearing, clino, roll, distance in metres), but advertises its own 128-bit GATT service UUIDs so it has a distinct identity in BLE scanners.

## Layout

The new device follows the existing **discox** pattern (subclass SAP rather than duplicate it):

- `dev/jedeye/JedeyeConst.java` — service + read/write UUIDs (`4A454445-5945-000{1,2,3}-…`)
- `dev/jedeye/JedeyeComm.java` extends `SapComm` — constructor bootstraps as SAP6 then swaps the three UUIDs; overrides `assertDevice()` to recognise JedEye; overrides `createProtocol()` to create a `JedeyeProtocol`
- `dev/jedeye/JedeyeProtocol.java` extends `SapProtocol` — empty body; the SAP6 frame parsing already does the right thing

For `JedeyeComm` to recognise its own device type, `SapComm.assertDevice()` is widened from `private` to `protected`. `SapProtocol.handleRead()` accepts JedEye on the SAP6 frame branch (`Device.isSap6(...) || Device.isJedeye(...)`). JedEye is not asked to send back an ACK — its firmware does not run the SAP6 ACK handshake — so `SapComm.changedChrt()` keeps the existing SAP6-UUID check around the `writeChrt` of the ACK.

Cross-cutting edits mirror the Cavway X1 / discox additions:

- `dev/Device.java` — `NAME_JEDEYE = "JedEye_"`, `DISTO_JEDEYE = 12`, `isJedeye()` (instance + `int` + `String`), entries in `mModels` / `mModelNames` / `mAdvertisedNames` / `mBleModels` / `typeString` / `typeSimpleString` / `isKnownDevice` / `isBLE`(both) / `btnameToModel` / `btnameToName` / `btnameToType` / `fromName`
- `TDX/TDInstance.java` — `isDeviceJedeye()`; JedEye added to both flavours of `isDeviceBLE`
- `TDX/TopoDroidApp.java` — `new JedeyeComm(...)` branch in both `createComm()` dispatch sites
- `TDX/DeviceActivity.java` — JedEye in the model-display switch and in the BLE-scanner name-prefix handler

A second tiny commit (`SapComm: fix dangling else attaching to the wrong if`) silences a spurious "SAP comm: changed unexpected chrt …" error that fires after every successful read notification on SAP6 / discox / JedEye: the chain in `changedChrt()` was `if (read) {...} if (write) {...} else { error }`, with a missing `else` on the second `if`. Joining the two `if`s makes the `else` only fire for genuinely unexpected UUIDs. Happy to split that commit out into its own PR if you'd prefer.

## Testing

Tested end-to-end on real hardware: TopoDroid (this branch, sideloaded as a debug APK) connecting to a real JedEye device, scanning, pairing, and capturing measurements. Shots arrive correctly (3.79 m / 315.9° / 25.7° in one log) and are inserted as standard `insertDistoXShot(...)` rows with station auto-assignment running normally. Burst of 50+ measurements without disconnects after a NINA firmware update on the device.

No native code, no new resources, no dependency changes.

body:
## Summary

Lands C4.0 — \`pkg/query/planner.go\` (~325 LOC) extracted from \`origin/archive/gemini-bulk-2026-05-13^3\` per Track C critical path. Net-new code: there is no current planner-equivalent in \`pkg/query\`; the existing Step-based Executor goes directly from Query AST to per-step materialization. C4.0 introduces the alternative Volcano-style translation that emits a tree of C3.0 operators.

## What's lifted

- \`Planner\` struct (graph \`storage.Storage\`)
- \`NewPlanner\` / \`Plan\` / \`PlanSub\`
- \`planMatchWithOptimization\` — MATCH → IndexSeek/NodeScan + Expand chain
- \`planSinglePattern\`, \`getPatternVars\`
- \`findEqualityCondition\` — n.prop = literal index-seek detector
- \`isWhereConsumedByIndex\` (currently always false; archive marker)
- \`hasAggregates\`
- \`(q *Query).withoutUnion\` — UNION recursion helper

Clauses handled: MATCH (hash-join on common vars vs nested-loop on no overlap), OPTIONAL MATCH, UNWIND, WHERE, CREATE, SET, DELETE, REMOVE, MERGE, RETURN (Aggregate or Project), WITH+Next recursion, UNION recursion. One OTEL span per \`PlanSub\` entry.

## What's deferred

- **CALL clause handling** — \`q.Call\` references \`CallClause\` (C5 parser territory; field doesn't exist on \`Query\` yet) and emits \`CallOperator\` (C3-deferred to C6 co-land). Two prerequisites must land first. Marker comment lives at the original block position so the next agent can reinstate it cleanly.
- **Planner-level unit tests** — deferred to C4.1, mirroring the C1.0/C1.1 and C3.0/C3.1 splits. Operator + planner tests will likely surface the same kind of drift C1.1 caught (\`findKey\` vs \`findChild\` navigation bug).

## Drift fixes vs archive parent (3c27aaf)

| Issue | Fix |
|---|---|
| \`if q.Call != nil { ... }\` block (lines 86-94) referenced \`Query.Call\` field that doesn't exist in current AST + \`CallOperator\` deferred from C3.0 | Block stripped; marker comment preserves intent for future reinstatement |
| Imports were single-block (stdlib + third-party + local mixed) | Reordered per gofmt convention (stdlib / third-party / local) |

Spike-quality archive comments preserved verbatim:
- \`om.Patterns[0], // Simplified\` on OPTIONAL MATCH
- \`// For the spike, assume simple linear expansion\` on Relationship chaining
- \`// In real life, we'd only consume the specific part\` + \`return false // Keep FilterOperator just in case for now (redundant but safe)\` on \`isWhereConsumedByIndex\`

These are honest spike markers — left intact to keep the C4.0 lift surgical; cleanup is C4.1 territory once tests anchor the contract.

## Coexistence, not replacement

This Planner has **NO consumers in this PR**. The existing Step-based \`Executor\` (\`executor.go\` + \`executor_steps.go\`) keeps serving \`/v1/cypher\` unchanged. C5 (parser additions for CALL/CREATE/SET/DELETE/REMOVE/MERGE) + a future planner-driven executor path wire it up.

- [x] \`go vet ./...\` clean

- [x] \`go test -short ./pkg/query/\` — pass (existing suite unaffected; ~21s)
- [ ] Planner-level unit tests — C4.1 follow-up
- [ ] End-to-end Cypher → Planner → Operator integration — needs C5 + a planner-driven executor

## Sequencing

Closes Track C "C4" in \`docs/NEXT_STEPS_2026-05-13.md\`. Unblocks **C5** (Cypher parser additions for CALL/CREATE/SET/DELETE/REMOVE/MERGE) which is the next critical-path move. C6 (procedures registry) co-lands with the deferred CallOperator + the q.Call block reinstatement.

body:
## Summary

Closes 4/16 of the lazy `omicsclaw/` → `bot/` reverse imports tracked in
the Phase 1 boundary guardrail (`tests/test_no_reverse_imports.py`).
`omicsclaw/runtime/preflight/sc_batch.py` is now **completely free** of
reverse imports — the engine-side single-cell preflight no longer
reaches back into `bot/` at runtime.

Approach: three thin slices, each landing as its own commit with the
ratchet lowered inline so intermediate states stay green.

1. **`refactor(runtime): lift _lookup_skill_info into omicsclaw.runtime.skill_lookup`** — pure registry walk, no bot state; `bot.skill_orchestration._lookup_skill_info` stays as a thin alias for backward compat. Ratchet 16 → 14.
2. **`refactor(runtime): lift skill-chain helpers into omicsclaw.runtime.skill_chain`** — `_normalize_extra_args`, `_run_skill_via_shared_runner`, `_run_omics_skill_step` all move to `omicsclaw/runtime/skill_chain.py`. The new `run_omics_skill_step` takes an explicit `output_root: Path` so the runtime side stays free of bot path constants; the bot adapter keeps the `OUTPUT_DIR` default. Ratchet 14 → 13.
3. **`refactor(preflight): invert control flow so sc_batch never re-enters execute_omicsclaw`** — `_auto_prepare_sc_batch_integration` now returns a control-signal dict (`None` / `{"final_message": str}` / `{"chained_args": ..., "summary_prefix": ...}`) instead of calling back into `bot.tool_executors.execute_omicsclaw`. The bot side consumes the dict and self-recurses with `auto_prepare=False`. Same observable behavior; engine side is strictly one-way. Ratchet 13 → 12, `sc_batch.py` drops off the allowlist.

## Why

Phase 1 (#192) shipped the boundary guardrail and a ratcheted allowlist
of 16 grandfathered lazy reverse imports. `omicsclaw/runtime/preflight/sc_batch.py`
held 4 of them and was the easiest win to attack first — the helpers
involved (`_lookup_skill_info`, `_run_omics_skill_step`,
`_run_skill_via_shared_runner`) were already 95% domain-agnostic; only
`OUTPUT_DIR` and one chain-tail callback were keeping them on the bot
side.

Lifting them out means:
- The single-cell preflight is now testable without any `bot/` import.
- `bot.skill_orchestration` shrinks ~140 LOC (mostly delegation aliases).
- Identity invariants from Phase 1 (`bot.core.X is bot.skill_orchestration.X`)
  are preserved — verified end-to-end.

The remaining 12 entries in the allowlist live in
`omicsclaw/app/server.py` (6) and `omicsclaw/interactive/{interactive,tui}.py` (6).
Both require larger architectural moves (lifting `CHANNEL_REGISTRY` /
`ChannelManager` to `omicsclaw/`, exposing a surface-agnostic engine
entry for interactive). Separate Phase 2 slices.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/test_no_reverse_imports.py` — 3/3 green (top-level=0, lazy
      allowlist matches 12 real grandfathered sites, count pin 12).
- [x] Full Phase 1 regression: `tests/engine/ tests/bot/
      tests/test_bot_agent_loop_imports.py tests/test_compact_slash_command.py
      tests/test_channels.py` — 143 passed, 4 errors. The 4 errors are
      the pre-existing pydantic v1/v2 collection failures documented in
      the Phase 1 PR (`tests/bot/test_skill_orchestration.py` ×2 +
      `tests/bot/test_tool_executors.py` ×2). Confirmed unchanged.
- [x] Identity invariant: `bot.core._lookup_skill_info is bot.skill_orchestration._lookup_skill_info` — true.
- [x] sc_batch.py imports via `bot.core` entry order — no circular-import
      regression beyond the pre-existing bot.core ↔ bot.tool_executors
      pattern documented in `bot/tool_executors.py:11-25`.

body:
### Motivation
- Fix browser errors (missing `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, failed websocket handshake, `transport close`, polling errors) when the Vercel frontend (`https://nivine.vercel.app`) connects to the Render backend (`https://niviine.onrender.com`).
- Ensure Socket.IO uses a secure, production-ready configuration with `wss`/polling fallback, credentials support, and robust reconnect behavior. 
- Prevent origin / trailing-slash mismatches and supply explicit preflight handling so modern browsers can complete OPTIONS handshakes. 

### Description
- Tightened Express CORS by normalizing request origins, allowlisting configured env origins, adding `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials`, explicit allowed headers/methods, and returning `204` for allowed `OPTIONS` and `403` for disallowed `OPTIONS` in `server.js` (preflight handling and headers). 
- Replaced wildcard Socket.IO CORS with a validation callback that normalizes and allowlists origins, enabled `credentials`, explicit `allowedHeaders`, kept `transports: ['websocket','polling']`, and enabled `allowUpgrades` so clients can fallback cleanly in `server.js`. 
- Normalized frontend env URL handling in `lib/config.ts` by adding `SOCKET_URL`, `API_URL`, and `BACKEND_API_URL` helpers to avoid trailing-slash mismatches. 
- Hardened client socket code in `lib/socketService.ts` to use `SOCKET_URL`, `withCredentials: true`, explicit `transports`, and production reconnect/backoff parameters (`reconnectionAttempts: Infinity`, delays/backoff, `autoConnect:false`) while keeping polling fallback. 
- Updated `.env.example` and `render.yaml` to include `FRONTEND_ORIGIN`, `CORS_ORIGIN`, and `VERCEL_FRONTEND_URL` set to `https://nivine.vercel.app` and documented required Vercel env vars (`VITE_API_URL`/`VITE_SOCKET_URL`). 

### Testing
- Ran `npm install` which failed in this environment due to a registry policy error (`403 Forbidden` for `@deepgram/sdk`), preventing a complete dependency install. 
- Ran `npm run build` which failed here because `vite` was not available in the environment image, so a full build test could not be completed locally. 
- Static inspection and manual smoke-checks of the CORS/socket code paths were performed; runtime validation on Render/Vercel is still required (deploy with `FRONTEND_ORIGIN=https://nivine.vercel.app` on Render and `VITE_API_URL`/`VITE_SOCKET_URL=https://niviine.onrender.com` on Vercel to verify end-to-end).

author: justinawei
body:
## Summary

- Replaces the "most recently active speaks" swarm heuristic. That flipped focus on every event when two agents were busy, so the listener heard them stepping on each other. Today's main avoids that by destructively dropping older queued items via `queue_drop_other_session` — coherent but lossy: you never hear the agents you're not currently driving.
- New model: when two or more sessions are active (last 3 minutes), every non-pierce event lands in its own session's pending pile. A per-session scheduler ticks every second and drains any channel that's idle for 2 seconds (natural turn boundary) OR has hit 5 pending items (backpressure cap). Longest pile wins ties.
- Each per-channel flush speaks as one utterance attributed to that session, so the speaker-change label naturally tags who said what and the speech queue serializes channels. No two voices overlap, and the background agents' summaries arrive instead of vanishing.
- Single-channel scenarios bypass the scheduler entirely — one CC session firing events still speaks live, no two-second batching latency.
- Pierces (failures, questions) still cut through immediately with an `Agent <name>:` label, regardless of mode.

Draft because the per-channel drain still uses the existing tag-count digest format (`Api: 3 edits, a test`). That works but isn't very narrative. Want to validate the structure works end-to-end with real parallel agents before swapping in a Haiku-summarized version of the actual prose.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest -q` (354 passed, 1 skipped)
- [x] `ruff check heard/ tests/`
- [ ] Two CC instances in two terminals working concurrently — each agent's bursts should drain as a single attributed summary about two seconds after it goes quiet.
- [ ] One CC session by itself — narration plays live with no extra latency (scheduler should not engage).
- [ ] Failure / question events during multi-channel — pierce immediately with the agent label.

author: neill-k
body:
💡 **What:** Added `aria-label` to the user account menu button and `aria-busy={loading}` to the GitHub sign-in button in `src/components/AuthButtons.tsx`. Also created an entry in `.Jules/palette.md` noting these learnings.
🎯 **Why:** 
1. The account menu button displays the user's `email`, but uses the utility class `hidden sm:inline`. On smaller viewports, the text is hidden, and because the user avatar icon has `aria-hidden="true"`, the button loses its accessible name entirely. Providing a static or dynamic `aria-label` ensures screen readers can announce it properly on mobile.
2. The "Sign in with GitHub" action is asynchronous. While it disabled the button visually and behaviorally, screen reader users wouldn't know why it was unresponsive or that a process was ongoing. Adding `aria-busy={loading}` fixes this.
♿ **Accessibility:**
- Ensures an interactive element retains an accessible name on small viewports.
- Communicates background loading processes for a critical auth interaction.

## Resumo

- **Nova aba "Emissões"** na Central de Auditoria: rastreio completo de quem emitiu cada voucher (individual e lote), com filtros por dia, tipo, serviço e operador — e exportação CSV separada.
- **Migration `20260513000000`**: adiciona `created_by` em `service_voucher_batches` e atualiza o RPC `issue_voucher_batch_v1` para gravar o operador no momento da criação do lote.
- **"Emitido por" nos cards de lote**: cada lote exibe o nome do operador responsável pela emissão.

## Detalhes

### Etapa e grupo verificados ✅
A emissão individual (`issue_voucher_v1`) e em lote (`issue_voucher_batch_v1`) já exigiam `event_stage_id` obrigatório (exceção se nulo). A atribuição ao grupo é feita pelo campo `label` do lote. Ambos continuam funcionando sem alteração nessa lógica.

### Rastreio de emissão (novo)
A tabela `service_voucher_audit` já registrava toda criação/revogação com `issuer_id = auth.uid()` via trigger. O que faltava era **expor isso na UI**. A nova aba "Emissões" em `/admin/vouchers/auditoria` mostra:

| Campo | Descrição |
|---|---|
| Data/Hora | Quando foi emitido |
| Tipo | Emissão / Reemissão / Revogação / Expiração |
| Serviço | Alimentação / Transporte / Alojamento |
| QR Code | Código do voucher |
| Pessoa / Lote | Nome (nominal) ou label do lote (agregado) |
| **Operador** | Nome do usuário que executou a ação |

### Considerados e não registrados
- Para vouchers nominais: a coluna "Pessoa" mostra quem recebeu; ausência de linha = não emitido.
- Para lotes: os cards de lote mostram `X ativos / Y total`, permitindo ver quantos foram emitidos e quantos usados.

## Plano de teste
- [ ] Emitir um voucher individual e verificar que aparece na aba "Emissões" com o operador correto
- [ ] Emitir um lote e confirmar que o card de lote exibe "Emitido por [nome]"
- [ ] Filtrar emissões por operador e por dia
- [ ] Exportar CSV de emissões

This PR updates [transformers](https://pypi.org/project/transformers) from **2.11.0** to **5.8.1**.



<details>

   ### 5.8.1
   ```
   This release is mainly to fix the Deepseek V4 integration!!! 

<img width="714" height="774" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0d85e891-a0ff-436e-a9d4-b6633096f2b5" />


* [fix] Add fatal_error to ContinuousBatchingManager so the serving... by qgallouedec, remi-or
* Fix WeightConverter regex incorrectly matching shared_experts as experts by silencelamb, claude
* Fix deepseek v4 by ArthurZucker (45892)
* Deepseek v4 csa mask collapse by ArthurZucker, Sawyer117 (45928)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 5.8.0
   ```
   New Model additions

 DeepSeek-V4

<img width="6604" height="3574" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4c0fdb29-f770-463c-a97b-d24438896a4c" />

DeepSeek-V4 is the next-generation MoE (Mixture of Experts) language model from DeepSeek that introduces several architectural innovations over DeepSeek-V3. The architecture replaces Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) with a hybrid local + long-range attention design, swaps residual connections for Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC), and bootstraps the first few MoE layers with a static token-id → expert-id hash table. This implementation covers DeepSeek-V4-Flash, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, and their -Base pretrained variants, which share the same architecture but differ in width, depth, expert count and weights.

**Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/deepseek_v4) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash/blob/main/DeepSeek_V4.pdf)
* Add DeepSeek V4 (45643) by ArthurZucker in [45643](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/45643)

 Gemma 4 Assistant

<img width="2000" height="400" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/02c79b0b-a172-4495-b09d-a6a4b625ee66" />

Gemma 4 Assistant is a small, text-only model that enables speculative decoding for Gemma 4 models using the Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) method and associated candidate generator. The model shares the same Gemma4TextModel backbone as other Gemma 4 models but uses KV sharing throughout the entire model, allowing it to reuse the KV cache populated by the target model and skip the pre-fill phase entirely. This architecture includes cross-attention to make the most of the target model's context, allowing the assistant to accurately predict more drafted tokens per drafting round.

**Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/gemma4_assistant)
* First model (45788) by SindhuRaghuram97 in [45788](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/45788)

 GraniteSpeechPlus

<img width="1310" height="930" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/94fc3730-742c-4b9e-ab6a-ed2e5c75d0bf" />

Granite Speech Plus is a variant of Granite Speech that enhances the projector by consuming the concatenation of the encoder's final hidden states with an arbitrary subset of its intermediate hidden states along the feature dimension. It is a multimodal speech-to-text model that can transcribe audio, provide speaker annotation and word level timestamps by responding to text prompts. The model inherits the same architecture components as Granite Speech including the speech encoder, query transformer projector, language model, and optional LoRA adapter.

**Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/granite_speech_plus)
* Support for a new Granite-Speech-Plus model (45695) by zvik in [45695](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/45695)

 Granite4Vision

Granite Vision 4.1 is a vision-language model from IBM Research designed for enterprise-grade document data extraction. It specializes in chart extraction (Chart2CSV, Chart2Summary, Chart2Code), table extraction (JSON, HTML, OTSL), and semantic key-value pair extraction. The model builds on LLaVA-NeXT with architectural innovations including SigLIP2 Vision Encoder, Window Q-Former Projectors, and DeepStack Feature Injection with 8 vision-to-LLM injection points.

**Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/granite4_vision)
* Add Granite 4.1 Vision (granite4_vision) (45597) by artem-spector in [45597](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/45597)

 EXAONE-4.5

<img width="3840" height="2160" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/55eb732d-f9da-4f97-8226-2cd3f6476ca0" />

EXAONE 4.5 is the first open-weight vision language model developed by LG AI Research, integrating a dedicated visual encoder into the existing EXAONE 4.0 framework to expand multimodal capabilities. The model features 33 billion parameters in total, including 1.2 billion parameters from the vision encoder, and achieves competitive performance in general benchmarks while outperforming similar-sized models in document understanding and Korean contextual reasoning. It builds on EXAONE 4.0 with key enhancements including an expanded vocabulary of 153,600 tokens, support for up to 256K token context windows, and a Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) mechanism.

**Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/exaone4_5) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2604.08644) | [Blog Post](https://www.lgresearch.ai/blog/view?seq=641)
* Add EXAONE 4.5 implementations (45471) by nuxlear in [45471](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/45471)

 PP-FormulaNet

PP-FormulaNet-L and PP-FormulaNet_plus-L are lightweight models designed for table structure recognition, focusing on accurately recognizing table structures in documents and natural scenes. The models are part of the SLANet series and can be used for image-to-text tasks, specifically for detecting and processing mathematical formulas and table structures from images.

**Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/pp_formulanet)
* [Model] Add PP-FormulaNet Model Support (45626) by zhang-prog in [45626](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/45626)



 Breaking changes

Apex integration has been removed from the library (including RMSNorm usage in T5 and related models), so users relying on Apex for mixed precision or fused ops should migrate to PyTorch's native equivalents instead.
* 🚨 Get rid of most Apex references (45723) by Rocketknight1



 Tokenization

Fixed tokenizer mapping issues for DeepSeek R1 distilled (Qwen2) and DeepSeek OCR models, and resolved a significant performance regression in `PreTrainedTokenizer.convert_ids_to_tokens` where `skip_special_tokens=True` was rebuilding the special token set on every iteration, resulting in a ~300x speedup for that code path.


* deepseek r1 distilled tokenizer fix for qwen2 mapping (45741) by itazap in [45741]
* DeepSeek OCR specifies an incorrect tokenizer class on the Hub (45739) by hmellor in [45739]
* PythonBackend slow tokenizer convert_ids_to_tokens fix (45728) by i3hz in [45728]


 Bugfixes and improvements

* fix: correct spelling in continuous_api docstring (45749) by Dhruv908615 in [45749]
* Fix link to modular transformers documentation (45746) by SangbumChoi in [45746]
* Gemma4: fix failed test cases (45568) by kaixuanliu in [45568]

body:
## Summary

- A non-root, non-scrollable element renders as `ViewKind::Layer` in the iOS renderer ([`renderer.rs:358-387`](https://github.com/PupilTong/Paws/blob/main/ios-renderer-backend/src/renderer.rs#L358-L387)). Today both the clip-emit paths filter `Layer` out, so `overflow: hidden | clip` on a layer-backed element is silently ignored — descendant content draws past the box bounds.
- This PR emits `SetClipsToBounds` for Layer kind too. The Swift `OP_SET_CLIPS` handler now dispatches on the underlying object type: `UIView.clipsToBounds` for View / ScrollView, `CALayer.masksToBounds` for Layer.
- Spec reference: [CSS Overflow Level 3 §2.1](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-overflow/#overflow-properties). Both `hidden` and `clip` mandate clipping descendants to the box's content edge; the implementation difference (Layer vs View) is invisible to the spec.

## Why this shape

`UIView.clipsToBounds` and `CALayer.masksToBounds` are independent UIKit knobs (a UIView's `clipsToBounds` setter does not propagate to its backing layer's `masksToBounds`), so the Swift handler must dispatch on the actual object type stored in the view map. This mirrors the existing pattern for `OP_SET_BG_COLOR` at [`OpExecutor.swift:148-154`](https://github.com/PupilTong/Paws/blob/main/ios-renderer-backend/Sources/PawsRenderer/OpExecutor.swift#L148-L154), which already handles UIView-or-CALayer dispatch for background color.

`emit_full_node` for Layer skips the op when `state.clips == false` because `CALayer.masksToBounds` defaults to `false` — the explicit-false op would be wasted bandwidth on the op buffer. View / ScrollView keep their always-emit behaviour unchanged (so the root's `clipsToBounds = false` baseline still applies). The dirty-check path fires whenever a Layer transitions clip states across frames.

## Files

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `ios-renderer-backend/src/renderer.rs` | Extend the kind guards at line 273 (dirty-check path) and line 339 (`emit_full_node` initial path) to include `ViewKind::Layer`. Skip the no-op `clips == false` emit for Layer specifically. |
| `ios-renderer-backend/Sources/PawsRenderer/OpExecutor.swift` | `OP_SET_CLIPS` now dispatches on UIView (→ `clipsToBounds`) vs CALayer (→ `masksToBounds`). |

## Tests (Rust, added under `renderer::tests`)

- `test_layer_kind_emits_clip_op_for_overflow_hidden` — confirms a Layer-kind child with `overflow: hidden` produces both `DeclareLayer` and `SetClipsToBounds` ops.
- `test_layer_kind_emits_clip_op_for_overflow_clip` — same coverage for `overflow: clip`, mirroring `has_clip_overflow`'s shared treatment of hidden + clip.
- `test_layer_kind_overflow_visible_does_not_emit_clip_op` — inverse check: Layer-kind with the default `overflow: visible` must NOT emit its own clip op (guard against a future refactor accidentally always-emitting for Layer kind).

## WPT alignment

No new WPT translation in this PR. CSS Overflow Level 3 clipping at the rendering layer is a paint-correctness behaviour; upstream WPT covers it via reftests (e.g. `css/css-overflow/overflow-001.html` and siblings), which require a pixel-comparison framework Paws does not have yet. Behavioural verification on the engine side is via the three new renderer-level Rust tests; UIKit / Core Animation provides the actual clipping primitive once the op fires. | Status | Count |

| Translated (Yew flavor passing) | 1 |
| In progress | 0 |
| Skipped (with reason) | 0 |
| Not started | n/a |

- [x] `cd Paws && cargo test -p ios-renderer-backend` — 63 passed (was 60; +3 new tests).
- [x] `cd Paws && cargo test --workspace --exclude yew --exclude yew-macro` — every Paws crate green; only pre-existing yew doc-test failures remain (unrelated and unaffected by this change).

## Summary

New `/graph/3d` route renders the same Neo4j entity/relation data as `/graph` but in immersive WebGL via `react-force-graph-3d`. Existing 2D Canvas view caps out around 200 nodes with flat labels; the 3D view scales to 500+ nodes with sphere+sprite groups, bloom postprocessing, and edge particles reading as *knowledge flow* — useful for OpenClaw pitches and clinician demos.

## What's new

### Backend (`ro-ai-bridge`)
- `VisualizationQuery` gains `include_primekg: Option<bool>`
- New `build_visualization_primekg_bridge_cypher()` — pure Cypher builder, easy to test
- `get_visualization_data()` runs a second pass when `include_primekg=true`: tenant entities → `SAME_AS` → `:PrimeKG` nodes (the bridge created by `scripts/primekg_import.sh`)
- Graceful fallback: if the bridge query errors, returns tenant-only with a `warn!` log

### Frontend (`ro-ai-dashboard`)
- `/graph/3d` page with `dynamic(() => import("react-force-graph-3d"), { ssr: false })` because Three.js touches `window`
- Per-node: sphere mesh + optional degree-5+ halo + always-on sprite text label
- Theme-aware scene background (`slate-800` light / `slate-900` dark) so the dark WebGL canvas blends with the surrounding light dashboard chrome
- `UnrealBloomPass` wired through `fg.postProcessingComposer()` — toggle in the Rendering card. Edge particles + labels also toggleable
- **Graph Scope card** with tenant dropdown (sourced from `/iam/my-tenants`, overrides `X-Tenant-Id` so the user keeps their session) + **Include PrimeKG** checkbox
- `fetchGraphVisualization()` + `fetchGraphStats()` gain `tenantOverride`; `fetchGraphVisualization` also gains `includePrimekg`
- New deps: `react-force-graph-3d@1.29`, `three@0.184`, `three-spritetext@1.10`, `@types/three`

_(post-merge: capture from running dashboard at /graph/3d)_

## Summary
Three new models + four new routes to back the next batch of Worker Portal features.

**MachineIssue** (`models/MachineIssue.js` + `api/machineIssue.js`)
- `POST /api/v2/machine-issue` — worker reports a breakdown / maintenance need with `title`, `description`, `severity` (low/medium/high/critical).
- `GET /api/v2/machine-issue/employee/:empId` — worker history.
- `GET /api/v2/machine-issue?status=&machineId=` — admin list.
- `GET /api/v2/machine-issue/:id` — detail.
- `PUT /api/v2/machine-issue/:id/status` — admin updates status + resolution.
- `DELETE /api/v2/machine-issue/:id` — worker withdraws an open issue.

**Announcement** (`models/Announcement.js` + `api/announcement.js`)
- `GET /api/v2/announcement/active?dept=` — workers' feed (audience=all OR department-match, validity window enforced, pinned first).
- `GET /api/v2/announcement` — admin list.
- `POST /api/v2/announcement` — admin creates with type / audience / pin / validity.
- `PUT /api/v2/announcement/:id` — admin edits.
- `DELETE /api/v2/announcement/:id` — soft delete via `isActive`.

**EmployeeFeedback** (`models/EmployeeFeedback.js` + `api/feedback.js`)
- `POST /api/v2/feedback` — worker files complaint or suggestion, optional anonymous flag.
- `GET /api/v2/feedback/employee/:empId` — worker history.
- `GET /api/v2/feedback?status=&type=&category=` — admin list.
- `PUT /api/v2/feedback/:id/respond` — admin replies + updates status.
- `DELETE /api/v2/feedback/:id` — worker withdraws an open entry.

**Active Job** (`api/shift.js`)
- `GET /api/v2/shift/active-job/:empId` — single open shift with deep-populated `machine.elastics.elastic` + `machine.orderRunning` (JobOrder + Order + Customer + elastic refs) so the Worker Portal renders the Current Job screen in one round-trip.

author: rita-codes
body:
Move the implementation of recurring events out of the MIT-licensed scheduler packages and into the premium ones, so the feature can only run when the premium package is installed.

Until now, every line of RRULE parsing, occurrence expansion and scope-aware updates lived in `@mui/x-scheduler-internals` (MIT). The "is this premium?" check was a runtime string flag in state, which anyone could remove from the MIT bundle to use the feature without a license.

## What changed
  - **Logic** (`parseRRule`, `getOccurrencesForVisibleDays`, `updateRecurringEvent`, scope updates, RRULE projection, presets math) now lives in `@mui/x-scheduler-internals-premium`. The MIT bundles no longer contain any of this code.
  - **UI** (`RecurrenceTab`, `RecurringScopeDialog`) moves to `@mui/x-scheduler-premium`. The community `EventDialog` accepts them through a `slots` prop, and `EventCalendarPremium` / `EventTimelinePremium` supply them automatically.
  - **Selectors** that wrap recurring events also moved to premium.
  - **Gate** for showing recurring events changed from `state.plan === 'premium'` to `state.recurringEventsPlugin != null`. Removing the check from the MIT code no longer enables the feature, the implementation simply is not there.
  - **The `plan` state field is gone** (it was only used for this gate).

## Pattern used
Same shape as the existing `SchedulerLazyLoadingPlugin` from the premium internals: a slot on `SchedulerState` (`recurringEventsPlugin`) holds an object provided by the premium store on construction. The community code calls methods through that slot, the premium code provides the implementation.

The plugin itself is a plain object (singleton, no per-instance state) so the API matches what it really is: a bag of functions.

author: morganmcg1
body:
## Hypothesis

**Random Fourier Features (Tancik et al. 2020, NeRF-style RFF) on mesh coordinates — fresh input-encoding axis, mechanism-orthogonal to all 8 in-flight PRs and untested on this stack.**

The merged Kendall baseline (#1906) at val=71.43 / test=62.99 sees raw normalized `(x, z)` coordinates per-node, then passes them through MLP/Transformer layers with the standard low-frequency-bias of ReLU/GELU activations. Tancik et al. ("Fourier Features Let Networks Learn High Frequency Functions in Low Dimensional Domains", NeurIPS 2020) showed that **ReLU MLPs are theoretically biased toward learning low-frequency functions** on low-dimensional coord inputs — exactly the regime here (2D coords → high-freq pressure/velocity targets). Their fix: project coords through a fixed random matrix `B ∈ R^(d × m)` with `B_ij ~ N(0, σ²)`, then concat `[sin(2π·B·x), cos(2π·B·x)]` as input. The frequency bandwidth `σ` is the key knob.

**Why this matters for TandemFoilSet pressure prediction:**
- Foil leading-edge suction peaks, separation zones, and trailing wake gradients are inherently **high spatial-frequency phenomena**. Per-split errors are dominated by `val_single_in_dist` (79.18) and `val_geom_camber_rc` (88.09) — both involve high-curvature foil geometries with sharp pressure variation.
- Current Transolver attention learns features from raw `(x, z)` — but the **low-freq bias means it under-fits the high-freq pressure spikes** near foil edges. RFF provides an explicit sin/cos basis that lets the network learn these high frequencies directly.

**Why this is NOT a duplication of the closed `unified_pos` axis (PR #1454/#1551):**
- `unified_pos=True` was **grid-based reference-frame encoding** (lookup distances to a fixed reference grid). The closure mechanism: "normalized (x, z) input already conveys position fully within each mesh, so unified-pos adds redundant information that displaces capacity." That critique was about *redundant position injection*, not about learning *high-frequency functions*.
- RFF is fundamentally different: it gives the network **a sin/cos basis of varied frequencies** as a learning prior. The information content is the same `(x, z)` but the *representation* makes high-frequency functions easy to learn. It's a representational change, not a positional one.
- Tancik et al. directly contrasts RFF against "positional encoding" methods like NeRF's deterministic encoding — they're related but distinct mechanism families.

**Why this axis now:**
- **Fresh axis untouched on this stack.** Mechanism-orthogonal to optimizer-stability (#1937 closed, #2063 Lion in-flight), arch-structural (#1938 per-token FiLM), schedule (#2021 OneCycle), parameter-norm regularization (#1981 wd), aux-task (#2049 aux Re), input-augmentation (#1873 SDF), loss-shape (#1757 β), sample-rebalancing (closed #1954 HEM).
- **Composes with FiLM.** FiLM modulates intermediate features via global params; RFF operates on per-node coords *before* FiLM. Independent.
- **Composes with Kendall.** RFF changes input representation; Kendall reweights output channels. Independent.
- **Low complexity.** ~30 lines: random matrix buffer + sin/cos concat in `forward`. Frozen B (standard practice).
- **Directly OOD-targeted via mechanism.** High-freq fitting capacity should help `val_geom_camber_rc` (the highest-error camber split with sharp leading-edge gradients) AND `test_re_rand` (where Re-conditioned high-freq behavior shifts).

**Why two arms (σ sweep):**
- **`σ=1.0` (low-freq, conservative):** mild high-frequency lift, lowest risk of overfitting to noise. Most-likely-to-land arm. Predicted: small win.
- **`σ=4.0` (moderate-freq, aggressive):** stronger high-frequency basis, may unlock leading-edge resolution. Higher variance arm. Tancik et al. found σ has a Goldilocks zone — both arms bracket where the optimum should be.

**Why it might not land:**
- Tandem-foil pressure fields may not actually need high-frequency basis — the smooth-fluid structure is captured well enough by the existing attention mechanism.
- σ=4.0 may over-fit mesh-discretization artifacts (per-node noise) rather than physical structure → test regression.
- Coords are already normalized per-mesh; if the normalization removes the spatial-scale information needed for frequency calibration, RFF gives the same signal across all meshes regardless of physical size.
- Transolver's PhysicsAttention slice-routing may already implicitly capture high-freq behavior via the slice probabilities (acting as an adaptive basis); RFF would then add redundancy similar to the `unified_pos` failure mode.

## Predicted Δ on `val_avg/mae_surf_p` / `test_avg/mae_surf_p`

- **Arm `σ=1.0` (low-freq):** val **70.0–71.4** (≤−2.0% vs 71.43), test **62.0–63.0**. Most-likely-to-land arm.
- **Arm `σ=4.0` (moderate-freq):** val 69.5–72.0 (uncertain — could unlock or over-fit), test 61.5–63.5. Higher variance arm.

**Bracket interpretation:** if σ=1.0 wins, low-freq is the lever; merge and sweep finer `{σ=0.5, 2.0}`. If σ=4.0 wins, moderate-freq unlocks; sweep upward `{6.0, 8.0}`. If both regress, axis closes — Transolver already captures high-freq structure adequately.

## Current baseline (post-#1906 Kendall merge)

- **val_avg/mae_surf_p:** **71.4346** (seed 0, SWA-model eval)
- **test_avg/mae_surf_p:** **62.9866** (seed 0, SWA-model, 4-split all finite)
- **W&B baseline run:** `dkfjae5o`
- Config: Transolver (5 blocks) + FiLM (mid_dim=64) + Smooth-L1 (β=1.0) + per-sample Re-weight + Kendall σ heads + grad-clip max_norm=0.5 + wd=1e-4
- Schedule: CosineAnnealingLR(T_max=15), SWA (start_frac=0.75, swa_lr=1e-4, anneal_epochs=2)

## Concrete change spec

### Step 1 — add `FourierCoordFeatures` module to the model file

```python
class FourierCoordFeatures(nn.Module):
    """Random Fourier Features (Tancik et al. 2020) on per-node coordinates.

    Project (x, z) -> [sin(2pi*B*x), cos(2pi*B*x)] where B ~ N(0, sigma^2)
    is a fixed random matrix (registered as buffer, not parameter).
    """
    def __init__(self, coord_dim: int = 2, num_features: int = 16, sigma: float = 1.0):
        super().__init__()
        # B: (coord_dim, num_features), fixed at init, NOT learnable
        B = torch.randn(coord_dim, num_features) * sigma
        self.register_buffer("B", B)
        self.num_features = num_features

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        # x: (B, N, coord_dim), returns (B, N, 2*num_features)
        x_proj = 2.0 * math.pi * (x @ self.B)  # (B, N, num_features)
        return torch.cat([torch.sin(x_proj), torch.cos(x_proj)], dim=-1)
```

### Step 2 — wire into the model's input processing

Identify where the model receives per-node coords (likely in the Transolver `forward` or in `train.py` before passing to the model — check the input tensor shape and channel layout). Apply `FourierCoordFeatures` to the **normalized coords** (post any existing normalization), and **concatenate** the RFF output with the existing input features along the channel dim.

```python
# In model __init__:
if args.fourier_features:
    self.fourier_coords = FourierCoordFeatures(
        coord_dim=2,  # x, z
        num_features=args.fourier_num_features,
        sigma=args.fourier_sigma,
    )
    # input_dim is increased by 2 * num_features for the first linear/embedding layer
else:
    self.fourier_coords = None

# In forward, BEFORE the first projection layer:
coords = x_input[..., :2]  # whatever slice gives (B, N, 2) normalized coords
if self.fourier_coords is not None:
    rff = self.fourier_coords(coords)  # (B, N, 2*num_features)
    x_input = torch.cat([x_input, rff], dim=-1)
```

**Critical:** the input projection layer's `in_features` must be updated to `original_in_features + 2 * num_features` when `fourier_features=True`. Make sure this dimension propagates correctly through the model constructor.

author: majid667
body:
## Summary
Automated BTC 5-minute scalping bot for Polymarket with smart risk management, real-time monitoring dashboard, and daily loss limits.

## Key Features

### Smart Trading Logic
- **Winning Trades**: Bot continues trading all day when profitable
- **Losing Trades Limit**: Stops trading after 3 losing trades in a single day (consecutive or random)
- **Daily Reset**: Stats auto-reset at midnight for new trading day
- **Continuous Monitoring**: Real-time trade execution and monitoring

### Position Management
- **Position Sizing**: 5% per trade, scales with balance
- **Profit Target**: 1% per winning trade
- **Stop Loss**: 0.3% per losing trade
- **Max Trades/Day**: 100 trades per day limit

### Real-Time Dashboard
- Current balance with profit/loss display
- Losing trades counter (shows remaining before stop)
- Win rate and total P&L tracking
- Trading status indicator (Active/Stopped)
- Live trade history with entry/exit prices

### Risk Management
- Automatic stop after 3 losses per day
- Daily statistics tracking
- Comprehensive logging
- Session summaries

## Files
- `main.py` - Bot manager with daily reset logic
- `trading_engine.py` - Core engine with losing trade tracking
- `polymarket_client.py` - Polymarket API integration
- `config.py` - Configuration (MAX_LOSING_TRADES_PER_DAY = 3)
- `dashboard.py` - Web dashboard with status display
- `requirements.txt` - Dependencies
- `.env.example` - API credentials template
- `README.md` - Complete documentation

## How It Works

1. **Start Trading** - Bot scans markets and executes trades
2. **Winning Trades** - Continue trading for the whole day
3. **Losing Trades** - Count increments (1/3, 2/3, 3/3)
4. **After 3 Losses** - Stop trading, wait for next day
5. **Daily Reset** - At midnight, counter resets to 0/3

## Example Scenarios

**Scenario 1: Mostly Winning**
```
Trade 1: Win +$0.05
Trade 2: Win +$0.04
Trade 3: Loss -$0.02 (1/3)
Trade 4: Win +$0.06
Trade 5: Loss -$0.01 (2/3)
Trade 6: Win +$0.05
...continues all day
```

**Scenario 2: Quick Stop**
```
Trade 1: Loss -$0.02 (1/3)
Trade 2: Loss -$0.01 (2/3)
Trade 3: Loss -$0.02 (3/3)
🛑 TRADING STOPPED - Come back tomorrow!
```

## Setup
```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
cp .env.example .env
# Add your Polymarket API credentials
python main.py
# Access dashboard: http://localhost:5000
```

## Logging
Each trade logged with status:
- Winning: `Winning trade - Profit: $X.XX`
- Losing: `Losing trade #N - Loss: $X.XX (M remaining before stop)`
- Daily reset: `Daily reset: New day. Ready to trade!`
- Stop: `Trading stopped for today - Lost 3 trades.`

author: davidesner
body:
## Why
Production deployments since PR #1 have been returning **500 / 404** on every \`/api/*\` call with the runtime error \`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND\`.

Build log evidence:
\`\`\`
api/[...path].ts(1,17): error TS2835: Relative import paths need explicit file extensions in ECMAScript imports when '--moduleResolution' is 'node16' or 'nodenext'. Did you mean '../server/vercel.js'?
server/vercel.ts(1,26): ... Did you mean './db/client.js'?
server/vercel.ts(2,26): ... Did you mean './index.js'?
\`\`\`

Vercel's TypeScript bundler uses \`moduleResolution: 'nodenext'\` which requires explicit \`.js\` extensions on every relative import. Our code was written extensionless (works locally because tsx resolves them). \`vercel build\` printed TS2835 errors but exited 0, so deployments went READY while every function invocation failed with module-not-found at runtime.

## What
Added \`.js\` extensions to every relative import across \`server/\` and \`api/\` (20 files). Per the TypeScript NodeNext convention, you write \`.js\` in source even when the file is \`.ts\` — TS resolves it correctly at compile time, and the emitted JS already has the right extension at runtime.

Also untracked a stray \`.claude/settings.local.json\` that slipped in via \`git add -A\` and gitignored it.

## Test plan
- [x] \`pnpm test\` → 65/65 green
- [x] \`pnpm build\` → clean, no TS2835
- [ ] Vercel production redeploy from \`main\` after merge → \`/api/health\` returns \`{"ok":true}\`
- [ ] Login from the deployed UI succeeds

author: cjee21
body:
- Opt-in to using Segment Heap for Windows CLI and Qt GUI
   As described by Microsoft in latest MSVC changelog:
   > New MSBuild and CMake C++ projects now use Segment Heap by default, helping applications take advantage of modern Windows memory management and security features.
   >
   > Visual Studio now enables Segment Heap by default for new C++ projects. Segment Heap is a modern Windows heap implementation that improves performance, scalability, and security compared to the legacy NT heap. This change helps applications adopt these benefits and prepares them for future platform capabilities.
   >
   > You can configure this behavior in project properties under Manifest Tool → Input and Output. Existing projects are not modified automatically but can opt in using the same settings. 

- Unify resource file
   I just noticed that the MSVC2026 binary has version 25.10. This is because the resource file is one copy per MSVC version and stored together with project file and version update script was not updated to handle the new one. So now follow MediaInfoLib where there is only one resource file and stored in sources directory. This also makes CMake one not dependent on presence of MSVC2022 files. @g-maxime need to update version script to update the new location when this PR is merged.

author: mikecranesync
body:
## Summary

Two security/reliability fixes bundled:

### 1. RAG prompt injection via sentinel strings (closes #1007)

`rag_worker.py` injected raw chunk text into the system prompt without stripping prompt-boundary delimiters. A crafted OEM document containing `--- END REFERENCES ---` (or `--- END NEONDB CONTEXT ---`) could break the reference block and inject instructions with system-role authority into the LLM.

**Fix:** Added `_SENTINEL_RE` regex that strips known sentinel patterns from chunk text at both injection points (`_build_prompt_with_chunks` and `_build_prompt`) before concatenation into `system_content`. Matching text is replaced with `[REF_DELIMITER]` to preserve chunk structure without breaking formatting.

### 2. Stripe CSS/JS blocked by hub CSP (closes #995)

`middleware.ts` `buildCsp()` didn't include Stripe domains. Clicking "Start Free Trial" on `/pricing` hit `ERR_CONNECTION_RESET` on Stripe's fingerprinted CSS chunks from `js.stripe.com`.

**Fix:** Added Stripe origins to `script-src`, `style-src`, `connect-src`, and `frame-src` in `buildCsp()`. Previous PR #1241 fixed nginx-phase2-live.conf but was superseded by the CSP moving to Next.js middleware.

## Test plan
- [ ] CI passes (unit tests, lint, security scans)
- [ ] `bun test` in mira-hub passes  
- [ ] Visit `app.factorylm.com/pricing` → click "Start Free Trial" → Stripe Checkout loads without ERR_CONNECTION_RESET

author: benjaminball1984
body:
## Symptôme

Après merge de PR #38 (qui ajoutait `--legacy-peer-deps` à la commande de build Netlify), le build a échoué à nouveau avec le **même ERESOLVE** mais cette fois sur `npm install`, pas `npm ci` :

```
The build fails during `npm install` because `eslint@10.3.0` conflicts with
`eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y@6.10.2`, which only allows ESLint versions up to 9
```

## Diagnostic

Netlify exécute un `npm install` **automatique** AVANT notre commande de build personnalisée (comportement par défaut pour les projets Node.js). Ce pre-install ne lit pas le flag `--legacy-peer-deps` qu'on a mis dans la commande explicite — il utilise les options par défaut de npm.

## Fix

Création de `web/.npmrc` avec `legacy-peer-deps=true`. `.npmrc` est le mécanisme standard npm pour configurer le comportement par défaut — il s'applique automatiquement à toutes les commandes `npm install`, `npm ci`, `npm i`, peu importe qui les invoque (Netlify auto-install, CI GitHub Actions, dev local).

**Bonus dev local** : avant cette PR, un développeur clonant le repo devait taper `npm install --legacy-peer-deps` manuellement (sinon `npm ci` échouait). Désormais `npm ci` simple suffit.

Le flag `--legacy-peer-deps` dans `netlify.toml` (PR #38) et dans `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (depuis l'étape 18) reste en place — redondant avec `.npmrc` mais utile comme documentation et ceinture-bretelles.

## Test plan

- [x] Local : `rm -rf node_modules && npm ci` → succès (sans flag explicite)
- [x] `npm run typecheck` ✅
- [x] `npm run lint` ✅

author: botnicbot
body:
## Summary

- Gate 3 row 3 of pre-flight now attempts auto-resolution of missing `project:` from `target_ancestors` before halting.
- Exactly-one project value across ancestors → `pkb update_task` and proceed; zero or multi-valued → halt as today (no silent pick).

## Why

Friction F9, dogfood 2026-05-13: `task-a5f7e41e` and `task-3013a7d3` were `status=queued` without `project:`. Polecat refused after ~30s of worktree setup. One PKB read per ancestor (typically ≤ 3) is cheaper than a worktree refusal, and respects [Halt-on-substitute](../../aops-core/skills/supervisor/SKILL.md#halt-on-substitute) — multi-valued ancestors still halt.

Pairs with `mem-69a2394b` (upstream PKB lint that should prevent `status=queued` without `project:` in the first place). This is the runtime safety net; the lint is the primary fix.

Refs: aops-88447bbb

## Test plan

- [ ] Pauli preflight on a `status=queued` task with missing `project:` and exactly one project-bearing ancestor → resolves and dispatches.
- [ ] Pauli preflight on the same with multi-valued ancestors → halts at row 3 with `project ambiguous from ancestors: <values>`.
- [ ] Pauli preflight with zero project-bearing ancestors → halts at row 3 with `project unresolvable: no ancestor carries project`.

author: angelexevior
body:
The previous query used OR across dst and public_key columns, preventing MySQL from using indexes efficiently and causing full table sorts on the 17M-row transactions table, which locked the database for other queries.

Replaced with a UNION of three separate indexed lookups (by dst, by public_key, by alias), each bounded by the limit before merging. Requires composite indexes (dst, height) and (public_key, height) on transactions.

author: unverbraucht
body:
## Summary

Tooling, scripts, and probe kernels for the engine-drift-floor investigation on Qwen3.5 — the investigation that surfaced the RoPE convention mismatch fixed in #241. All additions are env-gated and zero-overhead when unused; no existing code path is modified.

Three logical groups bundled into one PR (all engine-drift-investigation infrastructure):

## (B) Investigation tooling

- **`crates/hipfire-runtime/examples/dump_qwen35_hidden_states.rs`** (NEW) — per-layer hidden-state dump via the existing `HiddenStateRingBuffer` from spec-decode infra. Overrides `extract_layers` to span the full layer range so one chunk produces a `[n_layers, n_pos, hidden_dim]` HFHS-v1 binary for offline compare.

- **`crates/hipfire-arch-qwen35/src/qwen35.rs`** — adds two helper functions + env-gated call sites inside `forward_scratch_layers`. The env-var reads are **hoisted to the top of the function** (read once per forward, not per layer) so the per-layer hot path stays clean:
  - `HIPFIRE_DUMP_DN_INPUTS=<path>` → dump Q/K/V/α/β at the input to `gated_delta_net_*`
  - `HIPFIRE_DUMP_A_RAW=<path>` → dump post-w_alpha projection `a` BEFORE `fused_sigmoid_alpha_gate`
  - `HIPFIRE_DUMP_DN_LAYER=<idx>` → target LinearAttention layer (default 4)

- **Python comparators** under `scripts/`:
  - `dump_hf_hidden_states.py` — HF transformers oracle. Uses `forward_pre_hook` on `model.model.norm` to capture pre-final-norm last-layer output (transformers' `hidden_states[n_layers]` is POST-norm and mismatches hipfire's `HiddenStateRingBuffer` capture point).
  - `dump_hf_dn_inputs.py` — monkey-patches `chunk_gated_delta_rule` to capture call args, replays in-rule `l2norm + 1/sqrt(D) scale` so output aligns with hipfire's post-`fused_qk_l2_norm_scale` state.
  - `compare_hidden_states.py` — per-layer cosine + relative-L2 across all positions.
  - `compare_layer_positions.py` — single-layer per-position drift bucketed; distinguishes recurrent state accumulation from constant input amplification.
  - `compare_dn_inputs.py` — per-tensor (Q/K/V/α/β) compare between hipfire and HF dn-input dumps.
  - `cross_engine_check.py` — sanity-checks that a BF16 `.kldref` is consistent against an HF transformers forward on the same tokens.

## (C) Diagnostic quantize env-gates

In `crates/hipfire-quantize/src/main.rs`, the K-map-level resolution block grows two additive env-gated overrides:

- `HIPFIRE_QUANTIZE_LM_HEAD_F16=1` → force `lm_head.weight` / `output.weight` to `QuantLevel::F16`
- `HIPFIRE_QUANTIZE_LA_F16=1` → force all `linear_attn.{in_proj_qkv,in_proj_z,in_proj_a,in_proj_b,out_proj}.weight` to `QuantLevel::F16`

Both default off. Used to A/B-test per-tensor Q8 quant noise as a KLD-floor contributor (it isn't — see the investigation summary). Diagnostic-only; not for cohort runs.

## (D) FP64 probe kernels

- **`kernels/src/rmsnorm.hip`** adds `rmsnorm_f32_f64acc` variant — fp64 accumulator in the sum-of-squares parallel reduction + fp64 rsqrt; inputs/outputs stay fp32. Same kernel module (one `.hip` file with two `extern \"C\"` functions); dispatched by `rmsnorm_batched` when `HIPFIRE_RMSNORM_F64=1`.
- **`kernels/src/gated_delta_net_f64acc.hip`** (NEW) — same algorithm as `gated_delta_net_f32` but the per-token state tile is held in fp64 (4 KB → 8 KB shared memory). Dispatched by `gated_delta_net_f32` when `HIPFIRE_DELTANET_F64=1`.
- **`crates/rdna-compute/src/{kernels,dispatch}.rs`** — register the new kernel sources + env-gated route swap. Shared-memory size adjusts to 8 bytes/slot in the f64-acc rmsnorm path.

## Investigation summary doc

**`docs/investigations/2026-05-12-engine-drift-floor/00-summary.md`** (NEW) — methodology, ruled-out hypotheses (KV quant, recurrent state precision, QK-norm precision, Q8 LA-weight quant noise, lm_head precision, loader convention mismatches), final attribution (distributed pipeline imprecision), recommendation (accept the post-RoPE-fix 0.08-nat floor as the engine-vs-engine cost), and reproducer commands. Matches the existing `docs/investigations/2026-05-07-rdna1-perf-research/` directory template.

The pre-existing `docs/plans/qwen35-mq4-quality-gap.md` quant-format-planning doc is **NOT touched** — keeps the AWQ / MFP4 / Unsloth-Dynamic planning thread untangled from this investigation.

## Smoke validation

On Q3.5-0.8B chunk 0 (gfx1151):
- `dump_qwen35_hidden_states` produces 192 MB hidden-state binary
- `HIPFIRE_DUMP_DN_INPUTS` produces 48 MB dn-input binary
- `HIPFIRE_DUMP_A_RAW` produces 192 KB α-raw binary
- `HIPFIRE_RMSNORM_F64=1` + `HIPFIRE_DELTANET_F64=1` both dispatch new kernels successfully (process completes, dump output is sane)
- `compare_hidden_states.py` reproduces session findings byte-exactly (layer 0 rel_L2 = 0.0614, layer 3 = 0.0874)

## Backwards compatibility

- All env-gates default off — when unset, the only added overhead is **three `std::env::var` calls per forward** (~3 μs/forward), gated by `Option::Some` checks.
- No new kernels are dispatched on normal inference paths.
- The `hipfire-quantize` env-gates are additive — when both are unset, the K-map-level resolution is byte-identical to before.
- The `ensure_kernel` cache correctly handles two-symbols-in-one-source for `rmsnorm.hip` (the f64 variant is fetched from the same compiled module).

## Test plan

- [x] Builds clean (no new warnings on any added file)
- [x] Smoke run: dump + compare pipeline reproduces session findings byte-exactly
- [x] FP64 probe kernels compile and dispatch successfully when env-gated
- [x] Quantize env-gates produce expected size deltas in the output `.hfq`
- [ ] Reviewer to verify: a normal `eval_hipfire` run with all env-gates UNSET produces byte-identical output to pre-PR (no logits change)
- [ ] Reviewer to verify: the new example builds under the documented feature flags (`--features deltanet`, with `arch-qwen35` from defaults)

body:
## Summary

Slice 4 of 9. Replaces the heatmap skeleton from T2 with a real 12-month activity heatmap that reads from \`WorkspaceActivityEvent\`. Three layers — pure calculator, reader service, component — each with their own tests.

## Layers

### 1. Pure level calculator — \`calculateLevels(cells)\`

In \`src/server/services/activity/heatmap.ts\`. Buckets per-day counts into levels 0–4 via quartile ranges of non-zero days:

- count === 0 → L0
- A single non-zero day → L4 (saturated)
- Spread inputs use linear interpolation across (max − min)
- Outliers pull the rest down but the max always lands in L4

Pure function, no DB, no timezone tricks — fully unit-testable.

### 2. Reader — \`getActivityHeatmap(db, { workspaceId, now? })\`

Runs \`SELECT date_trunc('day', "createdAt") GROUP BY day\` parameterised on \`workspaceId\` (raw SQL — Prisma doesn't expose \`date_trunc\`). Builds the 371-cell (53 weeks × 7 days) window ending at "today", fills unseen days with 0, runs the result through \`calculateLevels\`. Workspace scoping enforced at the SQL level.

### 3. tRPC — \`workspace.getActivityHeatmap\`

Member-gated query, falls back to team-based access for guest project members (same pattern as \`getHomeStats\`).

### 4. Heatmap component

Replaces the skeleton card with:

- 12×12 cells, 2.5px radius, 3px gap. Colours bound to \`--activity-heatmap-l1..l4\` tokens added in T2.
- Hover tooltip: \`<count> events · Month Day, Year\`, absolute-positioned via \`getBoundingClientRect\`.
- Today's cell has a pulsing inset border. Suppressed by the existing \`prefers-reduced-motion\` rule.
- Horizontal scroll on narrow viewports (min-width: 825px on the grid) so the contribution graph doesn't get squashed.
- Footer: total count on the left, Less–More legend on the right.

Heatmap counts events regardless of \`entityType\` — it's a general "how active was this workspace" signal, not a filter view. Week/Month/Year filter pills remain disabled in \`<Tooltip label="Coming soon">\` for now.

## Tests

### Unit (mocked Prisma, 7 cases) — \`heatmap.test.ts\`

- Empty input → all L0
- Uniform non-zero counts → all L4
- Zero days never bucket non-zero
- 1-to-4 spread → L1..L4 monotonically
- Outliers always reach L4
- Today flag unique to today's cell
- Input ordering + counts preserved

### Integration (testcontainer, 4 cases) — \`heatmap.integration.test.ts\`

- Events bucket by day; total counts only events in window
- Workspace scoping — wsA rows don't leak into wsB
- Empty workspaces return 371 cells all at L0
- Any \`entityType\`/\`action\` combination counts

## Test plan

- [x] \`npm run check\` clean
- [x] 13 activity unit tests pass (7 new + 6 existing)
- [x] Integration tests pass on testcontainer
- [x] No hardcoded hex
- [ ] Reviewer (manual): switch a workspace to "Activity dashboard", verify the heatmap renders with the right colours; hover cells to see tooltips; today's cell pulses; resize narrow to confirm horizontal scroll engages.

## Summary

Add [ADR 0005](docs/decisions/0005-ci-verification-strategy.md) recording how this project's invariants get verified on GitHub-hosted Linux runners. The ADR maps `CLAUDE.md` prohibitions 1, 2, 4, 6 and ADR 0004's no-global-state rule onto concrete CI checks, and documents the boundary between "CI scope" and "manual pre-release checklist".

### Three-tier CI strategy

- **Tier 1 — smoke** (every PR, < 1 min, blocking): `cargo build/test/clippy/fmt`, `nm -D` symbol check for `ladspa_descriptor`.
- **Tier 2 — standard** (every PR + push to main, < 5 min, blocking): `analyseplugin` golden diff, `applyplugin` WAV-based lifecycle exercise with RMS / NaN / Inf guard, `assert_no_alloc`-instrumented integration test, AddressSanitizer job.
- **Tier 3 — full** (nightly + workflow_dispatch, < 30 min, non-blocking): ThreadSanitizer for multi-instance, `strace` allow-list on the realtime path, `criterion` regression bench, `cargo audit` / `cargo deny`.

### Explicitly out of CI scope

`snd-dummy` / `snd-aloop` are not loadable on GitHub-hosted runners (kernel modules absent — [actions/runner-images#1114](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/issues/1114), unresolved). Real PipeWire `module-filter-chain` sessions, Ardour / Audacity loading, and `SCHED_FIFO` behaviour are deferred to a manual checklist documented at implementation time as `docs/manual-verification.md`. Triggers for promoting any of these into CI (e.g. a self-hosted runner appearing) are listed in the ADR.

author: seblef
body:
## Summary

- Adds `ICameraController` (`src/game/ICameraController.h`) — pure abstract interface with `SetCamera`, `OnEvent`, and `Update`.
- Adds `FPSCameraController` (`src/game/FPSCameraController.h/.cpp`) — FPS-style mouse look and keyboard movement.
- Updates `src/game/CMakeLists.txt` to include `FPSCameraController.cpp`.

## Behaviour

**`ICameraController`**
- `SetCamera(GameCamera*)` — binds a camera to drive.
- `OnEvent(const core::Event&)` — called by `GameSystem` for each event before `Update`.
- `Update(float dt)` — called once per frame; implementations push a new world transform to the camera.

**`FPSCameraController`**
- Arrow Up/Down = forward/back; Left/Right = strafe; A = ascend; Z = descend.
- Mouse delta → accumulates yaw/pitch; pitch clamped to ±1.5 rad.
- `Update()`: computes `look` from yaw/pitch, `right = kAxisY × look`, moves `position_` by held keys × `kMoveSpeed * dt`, then builds a column-based `Mat4f(right | kAxisY | −look | position)` and calls `camera_->SetWorldTransform()`.
- Constants: `kMoveSpeed = 10 units/s`, `kMouseSensitivity = 0.002 rad/px`.

## Test plan

- [ ] Build succeeds with no cpplint/cppcheck errors.
- [ ] Arrow keys move the camera; mouse look changes yaw/pitch correctly.
- [ ] Pitch clamps at ±1.5 rad (no gimbal flip).
- [ ] Calling `Update()` before `SetCamera()` is a no-op (null guard).

author: fhw12345
body:
## What

Adds the generic multi-agent machinery the rest of the project will compose on. No domain code (no Plus One agents, no real skills, no real tools yet — those are later batches).

## Why

Per ADR-002 we're building our own framework rather than using LangGraph. This PR is the foundation.

The framework gives us:
- **Cycle main loop**: Producer → Joiner → Controller, looped until convergence or depth cap, with a separate streaming variant for SSE.
- **Skill system**: file-based markdown-with-YAML-frontmatter, hot-loadable, with a cheap keyword-based router as baseline.
- **Tool system**: typed Pydantic-validated args, self-reported concurrency safety, partial-result batch dispatch.

These are the three pillars of the agent design and they're all generic — Producer / Joiner / Controller in later PRs are just \`async def\` callables that match the protocol.

## How

\`\`\`
backend/src/plus_one/core/agents/framework/
├── __init__.py    # Public API surface
├── types.py       # AgentContext, Decision, PhaseResult[T]
├── errors.py      # AgentError + family
├── skills.py      # Skill model + parse_skill_file + SkillRegistry + keyword router
├── tools.py       # Tool Protocol + ToolCall + ToolResult + ToolRegistry + run_tool_calls
└── cycle.py       # run_cycle + stream_cycle, ProducerFn / JoinerFn / ControllerFn aliases
\`\`\`

### Notable design decisions (each could be its own ADR if challenged)

1. **PEP 695 generics throughout** (\`class Foo[T]: ...\`, \`def f[T](...)\`) — consistent with the LLM layer (PR #1). Migration cost: zero, since this is greenfield.

2. **\`ToolResult.ok=False\` for all failure modes** — including tool exceptions, validation errors, and unknown tools. Dispatch never re-raises. This gives batch callers partial-result semantics by default; the alternative (some calls succeed, one raises, you get an exception with no info about the others) is hostile to agent code.

3. **Cycle aborts on empty Producer** — \`CycleAbortedError\` distinguishes "Producer had nothing to say" from "Controller decided we have enough." Separate failure modes need separate signals; conflating them masks bugs.

4. **\`run_cycle\` and \`stream_cycle\` are duplicated, not one wrapping the other** — Python doesn't let an async generator cleanly yield from a non-generator coroutine without a queue. The two paths are simple enough that duplication beats the abstraction. Tested independently.

5. **Skill is frozen** (\`ConfigDict(frozen=True)\`). Once loaded a skill cannot be mutated, only replaced via \`register(override=True)\`. Prevents subtle "agent mutated a shared skill" bugs.

6. **Concurrency-safe tools run via \`asyncio.gather\`; unsafe tools run sequentially.** Tools self-report \`is_concurrency_safe\`; the scheduler trusts them. Order in the result list mirrors submission order regardless of which queue ran the call.

7. **Skill keyword router is a deliberate baseline** — sums word matches in description + when_to_use, length-filtered to avoid noise. An embedding-based router can replace it without changing the API.

## Test

51 unit tests pass:

\`\`\`
backend/tests/unit/agents/framework/
├── test_types.py    # 5 tests
├── test_skills.py   # 14 tests (including frontmatter edge cases)
├── test_tools.py    # 13 tests (including parallelism wall-clock check)
└── test_cycle.py    # 9 tests (including stream variant)
\`\`\`

\`\`\`
$ uv run pytest tests/unit -m unit
...
51 passed, 1 deselected in 3.42s
\`\`\`

Notable test coverage:

author: arpitjain099
body:
Seven read-only CI workflows currently run with no `permissions:` declared. All do checkout + maven / native-image / sonar / linkage-check / upload-artifact. None push, comment, or call write APIs.

GITHUB_TOKEN usages:

- `NativeTests`: passed to `actions/setup-java` as a `github-token` (read for releases lookups)
- `compatibilityCheck`: passed to `softprops/turnstyle` to wait for sibling workflow status (read)
- `sonar`: passed for PR-metadata lookup (read)

`contents: read` is the right minimum for all seven.

Two workflows are intentionally **not** in this PR because they need very different scopes:

- `codeql-analysis.yml` — needs `security-events: write` for SARIF upload
- `renovate.yml` — needs `contents: write` + `pull-requests: write` for branch push + PR creation

Those deserve their own focused PRs.

author: therahul-yo
body:
Adds superton/puller/ package (10 modules, ~900 LOC) that replicates webpull's full feature set in pure Python:

  superton/puller/
  ├── __init__.py       Public API: Page, pull_url, pull_site
  ├── main.py           Orchestrator: single-page + full-site async generators
  ├── discovery.py      URL discovery: sitemap.xml, robots.txt, nav extraction,
  │                     JS bundle route parsing, BFS crawl, SPA hash-router
  ├── pool.py           asyncio.Semaphore-based worker pool (bounded concurrency)
  ├── worker.py         Per-URL fetch → optional Playwright render → extract
  ├── extractor.py      trafilatura content extraction (Defuddle equivalent)
  ├── detect.py         SPA shell detection heuristic
  ├── routes.py         JS bundle route scraping (path:/to:/href: patterns)
  ├── renderer.py       Optional Playwright Chromium wrapper (gated on [web])
  └── ua.py             User-agent rotation

CLI integration:
  * `superton add <url>` — single-page web ingest (detects http(s)://)
  * `superton pull <url>` — full site crawl with --max, --wing, --room, --render-js, --concurrency flags. Streams pages directly into Memory as drawers (no temp files).

Dependencies:
  * trafilatura>=1.12.0, beautifulsoup4>=4.12.0, lxml>=5.0.0 added to core deps (needed for content extraction).
  * playwright>=1.40.0 added as optional [web] extra for SPA rendering.

Feature parity with webpull:
  ✓ Sitemap.xml + sitemap index recursion
  ✓ robots.txt Sitemap: line parsing
  ✓ Nav-selector link extraction (nav, aside, sidebar, toc, menu)
  ✓ BFS crawl fallback with same-domain + scope filtering
  ✓ SPA detection (empty body + root div + framework signals)
  ✓ Hash-router discovery via Playwright render
  ✓ JS bundle route extraction (path:/to:/href: regex)
  ✓ Parallel fetch with configurable concurrency
  ✓ User-agent rotation
  ✓ Content extraction with fallback chain
  ✓ YAML frontmatter (title + url)
  ✗ Bun Worker threads (replaced by asyncio — same perf, simpler)
  ✗ Filesystem write (replaced by direct Memory.add — better for SuperTon)

body:
This pull request introduces a polymorphic "likes" system supporting likes on posts, comments, and replies. It adds a new `likes` table with appropriate schema, service, and API endpoints, and integrates like counts and user-like status into comment responses. The implementation ensures efficient batched queries for like data and avoids circular dependencies through careful module design.

**Likes system:**

* Added a new `Like` model and `LikeTargetType` enum to the Prisma schema, supporting likes on posts, comments, and replies, with indices and unique constraints for efficient lookups.
* Created a corresponding migration to add the `likes` table and indices, and set up foreign key constraints.
* Updated the `User` model to include a relation to `Like`.

**API and module integration:**

* Implemented the `LikesModule`, including `LikesService` and `LikesController`, with endpoints for liking, unliking, and listing likers for a target (post, comment, or reply). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-81493a6e9bbd0c9f6f0b34e3dd8bf92e6fdd07a6ca604853fda1dd18840b551fR1-R66) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6a84d264985023a229112bcc7eafebec0048844eaef87f1a96d3dfc1ca4562c9R1-R18)
* Integrated `LikesModule` into the main app and `CommentsModule`, ensuring like counts and user-like status are populated on comment and reply reads. **Comment response enhancements:**

author: shinpr
body:
## Summary

Two related daemon reliability fixes, one bug uncovered while shipping the other:

1. **Retry transient git/gh failures (`Retry transient git/gh failures in daemon`)** — Wrap six daemon git/gh call sites in a shared internal retry helper (5 retries, exponential backoff 1s/2s/4s/8s/16s, ±25% jitter, context-aware). Sites covered: workspace `git fetch origin <base>`, accepted-PR `git push -u origin HEAD`, `gh pr create`, the post-create PR-author `gh api` lookup, PR state polling for worktree cleanup, and PR comment listing. `vcs.PostPRComment` is intentionally left one-shot because POSTing a comment is non-idempotent. No new CLI flag, env var, profile/task YAML field, or executor/supervisor schema is added.

2. **Preserve porcelain leading space in `gitOutput` (`Preserve porcelain leading space in gitOutput`)** — `workspace.gitOutput` was applying `bytes.TrimSpace` to all captured git stdout, which stripped the leading space at column 0 of `git status --porcelain` for the first unstaged entry. The downstream `parsePorcelainPaths` reads the path at byte offset 3, so the missing space chopped the first character of the first changed file when handing it to `git add` during finalize (e.g. `CHANGELOG.md` → `HANGELOG.md`). `gitOutput` now strips only the trailing newline. Pinned with a regression test in `internal/workspace/worktree_test.go`.

The porcelain bug was the actual cause of recent daemon `git add failed: exit status 128` failures during accepted-task finalize.

## Test plan

- [x] `gofmt` (galley-dev required check)
- [x] `go test ./...` (all packages pass, including the new regression test)
- [x] `go build ./cmd/galley`
- [x] `go run ./cmd/galley schema check`
- [x] `go run ./cmd/galley task validate examples/afk-task.yaml`
- [x] `go run ./cmd/galley profile validate --kind quality examples/quality-default.yaml`
- [x] `go run ./cmd/galley profile validate --kind environment examples/environment-local.yaml`
- [x] `python3 -m json.tool` on all nine listed JSON sources

author: stevejb-ctrl
body:
> Steve: "What about when you click 'Ready for Qx'. This sits here for a while in a state saying 'Starting'. Does the loading pulse show then?"

It didn't — that button uses **SFButton** (the SF-design-system pill button), not the legacy \`Button\` that got the PulseDot in PR #97. SFButton had no \`loading\` prop; call sites just swapped text ("Starting…" instead of "Ready for Q1") and disabled the button. Visually, nothing said "loading" except the text.

## Changes

**SFButton gets a \`loading\` prop:**
- When true, the leading \`icon\` slot is replaced with a brand \`<PulseDot>\`, sized to the button (sm/md size → sm pulse; lg size → md pulse).
- Implicitly disables the button (saves call sites from \`disabled={... || loading}\` boilerplate).
- Call sites that were doing the text-swap pattern stay unchanged — both the pulse AND the "Starting…" text now coexist for double-modality feedback.

**Wired on the two visible pending-state buttons in LineupPicker** (the pre-game lineup screen):
- "Save plan & exit" → "Saving…" with pulse
- "Ready for Q1" → "Starting…" with pulse. The chevron-right trailing icon is dropped during load so the row reads cleanly as just \`[pulse] Starting…\`.

Other SFButton call sites with disabled-during-pending patterns can opt into the pulse the same way — single prop addition each.

## What this fixes

The \`Ready for Q1 → Starting…\` gap on the lineup picker now shows the alarm-orange pulse alongside the text. No more "did my tap register?" doubt.
