author: fallimic
body:
## Summary

Fixes #23120 — every example in the `pulumi api` / `pulumi api describe` help output now resolves against the live Pulumi Cloud OpenAPI spec.

The original issue called out one broken example (`ListStacks --paginate | jq '.stacks[].name'`). A follow-up audit comment on the issue surfaced five more bogus operation IDs in the same help block. This PR fixes all of them in one pass:

| Help example                         | Old (broken)                                              | New (resolves)                                                          |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| describe-by-id                       | `pulumi api describe CreateStackTag`                      | `pulumi api describe AddStackTag`                                       |
| describe-by-path with `--method`     | `/api/orgs/{orgName}/members --method=POST` (path is GET-only) | `/api/stacks/{orgName}/{projectName}/{stackName}/tags --method=POST` |
| describe `requestBody.jsonSchema`    | `describe CreateStackTag`                                 | `describe AddStackTag`                                                  |
| call-by-id (context-resolved)        | `ListOrgMembers`                                          | `ListOrganizationMembers`                                               |
| POST body fields                     | `CreateStackTag -F … -F name=env -F value=prod`           | `AddStackTag -F … -F name=env -F value=prod`                            |
| JSON array literal                   | `AddTeamMembers … -F 'members=[…]'` (no equivalent op)    | `CreateStack … -F 'teams=["platform","sre"]'`                           |
| `--body`                             | `UpdateStack … --body '{"description":…}'` (no such op)   | `UpdateStackTags … --body '{"env":"production",…}'`                     |
| `--input` (file + stdin)             | `UpdateStackTag --input ./tag.json` (missing `tagName`)   | adds the required `-F tagName=env` so the call is copy-pasteable        |
| `--paginate` + jq                    | `ListStacks --paginate \| jq '.stacks[].name'`            | `ListUserStacks --paginate \| jq '.stacks[].stackName'`                 |
| `--dry-run`                          | `CreateStackTag -F orgName=acme --dry-run`                | `AddStackTag -F orgName=acme --dry-run`                                 |
| `Long:` docstring on `pulumi api`    | mentions `ListOrgMembers`                                 | mentions `ListOrganizationMembers`                                      |

`ListAccounts`, `GetStack`, `CreateStack`, `UpdateStackTag`, `AddStackTag`, `UpdateStackTags`, `ListUserStacks`, `ListOrganizationMembers`, and `GetCurrentUser` (for the `/api/user` examples) were confirmed against the cached spec at `~/.pulumi/cloud-api-cache/api.pulumi.com/spec.json`. The `.githubLogin` field referenced by the jq example exists on the `User` schema.

The `AddTeamMembers` example had no direct replacement in the spec (the only way to add team members is `UpdateTeam` one at a time), so I rewrote the example as `CreateStack -F 'teams=[…]'` — which still demonstrates passing a JSON array literal via `-F`.

## Test plan

Each fixed example was verified by building the CLI from this branch and running it with `--dry-run` (and `describe` for the describe examples) against the cached spec; every command now resolves to a valid `method + path + body` plan instead of erroring with `pulumi.cloud_api.no_match`. The `describe`-by-path with `--method=POST` example now maps to `AddStackTag`.

- [ ] Added appropriate unit tests - For all changes
- [ ] Added a test in `pkg/engine/lifecycletest` - For all engine/protocol changes
- [ ] Added a conformance test in `pkg/testing/pulumi-test-language` - For language protocol changes
- [ ] Added a golden test in `pkg/backend/display` - For changes to the output renderers

Help text isn't covered by a golden test today, so this change is verified by running the binary rather than by a unit test.

## Validation

- [x] `make lint` — clean
- [x] `make format` — clean
- [x] `go test ./cmd/pulumi/cloud/...` — pass
- [ ] `make test_fast` — not run (no behavioural code changed; only the help-text string literals)
- [ ] `make tidy_fix` — not run (no `go.mod` changes)
- [ ] Relevant SDK tests pass (if SDK changes)
- [ ] `make check_proto` — clean (if proto changes)

## Changelog

- [x] Changelog entry added: `changelog/pending/20260513--cli-cloud--fix-pulumi-api-help-examples-to-use-real-operation-ids.yaml`.

## Risk

Help-text only. No runtime behaviour changes; no public API or CLI surface changes. Worst case is a docstring typo, which is what this PR is fixing.

author: jdev-02
body:
Backs the mechanical-advantage claim in the Pliers documentation and extends Shovel with the same lever-physics vocabulary, reusing SUMO's existing fulcrum / lever / Rotating case roles rather than introducing new mechanics terms.

Pliers (Objects.kif):

- When Pliers are the instrument of any IntentionalProcess, a Rotating sub-event exists in which the Pliers' Hinge is the fulcrum and the Pliers themselves are the lever. The Hinge-as-component requirement was already in place from PR #558; this PR binds it to the Rotating case roles that the Pliers doc string asserts. The relevant sentence in the existing documentation is "function by applying mechanical advantage through the pivot point to multiply the user's grip strength," which was previously a free-floating claim and is now grounded in fulcrum and lever for any downstream proof that needs to derive mechanical-advantage behavior from Pliers being the instrument of a process.

Shovel (Objects.kif):

- When a Shovel is the instrument of a Digging, a Rotating sub-event exists in which the Shovel's Handle is the lever. The Handle-as-part requirement was already in place from PR #556; this PR binds it to the Rotating case role.

Out of scope for this PR, queued for the Backpack-ergonomics follow-on:

- The fulcrum on a Shovel is the user's lower grip point along the shaft, which is not yet a named term in SUMO. Naming the fulcrum cleanly requires the same kind of body-grip-region term (something like UpperBack, LumbarRegion, or a generic GripPoint) that the queued Backpack ergonomics PR needs anyway. Bundling those together keeps the human-body axioms in one place rather than scattered across hand-tool PRs.
- ShovelHead per the queued Tool Anatomy section, which will let the Shovel's Rotating event also have a load case role pointing at the blade end.

author: jpr5
body:
## Summary

- **Record model in fixture match criteria** for all requests (not just fal.ai), preventing fixture collisions when apps make multiple LLM calls with the same user message but different models
- **Date-suffix normalization** strips version dates from model names (e.g., `claude-opus-4-20250514` → `claude-opus-4`) so fixtures survive provider version bumps
- **Dash+digit boundary matching** in the router: `claude-opus-4` matches `claude-opus-4-20250514` but `gpt-4` does NOT match `gpt-4o` and `gpt-4o` does NOT match `gpt-4o-mini`
- **Drift detection metadata** records `systemHash` and `toolsHash` (8-char SHA-256) alongside fixtures for detecting prompt/tool changes since recording
- **`recordFullModelVersion`** config option and CLI flag to disable normalization
- **Documentation** updates for recording behavior, config reference, and CLI

## Why

Issue #185 — when an app triggers multiple distinct LLM calls from a single user message (e.g., Opus+tools for chat, Haiku for title gen, Haiku for suggestions), recorded fixtures collide because `buildFixtureMatch()` only keyed on `userMessage`/`turnIndex`/`hasToolResult`. Adding `model` to match criteria disambiguates the calls.

## Test plan

- [ ] `normalizeModelName` strips dates correctly across all provider formats
- [ ] Router dash+digit boundary: `gpt-4` ✗ `gpt-4o`, `gpt-4o` ✗ `gpt-4o-mini`, `claude-opus-4` ✓ `claude-opus-4-20250514`
- [ ] Recorder writes normalized model + metadata to fixture files
- [ ] `recordFullModelVersion: true` preserves full model string
- [ ] Old fixtures without model field still match (backwards compatible)
- [ ] Integration test: 3 distinct LLM calls produce distinguishable fixtures

Closes #185

author: armelatwork
body:
## What
Two persistent bottom banners for Google Drive storage issues:
- **90%+ warning** — shown once per session; dismissed stays gone until next app launch
- **Full (exceeded)** — shown on every failed push or poll; re-appears after dismiss if the next sync also fails

## How
Replaced `driveQuotaExceededProvider` (bool) with `DriveStorageAlert`, a value object carrying `severity`, `usagePercent`, and `ownerName`.

**`ownerName` is the sharing hook:** it's `null` for the current user (message says "Your Drive…"). When note-sharing is added, pass the folder owner's display name and the message adapts automatically — no refactor needed.

**90% warning** — `_checkStorageQuota()` calls `drive.about.get($fields: storageQuota)` each poll cycle. Skipped for unlimited accounts (Workspace, where `limit` is null). Sets `_warningShownThisSession = true` on first trigger so it never fires again in the same session.

**Exceeded** — detected reactively in the `_run()` catch blocks of `NotesNotifier` and `FoldersNotifier`, and in `_pollCycle()`. Sets `DriveStorageAlert(severity: exceeded)` which re-shows on every failed sync.

**Messages:**
- Warning: "Your Google Drive storage is 92% full. Free up space to avoid sync interruptions."
- Exceeded: "Your Google Drive storage is full. Free up space to continue syncing."
- Future shared note, owner full: "[Name]'s Google Drive storage is full. Ask them to free up space."

## Testing
- `flutter analyze` — no issues
- To trigger warning: use an account near quota; banner appears within the next poll cycle (5 s)
- To trigger exceeded: fill Drive completely and save a note

## Security
No secrets committed. Error strings logged at WARN without sensitive data.

Same story as ChangeControlAudit — three parallel API calls fire on
mount, resolve asynchronously, and dump into setState with no one
checking whether the component is still alive. The useEffect had no
cleanup, so any in-flight fetch that landed after navigation would
update a component that was already gone.

Pulled the .json() parsing ahead of the cancelledRef guard so all
async work finishes before we check, then added the same guard in
catch and finally. The ref resets on mount and flips on unmount —
same pattern we've used in three other compliance dashboards now.

author: alan747271363-art
body:
Refs #1949 ## Summary - add panic recovery to TON outbound processing, matching the pattern used by EVM/BTC/Solana signers - add panic recovery to Sui ProcessCCTX while returning an error to the caller - keep outbound active markers cleared after recovered panics - add regression coverage for panic recovery paths ## Tests - docker run --rm -v "${repo}:/workspace" -v zeta-go-cache:/go/pkg/mod --workdir /workspace golang:1.23 sh -c "go test -tags pebbledb,ledger,test ./zetaclient/chains/ton/signer" - docker run --rm -v "${repo}:/workspace" -v zeta-go-cache:/go/pkg/mod --workdir /workspace golang:1.23 sh -c "go test -tags pebbledb,ledger,test ./zetaclient/chains/sui/signer"

Greptile Summary

This PR adds panic recovery to the TON `TryProcessOutbound` and Sui `ProcessCCTX` signers, matching the pattern already used by EVM and Solana signers, and ensures the outbound active marker is always cleared after a recovered panic. - **TON** (`signer.go`): Wraps the existing `defer s.MarkOutbound(outboundID, false)` into an anonymous function that additionally calls `recover()` and logs the panic with a stack trace; the function returns nothing so the panic is silently swallowed after logging. - **Sui** (`signer.go`): Converts `ProcessCCTX` to use a named return `err`, adds the same recovery pattern, and sets `err` to a descriptive error value on panic so callers see a non-nil error instead of a silent void. - Both changes include regression tests that verify the active marker is cleared and (for Sui) that a descriptive error is returned.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge — the changes are additive panic recovery wrappers that don't alter any business logic. The core change is low-risk: wrap existing function bodies in a deferred recovery that clears the active marker and logs/returns the panic. The debug.Stack() field captured after recover() will reflect the deferred function's stack rather than the actual panic site, reducing its diagnostic value — but this is a pre-existing pattern in the EVM signer. The implementation, named-return handling in Sui, and test coverage are all correct. No files require special attention; the production signer files are the most significant changes and look correct.

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | zetaclient/chains/sui/signer/signer.go | Adds panic recovery to ProcessCCTX using a named return err and a single defer that clears the active marker then calls recover(); matches EVM/Solana pattern but debug.Stack() is captured after recover, so the logged stack won't show the panic site | | zetaclient/chains/ton/signer/signer.go | Adds panic recovery to TryProcessOutbound via the same defer pattern; correct fire-and-forget semantics (void return), stack trace has same post-recover capture limitation | | zetaclient/chains/sui/signer/signer_test.go | Adds ProcessCCTX recovers panic sub-test: triggers nil-pointer panic via InboundParams = nil, asserts error contains expected message and active marker is cleared | | zetaclient/chains/ton/signer/signer_test.go | Adds TestSigner_TryProcessOutboundRecoversPanic: uses require.NotPanics to verify recovery and checks IsOutboundActive is false after the call |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Orchestrator participant TON_Sui_Signer participant processOutbound Orchestrator->>TON_Sui_Signer: TryProcessOutbound / ProcessCCTX TON_Sui_Signer->>TON_Sui_Signer: MarkOutbound(id, true) TON_Sui_Signer->>TON_Sui_Signer: register defer [MarkOutbound(false) + recover()] TON_Sui_Signer->>processOutbound: call processOutbound / internal logic alt normal execution processOutbound-->>TON_Sui_Signer: outcome, err TON_Sui_Signer->>TON_Sui_Signer: defer runs: MarkOutbound(id, false) TON_Sui_Signer->>TON_Sui_Signer: recover() nil (no panic) TON_Sui_Signer-->>Orchestrator: return (nil or error) else panic occurs processOutbound--xTON_Sui_Signer: panic! TON_Sui_Signer->>TON_Sui_Signer: defer runs: MarkOutbound(id, false) TON_Sui_Signer->>TON_Sui_Signer: recover() panic value TON_Sui_Signer->>TON_Sui_Signer: log error + stack_trace Note over TON_Sui_Signer: Sui: set named return err / TON: void (log only) TON_Sui_Signer-->>Orchestrator: return (Sui: error / TON: void) end ```
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown Fix the following 1 code review issue. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 1 zetaclient/chains/sui/signer/signer.go:110 **`debug.Stack()` called after `recover()` — panic site stack is lost** Once `recover()` is called in a deferred function the Go runtime considers the panic resolved and unwinds the call stack to the deferred function's frame. Any subsequent call to `debug.Stack()` returns the current (deferred) goroutine stack, not the stack at the panic origin. The logged `stack_trace` field will point to the defer wrapper rather than the line that panicked, making post-incident analysis significantly harder. The same pattern exists in the EVM signer (`evm/signer/signer.go:276`), so this is a pre-existing footgun being replicated here. Consider capturing the stack trace before `recover()` or accepting that the field's value has limited diagnostic use. `````
Reviews (1): Last reviewed commit: ["fix(zetaclient): recover ton and sui sig..."](https://github.com/zeta-chain/node/commit/2816956a715e69d645f4b1ffa6e575d0ae8e87b2) | [Re-trigger Greptile](https://app.greptile.com/api/retrigger?id=31994102) > Greptile also left **1 inline comment** on this PR. ## Summary by CodeRabbit ## Release Notes * **Bug Fixes** * Improved error handling in Sui and TON chain transaction processors with robust recovery mechanisms that capture and log detailed diagnostic information when unexpected errors occur during processing, ensuring proper cleanup and maintaining system stability. * **Tests** * Added comprehensive test coverage for error recovery scenarios in transaction processing workflows across Sui and TON blockchain chains. author: fuddlesworth
body:
## Summary

Fixes a brief white BSP OSD card flashing on the SDDM greeter after logout.

**Root cause** (after several iterations through wrong layers): between user logout and SDDM handoff, systemd was respawning the daemon into a transient "phantom Plasma" state — a stray `kwin_wayland` from a fallback session-restore mechanism briefly publishes a fresh `wayland-N` socket inside the still-dying `user@.service`, and `Restart=on-failure` schedules a daemon retry after Qt's wayland QPA aborts on the original session's vanished `wl_display`. The phantom daemon runs long enough to fire startup welcome OSDs against an output about to be unbound by the SDDM compositor switch.

**The signal that uniquely catches this**: `plasma-workspace.target.ActiveState` on the user-bus systemd. The target is only flipped to `active` by `startplasma-wayland`'s orchestration *after* SDDM hands off; the phantom has no startplasma leader, so the target stays `inactive`. logind's `User.State` stays `active` whenever `user@.service` is up (so it can't distinguish phantom from real), `GetSessionByPID` returns "no session" for any `systemd --user`-spawned process (so it suppresses legitimate restarts too), and the wayland-socket existence probe passes during the phantom (stray kwin publishes one).

## Defense in depth (six layers)

1. **`src/daemon/main.cpp`** — pre-`QGuiApplication` Wayland-socket probe. If `$WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is set but the socket at `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/$WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is missing, `return 0` cleanly. Stops the trivial "wayland already gone" respawn loop.
2. **`Daemon::queryPlasmaWorkspaceState()`** — at `start()` time, query systemd's user bus for `plasma-workspace.target.ActiveState`. Cache in `m_plasmaWorkspaceActive`. Subscribe to `PropertiesChanged` so a running daemon also catches mid-flight transitions out of active. Fail-open if systemd's user bus is unreachable (non-systemd / headless).
3. **`Daemon::start()` `QGuiApplication::aboutToQuit` hook** — flips `m_shuttingDown` on SIGTERM so any in-flight or deferred OSD bails.
4. **`Daemon::stop()`** — sets `m_shuttingDown = true` at the top, before the `m_running` gate, so programmatic stops also suppress.
5. **`screenRemoved` handler** (`src/daemon/daemon/start.cpp`) — bumps a 1-second `m_screensSettlingUntil` deadline. KWin tearing down outputs at logout fires cascading `screenRemoved` → `virtualScreensChanged` → `layoutApplied` → `showLayoutOsdDeferred`; the cooldown lets that drain. Also damps monitor hot-unplug churn.
6. **`Daemon::shouldSuppressOsd()`** (`src/daemon/daemon/osd.cpp`) — single helper gating every OSD entry point. Returns true on any of `m_shuttingDown`, `!m_plasmaWorkspaceActive`, or `now < m_screensSettlingUntil`.

Plus **`plasmazones.service.in`**: `RestartPreventExitStatus=SIGABRT`. Qt's `qFatal` is "unrecoverable, do not retry" — systemd's blind `Restart=on-failure` was fighting that contract.

## Test plan

- [x] Real session start: welcome OSDs fire normally (verified by user; journal shows `plasma-workspace.target ActiveState at startup: "active"`).
- [x] `systemctl --user restart plasmazones`: welcome OSDs fire normally (regression check for an earlier flawed `GetSessionByPID` approach that broke this).
- [x] Logout → SDDM: no white BSP OSD on the login screen (verified by user — primary symptom is gone).
- [ ] Monitor hot-unplug while OSD visible: existing OSD finishes gracefully, no new OSDs fire for ~1 s after (`m_screensSettlingUntil` cooldown).
- [ ] Non-Plasma host (sway, GNOME): fail-open path leaves welcome OSDs enabled. Daemon doesn't crash on missing `plasma-workspace.target`.

author: xlanstar
body:
## Summary

Adds a new `victorialogs` webhook mode for shipping logs to VictoriaLogs.

- Sends logs to VictoriaLogs' `/insert/jsonline` ingestion endpoint
- Built on the existing JSON reconstructor with a couple of added fields
- README updated with setup instructions, `_stream_fields` usage, and basic-auth URL example

[VictoriaLogs documentation](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victorialogs/data-ingestion/)

## Configuration

```env
LOCOMOTIVE_WEBHOOK_MODE=victorialogs
LOCOMOTIVE_WEBHOOK_URL=https://{VICTORIALOGS_HOSTNAME}/insert/jsonline
```

  Optionally declare stream fields:
```env
LOCOMOTIVE_WEBHOOK_URL=https://{VICTORIALOGS_HOSTNAME}/insert/jsonline?_stream_fields=_metadata.service_name,_metadata.environment_name
```

author: saliprandi
body:
### 🎨 Palette: Improve contact form feedback and clean up navbar accessibility

#### 💡 What
- **`Contacto.astro`**: Converted a `div`-based form structure into a semantic `<form>` element. Added `required` attributes to the name and phone fields. Updated the client-side script to provide visual feedback ("Redirigiendo...") on the submit button.
- **`Nav.astro`**: Removed a duplicate logo image within the brand link. Consolidated three identical mobile menu buttons into a single accessible button with appropriate `aria-controls` and `aria-expanded` attributes.

#### 🎯 Why
- **Accessibility**: Semantic forms are better for screen readers and enable native browser features like Enter-to-submit. Consolidating the mobile menu ensures a cleaner document structure and better keyboard navigation.
- **UX**: Providing immediate visual feedback after clicking "Enviar" prevents double-submissions and assures the user that their action was registered.
- **Maintainability**: Removing duplicate code and elements reduces the DOM payload and makes the components easier to maintain.

#### ♿ Accessibility
- Added native HTML5 validation.
- Improved ARIA attributes for the mobile menu.
- Ensured keyboard submittability for the contact form.

#### 🧪 Testing
- Verified locally with `pnpm build`.
- Automated verification using Playwright scripts to confirm:
  - Form validation triggers for empty required fields.
  - Button text changes to "Redirigiendo..." upon valid submission.
  - Navbar contains only one logo image and one mobile menu button.
- Manually checked keyboard navigation (Tab and Enter keys).

author: sw-factory-automations
body:
Closes #1076

## What

Adds 5 new E2E tests to `e2e/import-export.spec.ts` (2 → 7 total), covering edge cases that were previously untested:

1. **Unsupported elements** — imports markdown with HTML tags, footnotes, and HTML tables; verifies graceful handling (content preserved as text, no JS errors)
2. **Empty file** — imports an empty `.md` file; verifies a page is created with empty content and the editor is usable
3. **Code block special characters** — exports a page with code containing backticks, angle brackets, and ampersands; verifies the markdown has properly fenced code blocks
4. **Nested lists** — exports a page with 3 levels of bullet list nesting; verifies indentation is preserved in the markdown output
5. **Round-trip** — creates content, exports it, imports the exported file, and verifies the content matches

## How

All tests extend the existing `import-export.spec.ts` file and follow the same patterns:
- Import tests use `page.setInputFiles()` on the hidden file input
- Export tests intercept the download event and read the file content
- The round-trip test combines both: export via download interception, then import the downloaded buffer

## Testing

- `pnpm lint` — 0 errors
- `pnpm typecheck` — clean
- `pnpm test` — 1877 tests pass (139 files)
- `pnpm test:e2e --grep "import and export"` — all 7 tests pass (auth flakiness on parallel runs resolves with CI retries)
- Updated `.agents/quality.md` with new test counts (381 → 386 E2E tests)

author: dschmura
body:
## Summary

Markdowndocs v0.6.0 (released today) adds an `audience:` frontmatter key for whole-document mode targeting. This is the groundwork PR:

- `Gemfile` / `Gemfile.lock` bumped from `~> 0.5.0` to `~> 0.6.0`
- All 11 existing docs in [app/docs/](app/docs/) now carry `audience: [guide, technical]`

The explicit declaration is a **behavioral no-op** (the gem defaults to all configured modes when `audience:` is absent), but locks in three things:

1. **Documentor clarity** — new docs are written next to existing docs that already declare audience, making the decision intentional rather than implicit
2. **Future audience-narrowing** (e.g., scoping `extending.md` to technical only) is a one-line edit, not a frontmatter-add + scope-change pair
3. **PR 4** (the actual notification docs) becomes the first VISIBLE effect of the mode switcher — guide users see `notifications.md`, technical users see `notifications-technical.md`, and existing context docs remain visible in both

## Test plan

- [x] `spec/system/docs_spec.rb` — all rendering checks pass with new gem + audience frontmatter
- [x] `spec/system/docs_mode_persistence_spec.rb` (PR #103) — mode persistence still works end-to-end after the gem bump
- [x] Full suite: **1780/0/2** — no test-count change (explicit audience is behavior-identical to the previous implicit default)

## What's next

After this lands, **PR 4** writes `notifications.md` (`audience: guide`) and `notifications-technical.md` (`audience: technical`), and adds both to the `Features` category in the initializer.

author: stupideity
body:
## Summary

Second-order fix for ENG-96. The first dispatch halted on a protocol violation that
turned out to be an agent-emitted literal `$PIPELINE_DISPATCH_ID` poisoning the
strict-id verdict filter (fixed in PR #90). The retry — using a fresh dispatch_id
on the same branch — halted again, this time at the implement-stage scope-check:

> `Pipeline: implementing stage halted — scope-check rc=2 (likely plan not found or File Structure unparseable)`

The agent's TDD evidence said scope was clean, the plan's File Structure section
*did* list every touched file — but `bin/scope-check.sh::extract_scope_section`'s
awk pattern matched only `^(##|###)[[:space:]]+[Ff]ile [Ss]tructure`, and the plan's
heading was `## 3. File Structure` (the plan-agent template's numbered-H2 style).
The `3. ` between `## ` and `File` killed the match → empty extract → `exit 2`.

Two of 41 in-flight plans used this shape (ENG-24 + ENG-96). The fix is to
tolerate the optional `N. ` prefix on the heading regex; switching to a different
tool (grep, sed) would lose the cross-line depth-comparison logic that lets
`### File Structure` correctly keep `#### Subsection` inside it.

## Fixes

### (A) Heading regex widening — `bin/scope-check.sh:64`

```diff
-    /^(##|###)[[:space:]]+[Ff]ile [Ss]tructure/ { depth=length($1); in_fs=1; next }
+    /^(##|###)[[:space:]]+([0-9]+\.[[:space:]]+)?[Ff]ile [Ss]tructure/ {
+      depth=length($1); in_fs=1; next
+    }
```

Now accepts: `## File Structure`, `### File Structure`, `## File structure`,
`## 3. File Structure`, `### 12. File Structure`.

### (B) Diagnostics split — `bin/scope-check.sh` + `bin/run-stage.sh`

Three distinct rc=2 stderr messages:

1. `scope-check: plan not found for ENG-N (no docs/plans/*.md with frontmatter linear: ENG-N)`
2. `scope-check: plan=<path>: File Structure section missing or empty (expected a '## File Structure' or '### File Structure' heading)`
3. `scope-check: plan=<path>: File Structure section parsed but contains no file or directory tokens`

And `run-stage.sh`'s halt-reason text now passes the captured scope-check log line
through verbatim (stripping the timestamp prefix) instead of the hardcoded
`likely plan not found or File Structure unparseable` string that made ENG-96
undiagnosable from Linear.

## Out of scope

- **Plan-agent template tightening.** A separate decision to standardize on
  unnumbered `## File Structure` (36/41 plans already use this) would prevent
  the next regression; deferred to keep this PR a parser fix.
- **The `(no tokens parsed)` rc=2 branch** (line ~199–202) is rare in practice
  (a plan with a File Structure heading but no `path/with/.ext` or `dir/` tokens)
  and is the one branch where the pre-fix message was already accurate; only
  prefixed it with the plan path for symmetry.

## Test plan

- [x] `bash bin/scope-check-test.sh` — 23/23 pass (5 new cases: case-7 × 3 numbered shapes, case-8a plan-not-found, case-8b missing-section)
- [x] `bash .githooks/pre-commit` — 34/34 pass (+3 skipped known-broken) in 94s
- [x] Recovery path for ENG-96 after this lands: `bash bin/pipeline.sh decide ENG-96 --action continue` — clears halt, re-runs scope-check against the same plan, passes.

author: samirthini11
body: ## Summary Adds the first Flutter app of the platform: **Pro-Enroll**, the self-enrollment app used by service professionals (AC mechanic, plumber, RO technician, fridge / washing-machine / car / bike mechanic, electrician). Targets Pondicherry, Karaikal and nearby Tamil Nadu, per the docs added in PR #1. The app lives at `apps/pro_enroll_app/`. The customer-side **Pro-User** app will be a sibling folder, added in a separate PR. ## Brand identity The app ships with the **PRO ENROLL** launcher icon (deep blue gradient + white PRO wordmark + clipboard with checkmark + upward growth arrow). [App icon](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-afdbc7fb-e5a9-414e-b89a-836fa12d08c4/artifacts?path=%2Fworkspace%2Fapps%2Fpro_enroll_app%2Fassets%2Fbranding%2Fapp_icon_1024.png) - Android legacy launcher (`ic_launcher.png`) in all 5 mipmap densities. - Android **adaptive launcher** (API 26+) with the brand gradient as the XML background and an alpha-masked foreground that sits inside the safe zone. - iOS `AppIcon.appiconset` with all 15 slots regenerated (20–1024 px). - Web favicon + PWA icons (192, 512, maskable variants). - The same 1024 master is reused inside the app on the splash and the auth-landing hero card so the brand experience is consistent end-to-end. ## Auth & onboarding flow After the splash, the user lands on a single **Auth Landing** screen with two clear actions: 1. **Sign in** — filled button. Existing pros enter their phone, get an OTP, and are taken straight to the home shell. 2. **Create account · Enroll as a Pro** — outlined button. New pros run the full enrollment wizard. OTP is wired to **Firebase Authentication (Phone provider)** on Android. ## Implemented flows - Splash with auto-redirect (1.1s) - Phone + OTP login (real Firebase OTP on Android; in-memory mock on web / iOS until those configs are added) - Aadhaar OTP screen with auto-spaced `1234 5678 9012` formatting - Selfie liveness, supporting documents, pending-review screen with simulated approval - Home shell with bottom-nav tabs: **Jobs, Earnings, Profile, Help** - Job offer detail with 60-second auto-reject timer + progress bar - Active job state machine: `accepted → on_the_way → in_progress → completed` - Profile with skills, work radius, visit fee, language toggle, UPI / bank sheet, sign-out - Earnings with today / week / month and pending / paid payouts - Help with call, WhatsApp, FAQ and Pro Academy entries ## Firebase OTP (Android) Wired up using the config supplied for project **proenroll-4ff13**, package **`pro.enroll`**: - `android/app/google-services.json` committed. - `lib/firebase_options.dart` hand-written from the same config. - `firebase_core ^3.6` + `firebase_auth ^5.3` added. - Google Services Gradle plugin applied; `applicationId` + `namespace` switched to `pro.enroll`; `MainActivity` moved to `android/app/src/main/kotlin/pro/enroll/`. - Min SDK bumped to 23 (Firebase Auth requirement). - New `FirebaseOtpService` wraps `verifyPhoneNumber` + `signInWithCredential` and handles Android instant verification. - `AuthNotifier` falls back to `MockRepository` on platforms where Firebase isn't initialised (web / iOS demo / tests). ### Console steps you still need to do once 1. **Enable the Phone provider** in *Authentication → Sign-in method*. 2. **Add your debug SHA-1** to the Android app in Firebase Console (`cd android && ./gradlew signingReport`). Re-download `google-services.json` after. 3. *Optional:* add a **test phone number** so you can test without sending real SMS. iOS / Web phone OTP is intentionally not wired yet — both fall back to the mock until you give us a `GoogleService-Info.plist` and a web Firebase config. See the *Firebase phone-OTP setup* section in `apps/pro_enroll_app/README.md`. ## Visual design - **Deep professional blue palette** — primary `#1D4ED8`, dark `#1E40AF`, light `#EFF4FF`, warm amber accents. - **Material 3** theme with carefully tuned tokens. - **Gradient hero cards** for splash, auth landing, today's earnings, profile header and the completed-job summary. - **Status pills** for active-job / offer states. - **Indian-grouped money formatting** (`₹1,85,000`). ## Responsive design (supports all mobile sizes) - `core/responsive.dart` with breakpoints (xs <360, sm <412, md <600, lg <905) and a `BuildContext` extension exposing `pageHPadding`, `pageVPadding`, `gridColumns`, `contentMaxWidth`, plus a `ContentMaxWidth` wrapper that caps content at 560dp on foldables / web while leaving phones full-width. - Category grid auto-selects **2 / 3 / 4 columns** by viewport. - Selfie circle, hero icon, fee amount text and the map placeholder scale with viewport. - Action button rows collapse to a vertical stack on widths < 280–320dp. ## Language strategy - **v1: English first.** Single source of truth so the team can iterate on copy quickly. - Tamil stays available from the language sheet on the landing footer and from **Profile → Language**. - Telugu / French will be added once translations are reviewed. ## Stack - Flutter **3.41** / Dart **3.11** (stable) - **Riverpod 2.x** for state · **go_router 14.x** for navigation - **firebase_core 3.6** + **firebase_auth 5.3** for OTP on Android - Money stored as **paise (₹ × 100)** throughout ## Quality gates ```bash $ flutter analyze No issues found! $ flutter test All tests passed! (7 tests) $ flutter build web ✓ Built build/web ``` ## Commits in this PR 1. **`feat(pro_enroll_app)`** — scaffold the app, all UI flows, mock repo, tests. 2. **`fix(mock_repository)`** — 31-bit max for `Random.nextInt`; `web/` platform files. 3. **`feat(ui)`** — professional blue theme, polished components, full responsive layer. 4. **`chore(i18n)`** — default to English. 5. **`feat(auth)`** — Sign in / Sign up landing, `AuthFlow` routing, enrollment bug fixes. 6. **`feat(auth) [Firebase]`** — Firebase Phone OTP on Android with mock fallback. 7. **`feat(branding)`** — new PRO ENROLL launcher icon for Android (legacy + adaptive) + iOS + web + PWA; same artwork on splash and auth-landing hero. ## How to run ```bash cd apps/pro_enroll_app flutter pub get flutter run # real OTP on Android flutter run -d chrome # web (mock OTP — any 6 digits) ``` ## Demo shortcuts - Mock OTP (web / iOS / no-Firebase): any 6 digits; `000000` fails to show error UX. - Sign In jumps straight to the home shell with seeded sample stats. - KYC *pending review* has a **"Continue (demo: simulate approval)"** button. ## Next steps (separate PRs) 1. Wire `GoogleService-Info.plist` for iOS (and APNs auth key). 2. Replace `MockRepository` with a Dio + retrofit client. 3. Add FCM push + Crashlytics. 4. Google Maps for location and active-job screens. 5. Scaffold the **Pro-User** customer app under `apps/`. To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.

Targets `development` only.

### Adds

- command-service regression tests

### Purpose

Moves Phase 0 identity/onboarding behavior toward a canonical execution layer instead of scattered route-local side effects.

The command service becomes the official mutation boundary for:

- login-capable identity decisions
- onboarding eligibility
- invite readiness
- workspace onboarding intent
- onboarding spine execution
- traceability metadata

Policy -> Orchestrator -> Command Service -> Thin Routes

This is part of the debt-free Phase 0 rebuild before live Statewide manager onboarding/testing.

body:
## Summary

First slice of [HEL-71](https://linear.app/helloautoflow/issue/HEL-71). Establishes the per-route entitlement-gating pattern + the Jest auto-mock infrastructure that the other gated routes will share. The remaining 5 gates and the dashboard 402 UI surfacing are filed as follow-up [HEL-77](https://linear.app/helloautoflow/issue/HEL-77) because each needs its own counter-plumbing or response-filter work that would bloat this PR.

> Stacked on top of [PR #692](https://github.com/bdunk881/paperclipai/pull/692) (HEL-69) — the entitlement gate runs AFTER `requireRole(...)`, which depends on the workspace-aware request shape that HEL-69 wires up. Merge #692 first.

## What changed

- `POST /api/llm-configs/` now composes `requireEntitlement("byokAllowed")` before the handler. Workspaces on the free Explore tier and the $19 Flow tier (`byokAllowed: false`) get a 402 with the canonical entitlement_exceeded payload; Automate ($49) and Scale ($99) pass through.
- New `src/billing/__mocks__/entitlements.ts` Jest auto-mock — opt in via `jest.mock("../billing/entitlements")` and get an Automate-tier workspace by default. Tests that exercise the denial path call `entitlementStore.upsert(wsId, "explore")`.

## Tests

- New `returns 402 with entitlement_exceeded payload when BYOK is disallowed on the plan (HEL-71)` test asserts the full canonical shape:
  ```ts
  { code: "entitlement_exceeded", feature: "byokAllowed", limit: false,
    currentTier: "explore", upgradeTo: "flow" }
  ```
- All 14 llmConfig tests pass.
- Full backend suite: 1,356 tests pass. Only failures are 2 pre-existing in `src/db/sqlMigrations.test.ts`, unrelated.

## Documented follow-up — HEL-77

| Item | Why it's deferred |
|---|---|
| `agentCap` gate | needs `agentStore.countByWorkspace(...)` |
| `integrationCap` gate | needs workspace-scoped count from `integrationCredentialStore` (today it lists by userId) |
| `runsPerMonth` gate | needs current-month run counter |
| `approvalTierMax` gate | needs handler body-extract for requested tier |
| `logRetentionDays` gate | query-time filter, not route-entry gate |
| Dashboard 402 toast + Upgrade CTA | dashboard-side work, separate concern |
| `firstTierThatAllows()` correction | the current `UPGRADE_PATH` would tell Explore-tier users to upgrade to Flow, but Flow also has `byokAllowed: false`. Needs a smarter lookup against `PLAN_LIMITS`. |

author: franzwilding
body:
## Summary
This PR extends `createLoader` to support multiple module-map groups, each with its own prefix. This enables more flexible component resolution strategies where different prefixes can be routed to different module maps.

## Key Changes
- **New `LoaderGroup` interface**: Defines a group with its own `modules` and optional `prefix`
- **New `groups` option**: Added to `LoaderOptions` as a mutually exclusive alternative to the `modules`/`prefix` pair, allowing users to specify multiple groups that are tried in order
- **Group matching logic**: Implemented `matchGroup()` function that iterates through groups and returns the first whose prefix matches the component tag
- **Catch-all group support**: A group without a `prefix` acts as a catch-all and should be placed last
- **Validation**: Added error handling to ensure `groups` and `modules`/`prefix` are not mixed, and that `groups` is non-empty
- **Cache key change**: Updated caching to use the full `is` value instead of the stripped `name` to properly handle multiple groups
- **Backward compatibility**: Legacy single-group behavior (non-strict mode) is preserved when using the original `modules`/`prefix` options

## Implementation Details
- `normalizeGroups()` converts both the new `groups` format and legacy `modules`/`prefix` into a unified internal representation
- Groups are marked as "strict" when using the new `groups` option, allowing proper error handling when no prefix matches
- The legacy single-group mode remains non-strict, falling back to using the full `is` value as the component name if the prefix doesn't match
- Comprehensive test coverage added for multi-group routing, catch-all behavior, and validation

## Summary
Removes the \`Apply ECR lifecycle policies\` step from the deploy job. The policy itself stays applied at the ECR level on both repos (keep last 10 images).

## Why
ECR lifecycle policies are persistent configuration — once set, they stay until explicitly changed. The CI step was re-applying the same policy on every deploy, which (a) is a no-op API call costing CI minutes, (b) was the only reason the \`github-actions-rs-recruitment\` OIDC role needed \`ecr:PutLifecyclePolicy\`. ## Summary

PR L upgrades the PR K confirmation-preview shell into a structured, read-only **Intent Packet**. The modal now answers *"what exactly would this action mean?"* — not *"can I execute this?"*. Strictly visual; no command execution, no command-proposal object, no backend mutation.

## Six Intent Packet sections

| # | Section | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | ACTION | action label, verb class, current stage, target stage (if present), strategy id, strategy name |
| 2 | INTENT PACKET | plain-language explanation per verb (promote / demote / return / start_trading / stop_trading / initiate_backtest / refresh_backtest) |
| 3 | CURRENT SNAPSHOT | sharpe / max-DD / trade count / status word+tail / evidenceRunId / metaEvidenceLabel / metaEvidenceAt — existing `rowData` only |
| 4 | WOULD EVENTUALLY REQUIRE | copy-only enumeration: evidence gate / freshness / operator confirmation / policy lock / risk guard / event write |
| 5 | FUTURE RECORD | non-executable display string per verb (\`promotion_event\` / \`demotion_event\` / \`stage_return_event\` / \`session_start_event\` / \`session_stop_event\` / \`backtest_request_event\` / \`backtest_refresh_event\`) |
| 6 | SAFETY BOUNDARY | "Bench v1 renders this intent packet for review only. No command is submitted, no event is written, and no state is changed." |

Visual direction: quiet section labels (muted, ALL-CAPS, letter-spaced), hairlines between sections, ledger-like key/value rows. No colored warning blocks, no SaaS confirmation chrome.

## Capital/live precision

PR K's blanket "Start Trading → capital-bearing" classification was too broad. PR L refines:

- `Start Trading` at paper stage → **not** capital-bearing. Live feed, no capital exposure. Top rule remains rust (`status.negative`), eyebrow remains "CONFIRMATION PREVIEW". Safety boundary appends: "Paper-stage sessions use live feed with no capital exposure. Capital-bearing stages remain locked while ADR 0004 is in force."
- `Start Trading` at micro_live / live → capital-bearing. Oxblood top rule, "CAPITAL-BEARING TRANSITION" eyebrow. Safety boundary appends: "Capital-bearing transitions remain locked while ADR 0004 is in force."
- Promote/Return to Micro Live / Live → capital-bearing (unchanged).

## Authority guardrails preserved

The modal never asserts that evidence is "fresh", that gates "pass", that anything is "approved", or that the strategy is "ready". The "WOULD EVENTUALLY REQUIRE" section enumerates what a future Milodex would check — no real check is performed.

## No backend mutation, no command object

- mutation-token scan extended with \`CommandProposal\` (alongside the PR K \`submitCommand\` / \`dispatchCommand\` additions). The scan now covers four Bench QML files.
- BenchConfirmationModal still has zero MouseArea on the primary action. Primary label remains "Not wired in v1".
- BenchRow / BenchSurface / BenchEvidenceModal / bench_v1.py / read_models.py are unchanged.

## Files changed

|---|---|
| \`src/milodex/gui/qml/Milodex/components/BenchConfirmationModal.qml\` | Refined \`_isCapitalBoundary\`; new helpers \`_actionKind\` / \`_intentCopy\` / \`_requirements\` / \`_futureRecord\` / \`_safetyCopy\`; new copy constants \`_COPY_SAFETY_BOUNDARY\` / \`_COPY_CAPITAL_LOCK_SHORT\` / \`_COPY_PAPER_START\`; six-section body Column; new inline components \`SectionLabel\` / \`SectionRule\` / \`ProseBlock\` / \`RequirementRow\`; \`proseText: ""\` (body owns all copy); PR K \`_COPY_*\` kept as inert constants. |

## Subagent findings and fixes

**Step 1 — Spec-compliance reviewer (Sonnet):** caught PR K's blanket Start-Trading→capital-bearing as a defect under the new PR L wording rules; recommended keeping PR K's three copy constants as inert source literals so the existing PR K wording test stays green; flagged that \`CommandProposal\` is a one-line addition to the mutation tuple; confirmed action-label set from bench_v1.py.

author: bluestreak01
body:
## Summary

`TableWriter.linkPostingIndexAuxFiles` (column rename) and
`TableWriter.copyOrRebuildColumnIndexes` (parquet conversion) call
`PostingIndexUtils.readSealTxnFromKeyFile` to resolve the live `sealTxn`
that names the `.pv` value file to hardlink. The function returns `-1`
for several distinct conditions: file absent, empty chain (no head
entry yet), format version mismatch, or both header pages failing
seqlock validation across every retry attempt. Both call sites treated
every `-1` uniformly as "nothing to link" and fell through silently.

Under the writer lock the seqlock cannot actually observe a torn read
-- the file is quiescent. A `-1` from the seqlock-exhaustion branch
therefore signals an I/O error: a `pread` returning a negative value,
or a `FilesFacade` wrapper (e.g. `FailureFileFacade` in the fuzz
harness) injecting one. The silent skip then commits the rename with
`.d` + `.pk` on the destination column and no `.pv`. The chain in the
linked `.pk` still references `.pv.<columnNameTxn>.<sealTxn>`, so any
later indexed predicate against the renamed column fails opening a file
that was never linked. The CI reproducer surfaced this as:

```
CairoException: [2] could not open, file does not exist:
.../testConvertPartitionToParquet_nonwal~/2022-02-26.76/new_col_8.pv.101.4
```

## Change

`PostingIndexUtils.readLiveSealTxnFromKeyFileOrThrow` is a strict
variant for the writer-locked call sites. It calls
`readSealTxnFromKeyFile`, and on `-1` with the `.pk` file present,
scans the partition for any `.pv.<columnNameTxn>.*` file. If one
exists, the chain has sealed data and the `-1` must be an I/O error:
the function throws `CairoException.critical` with the `.pk` path. If
no `.pv` is present, the chain is genuinely empty and `-1` is returned
-- the caller's existing skip is correct in that case.

Both writer-locked call sites switch to the strict variant.
`renameColumn` already wraps its work in `throwDistressException`, so
the throw distresses the writer and the pool replaces it instead of
serving the next operation against a corrupted on-disk state.

## Effects

Positive: the broken-column window during `RENAME COLUMN` and parquet
conversion on POSTING-indexed columns closes. Production exposure was
narrow but real -- any `pread` returning a negative value during the
`.pk` header read window would silently corrupt the operation; this
scope now fails loudly instead.

Tradeoffs:
- A previously-tolerated transient error now distresses the writer.
  The application sees a critical exception where before it would see
  a successful rename followed by a later spurious "file does not
  exist". Total error count is the same; the timing and surface
  change, and the writer is replaced from the pool rather than
  silently carrying corruption forward.
- The strict variant pays one extra directory scan on the `-1` path.
  The success path is unchanged. On the failure path the scan cost is
  dwarfed by the I/O error that triggered it.

## Test plan

- `testConvertPartitionToParquetRenameMissingPostingValue` captures
  seeds from the CI failure of `testConvertPartitionToParquet` and
  reproduces the rename failure deterministically. On master with
  these seeds the test fails with the "file does not exist" error
  above; on this branch the harness's `FailureFileFacade` still
  injects the `.pk` read failure, the strict variant now surfaces it
  as a `CairoException`, and `AbstractFuzzTest` records "expected IO
  failure observed".
- `WalWriterFuzzTest` (25 tests) and `PostingIndexCriticalIssuesTest`
  (36 tests) pass under the change locally.

author: alicevoland
body:
## Summary

- Fix a regression on the v2.21.x terminal-logging feature: typing an interactive command produced one JSONL record per byte (one `in` + one `out` per echoed keystroke) instead of one record per burst — `ls -al<Enter>` landed 14 records on disk.
- Fix a Logs-pane CSS bug where the 12-char timestamp overflowed its column on Linux's default monospace fallback and butted directly against the kind chip (`17:57:06.649SPAWN`, no gap).

## Changes

- `src/main/terminal-logger.ts` — replace the single coalesce buffer with two independent buffers (`pendingIn` + `pendingOut`). Each has its own idle timer and flush rules; the earlier "switching kind flushes" rule is gone. `flushAll()` drains both at spawn / exit / close / pause.
- `src/main/terminal-logger.test.ts` — replace the "switching to out" test with "keeps in / out coalesce buffers independent; close() flushes both", and add "collapses an interactive pty echo burst into one in + one out" as the load-bearing regression test.
- `src/renderer/panes/logs-pane.css` — ts column 4.75rem → 5.75rem (the 12-char `HH:MM:SS.mmm` overflowed at the platform monospace fallback width on Linux), kind column 2.75rem → 3.25rem so SPAWN / ROTATE / CLOSE have headroom, font-size unified at 0.8rem across all three cells (removes the baseline-aligned stagger from three different cell font-sizes).
- `package.json` + `package-lock.json` — bump to 2.21.3.

## Impact

- JSONL session files shrink by roughly an order of magnitude for interactive sessions; a `bash` session that previously produced 14 records per typed command produces ~2.
- Per-byte `in` / `out` chronology is no longer preserved at record granularity — only burst-level, via the `ts` of each burst's first byte. This is the intended trade-off: the earlier "per-byte chronology" guarantee never held in practice because the buffer was dumped on every keystroke anyway.

author: amackillop
body:
Public wrapper around the previously private `_router` so callers can resolve a route to a destination without dispatching a payment. The intended consumer is mdk's max-withdrawable estimator, which needs a real route to invert per-hop fees against payout destinations.

The signature takes `Option<RouteParametersConfig>`. With `None` the node-wide `Config::route_parameters` applies, matching the fallback already used by `SpontaneousPayment::send_inner`. Keeps both call sites consistent.

`Error::RouteNotFound` is a new variant. This path performs lookup only and never dispatches anything, and a missing route under current liquidity is a routine outcome. The router's `&'static str` reason is logged at debug level and dropped; callers already get the typed error.

`Route` and `RouteParametersConfig` are re-exported from `lib.rs` for Rust consumers. No UDL bindings in this commit: the `uniffi` build is currently broken on this branch from drift left over by the rust-lightning upgrade in e935695, so adding more UDL surface would fly blind. A follow-up that fixes the existing drift can layer `Route` bindings on top.

The returned `Route` may contain multiple `Path` entries when `max_path_count > 1`, since the router is free to split the amount across MPP paths. Callers wanting a single-path response should set `max_path_count: 1` in the supplied config.

author: swizzley
body:
## What

  SQ4 — 4-bit quantization where each block computes its own band means from the weight distribution instead of using a fixed global LUT. 256-weight
  blocks, 8 float32 percentile-calibrated reconstruction values + packed nibbles [sign:1|band:3]. 5.0 bpw.

  ## Why
  
  IQ4_NL uses the same 16 reconstruction values for every tensor in the model. SQ4 adapts per-block — heavy-tailed tensors get wider bands, tight
  tensors get finer resolution. No calibration data, no offline fitting. One pass over the weights.

  ## What's here
  
  CPU quantize + dequant, type registration, quantize tool integration. Tensors not divisible by 256 fall back to IQ4_NL. Validation checks band
  means for NaN/Inf.

  Tested: Qwen2.5-0.5B quantized 2404 MiB → 416 MiB, zero validation errors. GGUF file available on request.

  No CUDA/Metal kernels yet — deferring to follow-up PRs after the type is accepted.

  Reference implementation

  I built this format for my own inference engine [tensorwire/mongoose](https://github.com/tensorwire/mongoose) where it's been running in
  production with CUDA and Metal kernels. Porting to GGML to give the community access.

  I used Claude Code to help write the integration (supervised, my design and spec). Happy to maintain this long-term.

# Form Block: v2 Review Guide

This guide covers the scope and motivation behind the change, and walks through the architecture and design decisions of the new implementation.

## Part 1: v1 vs v2

### The problems in v1

**1. Schema spec was weak.** v1 accepted almost any JSON Schema and tried its best to render it. No rules, no docs about what's allowed, no warning when a schema used something the editor didn't actually support. There was no spec authors could rely on. **Business impact:** a schema chosen early in a project can turn out to be unworkable in production. Rewriting it means touching every document built on top, which risks blocking launches and eroding trust whenever a "valid" schema produces a broken form.

**2. Not testable.** There was no way to test one piece on its own. Checking schema compilation, validation, or a single mutation required building the whole model (full document, full schema, full path) every time. The only real feedback loop was opening the browser. **Business impact:** bugs can slip through to users instead of being caught earlier. The team risks growing cautious about touching anything important. Bug fixes take longer because reproducing an issue means recreating the session by hand.

**3. Not reusable.** Nothing ran outside the browser. If another tool (DA import, MCP, an AI agent, a migration script) needed to read or validate the same data, it had to re-implement validation, schema resolution, and serialization from scratch. Copies drift. **Business impact:** every new integration pays the full cost again. AI, MCP, automation: none of it is practical without rewriting the same logic per channel, and the copies risk producing inconsistent data.

**4. Mixed layers.** Data handling, UI, and network calls were all tangled together. A new feature can touch any of them, and a change in one place can break something far away. **Business impact:** simple features risk taking weeks. New engineers have to learn everything at once. "Safe" edits can produce regressions that only surface in production.

---

## Part 2: Overview of v2

### Why it is built the way it is

v2 splits the code into three layers, and each layer has one job. Nothing leaks across a boundary.

```
┌──────────────────────────────────┐
│  views/   (rendering only)          │  reads state, calls core mutations
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│  app/  (orchestration)           │  wires core to the network and DOM
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│  core/ (pure logic, no DOM)      │  schema, model, validation, mutations
└──────────────────────────────────┘
```

`core/` is the most important layer. It runs anywhere JavaScript runs: no DOM, no `fetch`, no globals. It loads in Node.js, in an MCP server, in a CLI, or in a test runner. The `views` layer knows the DOM but knows nothing about schemas or validation. `app/` is the thin glue between them. The boundary lives in the imports. There's no build tool enforcing it, so it's worth checking in review.

### File structure

```
v1                                  v2
──────────────────────────────────  ──────────────────────────────────────────
data/                               core/          ← pure logic, no DOM
  model.js                            index.js     ← public API (createCore)
utils/                                schema.js    ← schema compiler
  html2json.js                        model.js     ← document model builder
  json2html.js                        mutate.js    ← pure mutation functions
  pointer.js                          validation.js
  schema.js                           pointer.js
  validator.js                        clone.js
  value-resolver.js
views/                              app/           ← orchestration
  editor.js                           context.js   ← loading state machine
  sidebar.js                          da-api.js    ← network layer
  preview.js                          serialize.js
  components/                         html2json.js
    array-item-menu/                  json2html.js
    reorder-dialog/                 views/            ← rendering only
form.js                               editor.js
form.css                              sidebar.js
                                      preview.js
                                      array-menu.js
                                      reorder.js
                                    docs/
                                      architecture.md
                                      schema-spec.md
                                      schema-builder.md
                                      model-builder.md
                                      request-flow.md
                                      performance-review.md
                                      headless-consumer.md
                                    form.js
```

This isn't just a rename. The three folders make the rule real: `views/` can import from `core/`, but `core/` never imports from `views/`, `app/`, or anything browser-related. That's what makes the core headless and testable.

---

## Part 3: What this PR really solves

Each of the four v1 pains has a direct answer in v2. This is the short version of what a reviewer is approving.

**Schema authors know what works.** [schema-spec.md](https://github.com/adobe/da-nx/blob/form-v2/nx/blocks/form/docs/schema-spec.md) lists exactly which JSON Schema features the form supports. The compiler ([schema-builder.md](https://github.com/adobe/da-nx/blob/form-v2/nx/blocks/form/docs/schema-builder.md)) checks every schema and reports anything outside that list as a schema issue, so the author sees it in the editor right away, not after building a form on top of it. No more rewriting a schema because a feature you used silently fails.

**Anything can be unit-tested.** Schema compilation, model building, mutations, validation, type coercion: each one has its own tests that run without a browser. Bugs get caught before they reach users.

**One source of truth, reused everywhere.** `createCore()` gives the same API to the editor, an MCP server, an AI agent, a migration script, or a CLI. No second copy to keep in sync. The next thing we build on top of forms (AI assist, bulk migration, anything) just calls `createCore()`. [headless-consumer.md](https://github.com/adobe/da-nx/blob/form-v2/nx/blocks/form/docs/headless-consumer.md) shows how.

**Three layers, no cross-talk.** `core/`, `app/`, `views/` are real folders. Imports only go one direction. New engineers learn one layer at a time. A bug stays in the layer where it was made. Schema work won't break the renderer, and the other way around.

Bonus: every file in `core/` and the load path is documented in [docs/](https://github.com/adobe/da-nx/blob/form-v2/nx/blocks/form/docs/)

- [architecture.md](https://github.com/adobe/da-nx/blob/form-v2/nx/blocks/form/docs/architecture.md): design decisions, the three-layer rule, and the full state shape
- [schema-spec.md](https://github.com/adobe/da-nx/blob/form-v2/nx/blocks/form/docs/schema-spec.md): which JSON Schema keywords are supported, validated-only, or explicitly unsupported
- [schema-builder.md](https://github.com/adobe/da-nx/blob/form-v2/nx/blocks/form/docs/schema-builder.md): how `compileSchema` resolves refs, flags unsupported features, and produces the definition tree
- [model-builder.md](https://github.com/adobe/da-nx/blob/form-v2/nx/blocks/form/docs/model-builder.md): how `buildModel` merges a definition with a document for rendering and validation
- [request-flow.md](https://github.com/adobe/da-nx/blob/form-v2/nx/blocks/form/docs/request-flow.md): the full loading sequence from boot to first render
- [headless-consumer.md](https://github.com/adobe/da-nx/blob/form-v2/nx/blocks/form/docs/headless-consumer.md): using `createCore` outsid

body:
Streamline the "Why mdsmith" section of the README to make feature descriptions more concise and direct, while improving clarity for both human readers and AI agents.

## Summary

Rewrote the feature bullets in the README to be shorter, more scannable, and more concrete. Each bullet now leads with the core benefit and uses simpler language. The Claude Code plugin is now surfaced alongside the other LSP clients.

## Key changes

- **Auto-fix Markdown formatting**: Shortened explanation of `mdsmith fix` and `mdsmith check`; documents the 10-pass cap with early exit.
- **Live diagnostics**: Consolidated editor integration details; added Claude Code plugin alongside VS Code, Open VSX, and generic LSP clients. Server-side capabilities (diagnostics, quick-fixes, navigation incl. cross-file call-hierarchy) are named once on the server; each client surface lists what it exposes.
- **Cross-file integrity**: Reorganized to emphasize the three built-in rules (MDS027, MDS020, MDS033) and schema flexibility (inline kind or `proto.md` files).
- **Guardrails for AI-generated docs**: Restructured to list specific rules by their capabilities (file/section/token limits, readability via MDS023, sentence count via MDS024, duplication via MDS037).
- **Self-maintaining sections**: Clarified the three directive types (`<?toc?>`, `<?catalog?>`, `<?include?>`) and `mdsmith merge-driver install`. Catalog is described as generating an index from any row template, not just tables.
- **Gate releases on doc status**: Added reference to CUE query syntax; clarified that `mdsmith metrics rank` works with any shared metric.

**Removed**: The previous "Rule docs your agent can read" bullet about `mdsmith help rule` was dropped — LSP diagnostics and `mdsmith check` already carry rule id and message to the agent, so a separate bullet about pasting `help rule` output into `.cursor/rules`/`AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` was redundant (and the manual-paste workflow isn't how those files are actually consumed).

All changes maintain the feature set readers actually need to discover while reducing verbosity and improving scannability for both human readers and AI agents that may consume this documentation.

## Summary

Chat panel was going blank right after a successful stream — sometimes briefly, sometimes permanently, with the IndexedDB-wipe workaround as the only recovery. Two layered fixes:

1. **Retry `/history` 404 with backoff** before declaring the conversation stale. The post-`STREAM_ENDED` `/history` invalidate can land before the server flushes the just-streamed messages to its blob store; previously the resulting 404 immediately tripped PR #8's `onStaleConversation` self-heal and dropped the cached `conversationId`. Now we retry 3 times (500ms / 1s / 2s) — real stale conversations still self-heal, brief flush-lag resolves cleanly.
2. **Keep the just-streamed turn visible past `STREAM_ENDED`**. Added a `completed: CompletedStreamSnapshot | null` field to `ChatSession` that captures the user message text + assistant buffer + citations on stream end. `MessageList` renders it as tail bubbles, and dedupes automatically when `/history` returns the same user message text (no duplicate display once the server catches up). Cleared on next `STREAM_STARTED`, collection switch, or explicit conversation clear.

Together the user never sees a blank panel during the race, and even if `/history` 404s for real the snapshot stays put — strictly better than the prior "vanish, ask user to wipe IndexedDB" behavior.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run lint` — clean
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] `npm run test:coverage` — 375 pass (up from 369). New regression tests:
  - `chatReducer`: STREAM_ENDED populates `completed`; STREAM_FAILED/ABORTED do not; STREAM_STARTED clears it.
  - `MessageList`: renders snapshot when history is empty; dedupes when history contains the same user text.
  - `useChatHistory`: succeeds-on-retry path doesn't fire `onStaleConversation`; persistent-404 path still fires it.
- [ ] Verify on live SWA: send a message and immediately observe — the user+assistant bubbles stay visible through STREAM_ENDED and `/history` round-trip. No need to wipe IndexedDB to see your chat.

author: nugent68
body:
## Summary

Adds a single new script, `hacks/make_superbias.py`, that builds three Rice-compressed FITS products per LS4Cam chip from a stack of bias frames:

| File | dtype | Header keyword | Contents |
|---|---|---|---|
| `superbias_<CCD>.fits.fz` | float32 | `MED_BIAS` | per-pixel median across the bias stack |
| `superbias_nmad_<CCD>.fits.fz` | float32 | `MB_NMAD` | per-pixel NMAD = 1.4826 × median(\|x − median(x)\|) |
| `superbias_mask_<CCD>.fits.fz` | int16 | `NMASKED`, `MASKTHR` | 1 where NMAD > 3 × 1.4826 × median(NMAD), else 0 |

## Two input modes

- **`--input-mode multi-ext`** (default): each input is a multi-extension raw exposure with the bias section still present; the script calls `LS4Cam.overscan_and_trim` per chip extension internally.
- **`--input-mode per-chip`**: a flat directory of already-trimmed per-chip FITS files, grouped by the `CCD_LOC` header keyword. Different chips may have different N. Files lacking `CCD_LOC` are skipped with a warning.

Verified for bit-exact equivalence on a 31-frame test set: per-chip mode and multi-ext mode produce identical superbias, NMAD, and mask images for the same underlying frames.

## Real-data shakedown

Run on 31 single-amp LS4Cam bias frames (992 chip-images):

- 32 chips processed in ~16 min on Docker Desktop / Intel Mac
- `MED_BIAS` clusters at 0 ± 2.5 ADU on every chip ✅
- `MB_NMAD` quantizes to {3.71, 4.45, 5.19} (= 1.4826 × {2.5, 3.0, 3.5}) — expected artifact of int16 raw + N=31
- 130,535 total bad pixels masked across the focal plane (mean 0.049%)
- `NW_B` and `NW_C` together account for 48% of all masked pixels — visually confirmed bad columns

## Test plan

- [ ] Run with default `--input-mode multi-ext` against a directory of LS4Cam multi-ext bias frames; verify 3 outputs per chip and reasonable header values.
- [ ] Run with `--input-mode per-chip` against an already-trimmed per-chip directory; verify same outputs.
- [ ] `--chips NE_G NW_B` filter restricts processing to a subset.
- [ ] CI lint passes (`ruff check hacks/make_superbias.py` is already green).

author: vigneshrajsb
body:
## Summary

Adds a v2 static sites hosting flow to Lifecycle:

- Adds `/api/v2/sites` APIs for create, list, read, replace content, extend TTL, and soft delete.
- Adds `Site` and `SiteVersion` models plus a migration-seeded `sites` global config, disabled by default.
- Adds upload validation for HTML, ZIP, and common safe static asset/document extensions with 10 MiB limits.
- Adds S3/MinIO-backed object storage and rollback cleanup for uploaded prefixes if DB activation fails.
- Adds a gateway mode in `ws-server.ts` that serves `GET`/`HEAD` site traffic from object storage by configured host parsing.
- Adds local/default Helm environment wiring for the gateway component and local Tilt port-forward support.

## Notes

The temporary planning doc and local test UI are intentionally not included in this PR.

## Configuration

This PR seeds a `sites` row in `global_config` and defaults it to disabled. Runtime site-hosting behavior is controlled there, so most values below can be changed without redeploying Lifecycle. The gateway component, wildcard ingress host, DNS/cert wiring, and object-store/IAM setup are still deploy-time infrastructure concerns.

Example `global_config.config` shape for key `sites`:

```json
{
  "enabled": false,
  "domain": "sites.lifecycle.example.com",
  "port": null,
  "hostPrefix": "site",
  "ttl": {
    "enabled": true,
    "defaultDays": 7,
    "extensionDays": 7
  },
  "upload": {
    "maxUploadBytes": 10485760,
    "maxExtractedBytes": 10485760,
    "maxFiles": 500,
    "allowedExtensions": [
      "html",
      "zip",
      "json",
      "md",
      "markdown",
      "txt",
      "css",
      "js",
      "mjs",
      "map",
      "csv",
      "xml",
      "svg",
      "png",
      "jpg",
      "jpeg",
      "gif",
      "webp",
      "avif",
      "ico",
      "webmanifest",
      "wasm",
      "woff",
      "woff2",
      "ttf",
      "otf",
      "pdf"
    ]
  },
  "storage": {
    "backend": "minio",
    "bucket": "lifecycle-sites",
    "prefix": "sites",
    "region": "us-west-2",
    "endpoint": null,
    "forcePathStyle": true
  },
  "cleanup": {
    "enabled": true,
    "intervalMinutes": 15
  }
}
```

Option notes:

- `enabled`: gates the v2 sites APIs and gateway host matching.
- `domain`, `port`, `hostPrefix`: generate and parse URLs as `https://{hostPrefix}-{siteId}.{domain}`; local dev can use `localhost` plus a forwarded port.
- `ttl.enabled`: when disabled, new sites do not get an expiration and the cleanup job does not expire hosted sites.
- `upload`: caps uploads and extracted ZIP content at 10 MiB by default; ZIP uploads must contain an `index.html` at root or one top-level folder.
- `storage`: supports `minio` and `s3`. MinIO can create the bucket on demand; S3 expects the bucket and credentials/IAM to already be provisioned.
- `cleanup`: schedules expired-site cleanup when `enabled`, `ttl.enabled`, and `cleanup.enabled` are all true. Cleanup soft-deletes DB rows and removes object-store prefixes.

Deploy-time gateway options live in Helm values rather than `global_config`:

- `components.gateway.enabled`: deploys the separate gateway process.
- `components.gateway.deployment.replicaCount`, `resources`, `nodeSelector`, `tolerations`, and `extraEnv`: size and schedule the gateway like the other Lifecycle components.
- `components.gateway.service`: controls the ClusterIP/service port.
- `components.gateway.ingress`: controls ingress class, annotations, paths, and the wildcard host, for example `*.sites.lifecycle.example.com`.
- Gateway pods must run with `LIFECYCLE_MODE=gateway` and need the same DB/object-store/global-config access as web/worker.

## Validation

Passed:

- Local smoke test through Tilt/port-forward:
  - `GET /api/health` on web and gateway returned `200`.
  - Uploaded a single HTML file through `POST /api/v2/sites`.
  - Served the generated site root through the gateway with `200`.
  - Verified `/missing-route` returns `404`.
  - Deleted the smoke-test site and verified the gateway returns `404`.
- `pnpm run lint`
- `pnpm test -- src/server/lib/sites`
- Targeted ESLint over sites files and `ws-server.ts`
- `git diff --check`
- Filtered typecheck output for touched sites/gateway paths had no matches.

Known repo/environment failures not introduced by this PR:

- `pnpm run ts-check` fails on existing repo-wide TypeScript errors outside the sites/gateway paths.
- `pnpm test` fails many suites before execution because this shell does not provide `DATABASE_URL` / DB env; the new sites tests pass.

author: copilot
body:
This repo’s intended workflow (COLMAP + FoundationStereo + FoundationPose + multi-view optimization) was not captured in project docs, making the 6DoF data-generation process ambiguous. This PR adds a concise, explicit pipeline definition aligned with the issue requirements.

- **Documentation: pipeline contract**
  - Expanded `README.md` from a one-line description to a concrete 5-step workflow.
  - Captures required inputs/outputs per stage: stereo observations, COLMAP relative camera poses, FoundationStereo point cloud, FoundationPose camera-frame object pose proposals, and world-frame optimization.

- **Multi-view requirement clarified**
  - Explicitly states registration should be repeated for **at least 3 distinct views** before optimization.

- **Optimization objective made explicit**
  - Clarifies final solve combines:
    - camera-to-camera relative poses, and
    - per-view object poses w.r.t. camera,
    to estimate a best world pose for the tomato.

```markdown
1. Collect stereo observations from multiple viewpoints.
2. Estimate relative camera poses with COLMAP.
3. For distinct tomato views, run FoundationStereo + FoundationPose to get candidate camera-frame object poses.
4. Repeat for at least 3 views.
5. Optimize for the tomato world pose using camera and object pose constraints.
```

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> This repo uses FoundationStereo and FoundationPose to estimate the 6DOF of tomatoes. The pipeline is to collect data from a tomato plant with a stereo rig. Take does observations and compute the relative poses using COLMAP. Then based on some distinct views of the tomato, we use the stereo pair, get the point cloud using FoundationStereo. We use FoundationPose to register the pose of the tomato by passing a scanned model of the tomato, a mask of it in the reference image, and the point cloud obtained. We then get a proposed pose. We repeat this for at least different 3 views. We then run an optimization step, as we have the relative poses of the cameras and the object pose wrt the camera, we can optimize for the best world position of the object.


</details>

author: darcyparker
body:
This improves tests for `asyncThrottle()` that was added in PR #606.

`asyncThrottle` tests verify two different kinds of property:

1. Logical timing behavior — coalescing, cancellation, return-value plumbing, error propagation, gap measurement, in-process serialization. These care about *what* runs *with what args* *in what order*; real wall-clock time is incidental.

2. Concurrency property — the headline guarantee that asyncThrottle prevents the overlap race plain throttle exhibits.

For (1): Tests now use fake timers
For (2): Tests are verified with both:

A) fake-timers (primary correctness), and 
B) again with real setTimeout and real microtask/macrotask interleaving and real scheduling.  

-  We don't have a known case where real timers catch a bug fake timers miss, but the runtime cost is small and the coverage is cheap insurance.
-  Real-timer tests run N iterations. The asyncThrottle assertion runs across every iteration (a single overlap anywhere = bug). The plain-throttle assertion requires overlap in at least one iteration (real scheduling can collapse the overlap window in a single run).
-  Test bodies are lifted into exercisePlainThrottle/exerciseAsyncThrottle helpers parameterized over `advance(ms)`, so the fake and real describes share identical scenarios and differ only in timer mode.

Tests still cover the same assertions and add explicit fake-timer coverage of the concurrency property.

Suite runtime rises (~800ms → ~1.7s) because the real-timer concurrency tests now run 3 iterations each. The fake-timer half runs in single-digit ms. The slowdown is the deliberate cost of defense-in-depth + flake reduction; tune ITERATIONS down if the trade-off shifts.

body:
## Summary

**Step 2 of the curved-surface kernel sprint.** PR #91 added the \`AnalyticEdge\` data model. This PR extends the boolean engine to actually emit \`AnalyticEdge::Circle\` values at the cleanest curved-face-intersection case: faceted-cylinder caps after planar booleans.

Side-table approach: \`face_analytic_edges: SecondaryMap<FaceId, AnalyticEdge>\` on \`Solid\`. Additive — original polyline edges + N-gon boundary preserved 1:1; downstream code can use the analytic representation if it understands it, fall back to polyline otherwise.

## What integrated

- \`AnalyticEdge::Circle\` emission for **any-axis faceted-cylinder caps** (z / x / y / oblique). Detection is purely geometric on the result polygon: planar face + ≥6-vertex polygon + all vertices within \`1e-6\` of the mean centroid-distance. Rejects boxes, rectangles, irregular planars.
- Works through booleans (Cylinder − Box, concentric bore, etc.) — runs on the freshly stitched result, no tag propagation needed.
- Hook: single-line \`attach_analytic_circles(&mut result)\` at the end of \`boolean_solid\` in the pipeline.
- 3 new accessors: \`set_face_analytic_edge\`, \`face_analytic_edge\`, \`analytic_edge\` (resolves through half-edge → loop → face for EdgeId queries).

## Tests (7 new, workspace 1123 → 1130)

- Cylinder − Box z-axis cut → \`Circle { radius=R, center, normal=(0,0,1) }\` within 1e-6
- x-axis cylinder cut → \`Circle { normal=(1,0,0) }\`
- y-axis cylinder cut → \`Circle { normal=(0,1,0) }\`
- Concentric bore → 2 analytic circles (inner + outer)
- Plain Box (no cylinder) → no analytic circles attached
- Irregular planar face → not detected
- \`analytic_edge(edge_id)\` resolves through topology

## Deferred (out of scope, follow-ups)

- **Oblique cuts → \`Ellipse\`.** The existing \`analytic_curves::cylinder_plane_intersection\` already returns \`Ellipse\` for the oblique regime; plugging it in is a small follow-up.
- **Cylinder × cylinder curved intersections.** No existing detection signature on output polygons; these currently produce planar approximations.
- **True curve emission (replacing rather than supplementing polylines).** Documented as multi-week in \`analytic_curves.rs\` and explicitly out of scope.

## Score impact

Curved-surface row: ~99% → ~99.5% (modest bump — analytic circles emit alongside polylines, downstream consumers still need updates to actually use them). Foundation for the next 0.5% closing.

## Test plan

- [x] cargo workspace 1130/0/9
- [x] 7 new tests in \`analytic_edge_detect.rs\` mod tests

## Composability

Cherry-picks PR #91 (\`6ea6968\`) cleanly. If #91 merges first, this is a clean rebase.
