body: Adds a small skeleton-loading system that renders animated placeholders during the brief window between mount and the snapshot fetch resolving — replacing the previous plain-text "Loading…" copy on every record-driven page. ## What's new A single skeleton module (`src/components/Skeleton.jsx` + `Skeleton.css`) exposes: - **Primitives** — `Skeleton`, `SkeletonText`, `SkeletonShell`. Every block uses a CSS shimmer sweep (linear-gradient driven by `background-position`) so it reads as "blank parchment" rather than a generic Material loader. The shell wraps the column in a `motion.div` for a short fade-in (and a fade-out when paired with `AnimatePresence`). - **Page-shaped variants** — `FeedSkeleton`, `BloggingTocSkeleton`, `CreatingGridSkeleton`, `RecordSkeleton`, `BlogPostSkeleton`, `CreatingWorkSkeleton`, `CommentsSkeleton`, `ProseSkeleton`. Each one mirrors the real layout's grid columns, gaps, and borders so the placeholder occupies the same footprint as the resulting content (no reflow when records arrive). The shimmer respects `prefers-reduced-motion` (CSS disables the keyframe and falls back to a static page-edge block). The Motion fade is short (~250ms) so reduced-motion users still get a usable cue. ## Where it's wired | Page | Skeleton | |---|---| | `Home`, `Posting`, `Logging` | `FeedSkeleton` (verb-badge + body rows) | | `Blogging` | `BloggingTocSkeleton` (number + title + summary + meta) | | `Creating` | `CreatingGridSkeleton` (4:3 thumb + kind/title/time) | | `Sharing` | `ProseSkeleton` | | `Record` | `RecordSkeleton` (replaces "Loading record…") | | `BlogPost` | `BlogPostSkeleton` (replaces "Loading post…") | | `CreatingWork` | `CreatingWorkSkeleton` (new — page previously rendered nothing while loading) | | `Comments` (sub-component on post pages) | `CommentsSkeleton` (replaces "Loading replies…") | ## Loading-state pattern Pages that previously initialized list state with `useState([])` now use `useState(null)`, so we can distinguish "snapshot fetch hasn't resolved" from "loaded but empty / no matches". The empty-state copy still renders correctly after load. ## Verified - `npm run build:offline` is clean (one Vite warning about chunk size which already existed). - `npm run dev` starts cleanly; `/`, `/src/components/Skeleton.jsx`, and `/src/pages/Home.jsx` all return 200.

author: pennerz
body:
…rasure

Copilot CLI v1.0.40+ writes ~/.copilot/config.json with leading // comment lines (JSONC). readConfig() used plain JSON.parse which failed on these comments, silently returning {}. When ensureFolderTrusted() then called writeConfig(), it overwrote the file with only trusted_folders — erasing copilotTokens, loggedInUsers, and all other auth data. This caused 'Session was not created with authentication info' errors, particularly visible in WSL where the config is separate from Windows.

Add stripJsoncComments() to remove full-line // comments before parsing. Add tests for JSONC stripping and auth data preservation.

author: anchapin
body:
## Summary

Fix the 5 integration-test failures that flipped from green to red on PR #1426
(issue #1417 — `Depends(get_current_user)` + ownership checks). The new auth
gating works correctly; it just exercises end-to-end response-model
serialisation paths that previously short-circuited, exposing a long-standing
bug in **one** integration fixture.

## Root cause

`backend/src/tests/integration/test_validation_api_integration.py::client`
rebinds `_val_mod.crud.get_job = AsyncMock(return_value=owned_job)` at module
level and never restores it. Because `_val_mod.crud` *is* the `db.crud` module
object, the patch leaks for the rest of the xdist worker session. Subsequent
tests then receive a bare `MagicMock` (where they expected `None` for unknown
job ids) and explode while the FastAPI handler builds the `ConversionJob` /
`FeedbackResponse` response models from `job.input_data.get(...)` etc., e.g.

```
pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 4 validation errors for ConversionJob
original_filename  Input should be a valid string ... input_type=MagicMock
status             Input should be a valid string ... input_type=MagicMock
target_version     Input should be a valid string ... input_type=MagicMock
options            Input should be a valid dictionary ... input_type=MagicMock
```

The `owned_job` mock was a shape mismatch on **every** field that response
models need (`id`, `user_id`, `status`, `input_data`, `progress`,
`created_at`, `updated_at`).

## The 5 fixed tests

| # | Test | Failure on PR #1426 head | Why this PR fixes it |
|---|------|--------------------------|----------------------|
| 1 | `test_end_to_end_integration.py::TestEndToEndIntegration::test_nonexistent_job_status` | `4 validation errors for ConversionJob` (mirror builder in `src/main.py:get_conversion_status`) | `crud.get_job` is restored on teardown → fake UUID round-trips to `None` → endpoint correctly returns 404 as the test asserts |
| 2 | `test_api_feedback.py::test_submit_feedback_invalid_job_id` | `AttributeError: 'ConversionFeedback' object has no attribute 'quality_rating'` | Same: the leaked mock made `if not job:` pass for a fake UUID, reaching production code that touches columns the ORM model does not expose. With the patch restored, the endpoint returns 404 first |
| 3 | `test_api_feedback.py::test_get_training_data_empty` | `assert [{... 'job_id': \"<MagicMock ...>\", ...}] == []` | The leaked mock made every job lookup short-circuit to a MagicMock; training-data scan returned synthetic feedback rows |
| 4 | `test_api_integration.py::TestConversionIntegration::test_check_conversion_status` | `4 validation errors for ConversionJob` | Same root cause as #1 |
| 5 | `test_api_integration.py::TestErrorHandlingIntegration::test_check_status_nonexistent_job` | `4 validation errors for ConversionJob` (was supposed to 404) | Same root cause as #1 |

Locally reproduced exactly (5 failed) and resolved (12 passed, 1 skipped) by
running:

```bash
pytest src/tests/integration/test_validation_api_integration.py \
       src/tests/integration/test_end_to_end_integration.py::TestEndToEndIntegration::test_nonexistent_job_status \
       src/tests/integration/test_api_feedback.py \
       src/tests/integration/test_api_integration.py::TestConversionIntegration::test_check_conversion_status \
       src/tests/integration/test_api_integration.py::TestErrorHandlingIntegration::test_check_status_nonexistent_job
```

## The fix (test-only, single file)

`backend/src/tests/integration/test_validation_api_integration.py` — `client` fixture:

1. **Restore the patch.** Snapshot `_val_mod.crud.get_job` before the rebind and
   restore it in a `finally:` block so the patch is fully scoped to the
   validation tests.
2. **Reshape the mock.** Replace `owned_job = MagicMock()` with
   `MagicMock(spec=db.models.ConversionJob)` and set every attribute the
   downstream Pydantic constructors need to JSON-serialisable values:
   `id` (UUID), `user_id` (str), `status` (`"queued"`), `input_data` (a real
   dict with `file_id`, `original_filename`, `target_version`, `options`),
   `progress` (`None`), `created_at` / `updated_at` (`datetime`).

Defence-in-depth: even if a future regression re-introduces the leak, the
`ConversionJob(...)` mirror builder in `src/main.py:get_conversion_status`
will now round-trip cleanly through Pydantic instead of raising
`4 validation errors for ConversionJob`.

## Verification

- **Integration suite (local, no Docker):**
  - Serial: `132 passed, 100 skipped` (was `5 failed, 127 passed, 100 skipped` on PR #1426 head).
  - `-n auto --dist=loadscope`: `132 passed, 100 skipped`.
- **Unit suite:** unchanged — no production code touched, no unit fixtures
  touched. The 3 unit failures observed locally
  (`test_export_zip_sanitization`, `test_get_job_success`,
  `test_get_job_invalid_uuid`) reproduce on `origin/fix/1417-endpoint-auth-audit`
  *without* this patch and are unrelated to this scope.
- **Lint:** `ruff format` / `ruff check` clean on the touched file.
- **Out-of-scope LFS noise** (`scripts/phase5_output/stage1/*/tokenizer.json`)
  is left untouched (issue #1427, Worker D's scope).

## Contract bug — recommended for a separate issue (NOT fixed here)

`src/api/feedback.py:155` returns `FeedbackResponse(...)` with
`quality_rating=db_feedback.quality_rating` (and `specific_issues`,
`suggested_improvements`, `conversion_accuracy`, `visual_quality`,
`performance_rating`, `ease_of_use`, `agent_specific_feedback`), but the
SQLAlchemy ORM model `db.models.ConversionFeedback` only declares `id`,
`job_id`, `user_id`, `feedback_type`, `comment`, `created_at`. Likewise
`db.crud.create_enhanced_feedback` accepts those rating kwargs but silently
drops them when constructing the model. So:

- The API claims a richer feedback contract than the schema stores.
- For a *valid* `job_id`, `POST /api/v1/feedback` would today raise
  `AttributeError` while building the response (the unit tests sidestep this
  with `MagicMock()` returns).

This is real production logic and is **out of scope per #1431's task brief**
("If you find that a mock failure reveals a real API contract bug in
production code, **DO NOT FIX IT** — instead document it in the PR body and
recommend a separate issue."). Recommended follow-up: open a `bug(api)` issue
to either (a) drop the extended fields from `FeedbackResponse` or (b) add
the missing columns + persistence in `create_enhanced_feedback`.

Closes #1431
Unblocks #1417 (PR #1426 Integration Tests gate)

body:
## Changes

`ImageProcessor.ProcessImage` previously guarded the encoder call with
a single process-wide `AsyncNonKeyedLocker` capped at
`Environment.ProcessorCount`. Encoding two completely unrelated source
images was therefore serialized against the same set of slots, even
though the work is fully independent.

This PR introduces a two-layer locking strategy:

1. **Outer `AsyncKeyedLocker<string>`** keyed by `originalImagePath`.
   Two resize requests for _different_ source images can now run in
   parallel without contending; two requests for the _same_ source are
   still serialized. After acquiring the per-source lock, the cache
   file existence is rechecked so that a request that lost the race
   reuses the just-produced output instead of redoing identical work.
2. **Inner `AsyncNonKeyedLocker`** retained with the existing
   semantics — it acts as a global memory-pressure cap on
   simultaneous encoder invocations (the original intent of the
   `ParallelImageEncodingLimit` configuration).

The `AsyncKeyedLock` package is already a dependency (the namespace
is in `ImageProcessor`'s `using` directives and is used across the
codebase, e.g. `ProviderManager._imageSaveLock`,
`TranscodeManager._transcodingLocks`). The pool-size constants
(`PoolSize = 20`, `PoolInitialFill = 1`) match the pattern used
elsewhere.

## Issues

Closes _no specific open issue_, but is a small correctness/contention
improvement to the image-encoding pipeline.

## Type of change

- [x] Refactor (non-breaking change that improves contention behavior)

## How Has This Been Tested?

Builds locally against `master` (net10.0) with zero warnings. Same
codepath was deployed and exercised manually against a running
10.11.6 Docker container; image responses behave identically and no
regressions were observed. The user-visible effect is a contention-
only one — it does not change any cache layout, request handling, or
output bytes.

- [x] My code follows the code style of this project.
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code.
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings.

## Summary

Final cherry-pick for the v2 redesign — six discrete frontend pieces. Backend fixes (.docx upload + Claude default bump) ship separately in #21.

### 7a · Mobile drawers below 920px
- `<DocsSidebar />` and `<SystemPanel />` become fixed slide-in drawers, anchored below the header.
- Toggle from header (constructs left, system right), close via scrim tap / Esc / horizontal swipe.
- New `<MobileScrim />` + `useSwipeToClose` hook.

### 7b · Touch-target sweep
Header icons, SystemPanel tabs, ChatMessage copy button, Composer mode pill, Modal close, BackToTopButton, FloatingInsightPanel expand — all ≥44×44px on touch (some always, some via the `(hover: none)` media query). New `button:has(> svg:only-child)` rule adds `min-width: 44px` for icon-only buttons.

### 7c · FloatingInsightPanel readability
Outer container bg swapped `bg-surface-card` (2% opacity) → `bg-surface-elev` (solid). Chat messages no longer bleed through when expanded.

### 7e · FloatingInsightPanel slide-to-top
Restructured ChatInterface so the message container + insight panel are siblings inside a `relative + overflow-hidden` wrapper. Panel is `position: absolute` anchored to the bottom; expanded state grows upward via `transition-[max-height]`. Single CSS property animation, GPU-friendly.

### 7d-fe · Model lineup refresh
- **OpenAI:** GPT-5.5 / 5.4 / 5.4-mini / 5.4-nano
- **Anthropic:** Claude Opus 4.7 / Sonnet 4.6 / Haiku 4.5 (+ Sonnet 4 / 3.5 kept as legacy fallbacks)
- Defaults: \`gpt-5.4-mini\` + \`claude-sonnet-4-6\`. BFF fallback IDs updated to match.

### 7f · Auto-hide chat scrollbar
New \`useAutoHideScrollbar\` hook adds an \`is-scrolling\` class on scroll, removes it 1s after the last scroll event. \`.scrollbar-matrix\` thumb is transparent by default, visible while scrolling and on hover (desktop only). Touch devices see the bar only during active scroll.

### Privacy copy honesty (drive-by)
User flagged the old "API keys… sent directly to Anthropic" line as misleading (suggests browser→Anthropic with no intermediary, which isn't how the Next.js BFF works). Rewrote as a two-paragraph block in Settings covering (a) keys are stored in localStorage and used by the BFF on your behalf, (b) chats + docs are session-scoped and deleted on session end. Extended the README with a matching "Privacy & API keys" section.

## Test plan

- [x] Desktop ≥921px: rails render as static side panels, no scrim, no drawer behavior.
- [x] Mobile ≤920px:
  - [x] Tap header "Toggle constructs" → docs drawer slides in from left, scrim dims content, chat scrolls locked.
  - [x] Tap scrim → drawer closes.
  - [x] Swipe drawer left ≥80px → closes (swipe right on system rail).
  - [x] Press Esc → drawer closes.
  - [x] Resize back to desktop while drawer open → drawer auto-closes.
- [x] Touch targets ≥44px verified via DevTools touch emulation.
- [x] FloatingInsightPanel expanded: bg is solid, messages don't bleed through. Tap chevron → panel slides up to nearly full chat-area height. Tap again → slides back to bottom. Smooth in both directions.
- [x] Auto-hide scrollbar: scroll chat → thumb visible. Stop → fades after 1s. Hover (desktop) → thumb reappears. Touch device → only visible during scroll.
- [x] Settings → model dropdowns show new lineups. Existing-user with `gpt-3.5-turbo` in localStorage keeps their preference until next save (then dropdown forces a valid new value).
- [x] Send a chat → BFF picks correct fallback (`gpt-5.4-mini` / `claude-sonnet-4-6`) when no per-request model is supplied.
- [x] Settings → Privacy section reads honestly about BFF architecture.

body:
## Summary

The full-Sentry-init branch in `get_logger` (LoggingIntegration + `before_send_*` filters + traces) was gated on `sentry_environment` being **exactly** `"production"` or `"test"`. Anything else with a DSN — including the common short form `"prod"` — fell through to the bare `elif sentry_dsn:` branch which sets `default_integrations=False`, silently disabling auto-capture of `logger.error()` calls as Sentry Issues.

`heal-email-service` uses `"prod"` / `"test"` as its env naming convention (test works because that string is identical, but prod would have shipped a Sentry blind spot). Broaden the gate to accept `"prod"` as a synonym.

## Before

```python
if (sentry_environment == "production" or sentry_environment == "test") and sentry_dsn:
    # full init
elif sentry_dsn:
    sentry_sdk.init(..., default_integrations=False, traces_sample_rate=0.0)
```

## After

```python
if sentry_environment in ("production", "prod", "test") and sentry_dsn:
    # full init — now reached for "prod" too
```

## Scope

Just the short-form `"prod"`. Not adding `"staging"`, `"stage"`, `"dev"`, etc. — keep the allow-list explicit; any consumer that wants the full path can pass one of these three.

## Test plan

- [x] New unit test `test_dsn_with_prod_shortform_inits_full_sentry` asserts:
  - `sentry_sdk.init` called once
  - `LoggingIntegration` constructed (would be absent on the bare branch)
  - `environment` kwarg passes through as `"prod"`
  - `enable_logs=True`
- [x] Existing `test_dsn_with_production_inits_sentry` still passes (no regression on `"production"`)
- [x] Existing `test_dsn_without_production_uses_minimal_init` uses `"development"` and still falls through to the bare branch (no regression on negative case)
- [x] Full suite: 49 passed

## Rollout

This goes into `main` and ships in `v1.0.0` alongside the breaking-change rename PR (#7, already merged). Tag push is still pending the heal-api + heal-email-service consumer PRs being ready.

author: joshwilks111-max
body:
## Summary

Post-ship `/review` (multi-specialist + adversarial across 3 parallel agents) surfaced 22 findings on the initial PoC drop. This PR lands the 3 real bugs + ~7 mechanical AUTO-FIX items. Remaining 6+ findings are filed into `TODOS.md` for a future session.

## Critical fixes

**C1 — `src/audit.ts:safeWrite` doesn't catch sync throws** (conf 9, adversarial)
- `FileAuditWriter.write` runs `mkdirSync` + `writeFileSync` synchronously before returning `Promise.resolve()`. If either threw (EACCES, ENOSPC, EPERM), the throw escaped before `.catch()` could attach. Violated CLAUDE.md hard rule #2 — audit failure must NOT propagate.
- Fix: convert `safeWrite` to `async/await` with `try/catch`. Catches both sync throws and rejected promises.

**C2 — `assertFixtureShape` crashes on `null`** (conf 9, adversarial + testing + self)
- A fixture containing literal `null` (or a JSON number/string) raised `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null` instead of the locked missing-field message.
- Fix: typeof-object/null guard before the cast. Re-uses the first required field's missing-field message so the contract holds.

**C3 — Replay loader ignored `prompt` argument** (conf 9, adversarial)
- The fixture's recorded `prompt` was never checked against the passed-in prompt. Template prompt drift would produce audit rows claiming (new prompt, old response) — a credibility-surface lie.
- Fix: compare `parsed.prompt` against the passed-in prompt; throw clear message on mismatch.

## AUTO-FIX bundle

- **I3** — Wrapped `demo.ts` body in `async main()` with `import.meta.main` guard. No more module-load side effects on import.
- **I4** — `JSON.parse` in `diffAudit` now in `try/catch`; corrupted golden files produce a structured `DIFF` line instead of crashing the gate.
- **I7** — Removed redundant `mkdirSync('audit')` (recursive `mkdirSync('audit/<runId>')` handles parent).
- **I8** — Removed unused `spyOn` import + dead `safeRun`/`captureRun` helpers in `check.test.ts`.
- **I9** — Extracted magic `80` into `const WRAP_COL` in `generative.ts`.
- **I10** — Stripped "Lane A/B/C" / "Task N" / "Round 0" build-process metadata from docstrings.
- **I11** — Added `TODO(v1.5)` `latency_ms` markers to both formatter row literals to mirror the one already on `audit.ts`.

Plus an internal-honesty fix: composite audit writer in `demo.ts` now writes file FIRST, then pushes to memory only on success. `memory.rows.length` now reflects on-disk truth. Print loop tolerates dropped audit rows gracefully.

## Filed as TODOs (`TODOS.md` → "From /review (2026-05-14)")

- I1 — Belt-and-braces `fileCount` via `readdirSync` (still soft consistency)
- I2 — Sort `readdirSync` in `check.ts` (Windows portability)
- I5 — Resolve `createAuditHook` fate (delete vs route formatters through it)
- I6 — Cover non-ENOENT readFileSync errors in `replay.ts` (EACCES/EISDIR/EBUSY)
- I12 — CI matrix on Windows + macOS
- I13 — Coverage gaps: FS-write-failure path, wrapAt80 boundary, structured null branches, e2e cleanup, brittler-than-needed assertNever regex, smoke-test hermeticity
- Style: stdout-vs-stderr convention on FAIL output, table padding under boundary values

- [x] `bun run test` — 71 pass, 0 fail, 98.04% aggregate line coverage (gate ≥0.9)
- [x] `bun run demo` produces identical stdout to prior runs (byte-deterministic)
- [x] `bun run check` — OK: 2 calls match golden

author: alexey-pelykh
body:
## Summary

Hand-rolled GraphQL mutations across talent-profile services selected `errors { message field }`, but the canonical schema (`packages/core/src/__generated__/talent-profile.ts:1372`) is:

```ts
export type UserError = {
  __typename?: 'UserError';
  code: Maybe<Scalars['Unknown']['output']>;
  key: Maybe<Scalars['Unknown']['output']>;
  message: Maybe<Scalars['Unknown']['output']>;
};
```

No `field`. Live E2E (#219 / #247) caught the systemic regression with:

```
createPortfolioItem failed: Field 'field' doesn't exist on type 'UserError'
cancelResumeUpload failed: Field 'field' doesn't exist on type 'UserError'
updateCustomRequirements failed: Field 'field' doesn't exist on type 'UserError'
```

The server returned this as a top-level GraphQL error; `ensureNoTopLevelErrors` collapsed it to `GRAPHQL_ERROR`. Unit tests with mocks accepted any shape — the contract-rule case described in CLAUDE.md § Schema/contract validation rule.

## Fix

Replace `errors { message field }` with `errors { code key message }` across `packages/core/src/services/profile/**` and update matching interfaces + consumer code.

Closes #248.

### Files touched (18)

**Source (11)**: shared, basic, certifications, education, employment, external, industries, portfolio, resume, reviews, visas — 33 wire selectors replaced (inline + multi-line forms), 9 local `UserError`-like interfaces aligned to `{ code?, key?, message? }`, 10 `first.field` consumer sites replaced with `first.key`.

**Tests (7)**: 7 unit-test fixtures + 1 stale type annotation updated to use `key:` instead of `field:`.

### Why `code key message` (not just `message`)

The consumer code formats a diagnostic hint `${verb} rejected (${first.key}): ${first.message}` — dropping `key` would lose the "which field caused the rejection" surface in user-facing error messages. Preserving `code` + `key` keeps full diagnostic info from the schema.

### Out of scope

- The CLI's `EnvelopeError.field?` (#128 v1.0 envelope ABI in `packages/cli/src/lib/envelopes.ts:68`) is a separate output-side concept. No call site currently threads `UserError`→`EnvelopeError.field`. Leaving the public envelope ABI untouched is intentional — renaming it would be a separate v1.0 ABI decision.
- Skills service already used the canonical shape — no change needed.

## Schema/contract validation rule compliance

Per CLAUDE.md § Schema/contract validation rule + § Code-review checklist:

- **Rule triggered**: YES — the change touches `packages/core/src/services/profile/{basic,certifications,education,employment,external,industries,portfolio,resume,reviews,visas}/index.ts` (most hand-rolled mutations in this PR's surface).
- **How satisfied**: the load-bearing E2E tests already exist as `packages/e2e/src/{36..40}*.e2e.test.ts` (introduced in #247). They currently fail with `Field 'field' doesn't exist on type 'UserError'`; this PR fixes them. The PR itself does NOT introduce new inferred wire shapes — it ALIGNS hand-rolled selectors to the canonical generated schema (`packages/core/src/__generated__/talent-profile.ts:1372`), which is the authority and is unchanged.

**Doc surface**: no doc surface affected by this change

### Live e2e verification

> [!NOTE]
> Live `TTCTL_E2E=1` requires interactive 1Password unlock and was NOT available in the subprocess that authored this PR. The orchestrator/operator should run the existing e2e suite locally to verify the previously-failing tests now pass:
> ```
> TTCTL_E2E=1 pnpm test:e2e
> ```
> Expected: tests in `packages/e2e/src/{36..40}*.e2e.test.ts` (portfolio, visas, external, resume, reviews) that previously failed with `UserError.field` rejection now pass.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm build` — clean (5/5 tasks, TypeScript compile across all packages)
- [x] `pnpm test` — 1684 unit tests pass (10/10 tasks, 799 core / 683 cli / 202 mcp / e2e smoke)
- [x] `pnpm lint` — clean (eslint, prettier, license-check, check-e2e-coverage WARN mode unchanged)
- [x] `pnpm prettier --check .` — all files match style
- [x] Adversarial gap-search: no drift across services; CLI envelope correctly left untouched
- [ ] Live `TTCTL_E2E=1 pnpm test:e2e` — to be run locally by operator (interactive 1P unlock unavailable in subprocess)

author: iamjohnnymac
body:
## Summary

PR D of v0.2.0. Ships five MPO/MTP cassette `DeviceType` JSON templates plus a `load_osp_cassettes` management command that imports them into NetBox. Operators run one command to seed all five cassettes, ready for use with the MTP harness deploy form (PR C).

## Surface area

- 5 JSON files at `netbox_osp/device_types/cassettes/`:
  - `mpo-12f-lc-cassette.json` — 1× MPO (12 pos) rear + 12× LC fronts
  - `mpo-24f-lc-cassette.json` — 1× MPO (24 pos) rear + 24× LC fronts
  - `mpo-12f-mpo-cassette.json` — 1× MPO (12 pos) pass-through
  - `lgx-lc-12f-panel.json` — 1U LGX panel, 12-fibre MPO → LC
  - `ru1-lc-24f-panel.json` — 1U 24F LC patch panel (2× MPO-12 rears)
- Each follows `netbox-community/devicetype-library` JSON schema
- `python manage.py load_osp_cassettes` — idempotent (slug-keyed update_or_create), atomic per cassette, materialises `RearPortTemplate` + `FrontPortTemplate` + `PortTemplateMapping` rows. `--dry-run` flag for safe inspection.
- `pyproject.toml` package-data extended with `device_types/**/*.json`
- 11+ tests in `tests/test_cassettes.py` covering: each JSON parses, required keys present, front_port.rear_port lookup integrity, rear_port_position bounds, idempotent import.

**Zero new model migrations. Zero new model definitions.** Pure orchestration + data.

## Why

PR C (MTP harness deploy) needs a cassette `DeviceType` to instantiate at each destination rack. Without this catalogue, operators have to hand-build cassette device-types via the NetBox admin UI — defeats the "one-click" value proposition. Shipping a curated set in-tree keeps the install path: \`pip install netbox-osp\` → \`migrate\` → \`load_osp_cassettes\` → done.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI matrix (Python 3.12 / 3.13 × NetBox 4.6.0) passes
- [ ] All 5 JSONs parse and import without conflicts
- [ ] Re-running \`load_osp_cassettes\` is a no-op

author: sam-at-luther
body:
## Summary

Add `pkg/composer/plan_acceptance.go` implementing decision #34's plan contracts so reliable's importer wizard Phase 2 (and any other caller parsing Terraform plan JSON) gates on a shared validator instead of inlining the rules.

## Why

The first-import and subsequent-apply contracts from `docs/managed-resource-tiers.md` are well-defined but had no shared helper. `luthersystems/reliable#1346` Phase 2's PlanPreview screen already shows the four counters (imports / drift / replace / destroy) and a clean-vs-warning banner — moving the rule encoding here means reliable consumes the validator and any future caller (CLI, deploy service) gets the same gate for free. Same pattern reliable already follows for `ValidateImportedResources` and `ValidateImportedResourceAuthorization`.

## Exported API

- `ValidateFirstImportPlan(plan, opts) []ValidationIssue` — asserts the first-adoption contract: exactly `opts.ExpectedImports` import actions, 0 add, 0 destroy, 0 unrelated replace; updates allowed only on the provenance allowlist. Imports counted across `plan.ResourceChanges` and `plan.ResourceDrift` (the latter catches imports surfaced as pre-plan drift on a re-run).
- `ValidateSubsequentApplyPlan(plan, irs, opts) []ValidationIssue` — asserts the looser re-apply contract: every non-no-op change must be either a provenance repair or covered by a matching `FieldEditApproval` on the corresponding `ImportedResource.FieldEdits`. Import `{}` block no-op on subsequent applies is the documented expected shape and passes.
- `FirstImportProvenanceKeys(cloud) []string` — returns the canonical AWS or GCP provenance tag/label paths including the provider-computed mirrors (`tags_all`, `effective_labels`, `terraform_labels`) so a single provenance write doesn't trip the unauthorized-change rule.

## Issue codes

Follow the existing `imported_resource_*` / `imported_plan_*` family conventions:

- `imported_plan_unexpected_import_count`
- `imported_plan_unexpected_create` / `_destroy` / `_replace`
- `imported_plan_unauthorized_change`
- `imported_plan_unapproved_create` / `_destroy` / `_replace`
- `imported_plan_nil_input`

Output shape is `[]ValidationIssue` so `dedupeAndSortIssues` handles them uniformly with the other validators.

## Test plan

- [x] 21 new tests covering all issue acceptance criteria (table-driven, mirrors `imported_validate_test.go` idioms)
- [x] `go test ./...` — 3153 passed (one pre-existing GCP-VPC compose integration test was flaky due to `terraform init` provider download under parallel load; passes in isolation and is unrelated to this change)
- [x] `go vet ./...` — clean
- [x] `go build ./...` — clean
- [x] `terraform fmt -check -recursive` — clean (no `.tf` touched)
- [x] All nine repo lint scripts pass

## Acceptance coverage

| # | Issue acceptance | Test |
|---|---|---|
| a | `ValidateFirstImportPlan` returns nil for N imports + provenance-only label writes | `clean import-only plan with provenance label adds passes` |
| b | Same call fails on a `create` of a non-provenance resource | `import + unrelated create fails` |
| c | Non-provenance label change in an import update fails | `import + non-provenance label change fails` |
| d | `ValidateSubsequentApplyPlan` fails on a `replace`/`delete` not covered by approval | `replace without approval fails`, `destroy without approval fails` |

Plus boundary tests: import surfaced as `ResourceDrift` is counted, import count mismatch, replace detection vs separate create+delete, `diffPaths` leaf-level shape.

Closes #402

author: tohuvavohu
body:
## Summary

Closes #135.

This fixes the scheduler invariant that science `AT` entries should only be emitted when they collect at least `ss_min` after slew/INSAA.

Changes:
- reject science targets that cannot collect `ss_min` before the next science deadline, then retry the next queue candidate
- drop science plan fragments that get closed before collecting `ss_min`
- avoid normal science termination while ACS is still slewing
- keep interrupted under-collected science targets retryable after emergency charging
- clamp `PlanEntry.exposure` at zero so serialized plans do not report negative exposure

## Validation

- `ruff check conops/ditl/queue_ditl.py conops/targets/plan_entry.py tests/scheduler_queue/test_queue_ditl.py tests/plan_entry/test_plan_entry.py`
- `mypy --strict conops/ditl/queue_ditl.py conops/targets/plan_entry.py`
- `pytest`

Result: `1920 passed, 1 skipped`.

Closed-loop regenerated comparison against the reconstructed problematic Tamalpais case:
- invalid v0: 36 short science entries, 16 negative exposures
- fixed run: 0 short science entries, 0 negative exposures
- observing time increased from `18:30:42` to `19:33:02`
- slewing decreased from `04:35:18` to `03:30:43`

author: lemonforest
body:
## Summary

Phase B3's wheel sanity check used `grep -E 'srmech/_native/.*\.(so|dll|dylib)$'` on `python -m zipfile -l` output. The `$` anchor never matches because zipfile -l interleaves file size + timestamp after the path. The wheel DID contain `srmech/_native/libsrmech.so` but the grep returned no matches and the job failed.

Fix: inline Python heredoc that opens the wheel as a zip and walks `namelist()`. Same intent, correct implementation.

Caught at PR #388 rc5 first push: scikit-build-core wheel job failed with "wheel does NOT contain srmech/_native/libsrmech.{so,dll,dylib}" even though the build log explicitly showed `-- Installing: .../srmech/_native/libsrmech.so`. publish step correctly skipped (`needs: [build-wheel, build-sdist, build-pure-wheel]`), so no broken artifact reached TestPyPI.

## After merge

Delete the `srmech-v0.1.1rc5` tag, re-tag at the merge commit, push — the rc5 publish then runs against the fixed workflow.

## Summary

13 improvements identified in PR #81's follow-up, landed as one logical sweep. The bot is now in shape to actually ship.

## What's in here

### Infrastructure (#1, #2, #10, #13)
- **CI workflow** for pr-bot — builds + tests on every PR touching \`apps/pr-bot/**\`. The root CI didn't cover the bot, which is how it rotted unnoticed.
- **Deploy workflow** to Fly.io on main, with image labels carrying the root version + git SHA. Skips gracefully when \`FLY_API_TOKEN\` is unset.
- **Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK** so non-Fly orchestrators get the same signal Fly already has.
- **\`__CTXLOOM_VERSION__\` baked into the bundle** so Sentry events from the bot show the actual release tag (was \`release: dev\` for everything).

### Observability (#4, #7, #8)
- \`captureError\` wired in all three handlers (pull_request, issue_comment, installation_deleted) and via \`app.webhooks.onError\`. Each event carries \`component: pr-bot\` + handler-specific context.
- Webhook errors distinguish **signature failures** (WARN — possible attack or rotated secret) from handler errors (ERROR). Both forwarded to Sentry.
- **Repo cache eviction** wired to \`setInterval\`. \`RepoCache.evict()\` existed but was never scheduled — the 10 GB Fly volume was a ticking time bomb. 7-day default, configurable via \`CTXLOOM_CACHE_MAX_AGE_DAYS\` / \`CTXLOOM_CACHE_EVICT_HOURS\`.

### Security & safety (#5, #9)
- **Per-installation token-bucket rate limiter** for \`/ctxloom\` slash commands. \`refresh\` (expensive — rebuilds graph) gets capacity 3 + refill 1/min. \`explain\` / \`ignore\` get generous limits. Drops silently so an attacker can't amplify their throughput by triggering replies.
- **\`PRIVATE_KEY\` hardened**: PEM by default; base64 only with explicit \`PRIVATE_KEY_BASE64=1\` flag, decoded result validated to be a PEM. Loud errors on anything ambiguous. The previous "PEM or base64 for convenience" dual-mode was a known footgun.

### Polish (#3, #6, #11, #12)
- Removed \`https://github.com/apps/ctxloom-pr-bot\` marketplace placeholder — self-host only until that's real.
- Confirmed \`max_inline_per_pr\` is enforced (\`pullRequest.ts:152\`).
- **22 new tests**: \`requirePrivateKey\` (10), \`slashCommandRateLimit\` (6), \`installationDeleted\` edges (3), \`configSchema\` drift guard (3).
- **\`apps/pr-bot/schema/ctxloom.schema.json\`** — JSON Schema mirroring the Zod schema. VS Code / JetBrains YAML extensions will autocomplete and validate \`.ctxloom.yml\`. Drift-guard test keeps the two in sync.

## Verification

|---|---|
| \`npm run build -w @ctxloom/pr-bot\` | ✅ 238 KB |
| \`npm test -w @ctxloom/pr-bot\` | ✅ 87/87 (was 65) |
| Root \`npm test\` | ✅ 763/763 |
| Root \`npm run lint\` | ✅ clean |

## Repo configuration the user must set before production

For the deploy workflow to actually deploy:

- **Secret**: \`FLY_API_TOKEN\` — Fly.io deploy token scoped to ctxloom-pr-bot

If unset, the workflow logs a warning annotation and exits 0 (so first-time setup doesn't break main). After it's configured, every push to main touching \`apps/pr-bot/**\` deploys automatically.

body:
## Summary
- Slow `search-index-sync-models` cron from `*/2 * * * *` to `*/5 * * * *` to relieve sustained disk-write pressure on the `meilisearch-0` instance (DataPacket node `talos-uvh-ow7`).
- Each cron tick produces one Meilisearch commit per index; lower cadence batches more queue entries per commit, cutting disk flushes proportionally without changing what gets indexed.

## Why
Cluster investigation today found `meilisearch-0` writing 200+ MB/s sustained to a single NVMe also hosting Talos `/var`, with write latency 1.1–2.3s (vs <1ms baseline). Cascading 408s on meilisearch and 502/504s on co-tenant `civitai-advertising-primary` pods. The dominant writer was `models_v9`, fed by this cron + ~30 producer call sites that enqueue to a Redis SET-backed queue (already de-duplicated per cycle in `src/server/redis/queues.ts`). Halving the cron rate is the cheapest, most reversible producer-side relief.

Full handoff doc: `claudedocs/meilisearch-node-saturation-handoff.md` in the talos-infra repo.

## Trade-off
Model search results stale ≤5 min instead of ≤2 min. Other indexes (users, articles, images, collections, bounties, imageMetrics, comics) unchanged.

## Test plan
- [ ] After deploy, verify `talos-uvh-ow7` `nvme0n1` write latency drops below 100ms sustained (Prometheus: `rate(node_disk_write_time_seconds_total{instance="192.168.10.3:9100",device="nvme0n1"}[5m]) / rate(node_disk_writes_completed_total{...}[5m]) * 1000`)
- [ ] `civitai-advertising-primary` 502/504 rate in Traefik returns to baseline (~0/s)
- [ ] Model search continues to surface newly-published / freshly-edited models within ~5 min (manual spot-check)
- [ ] No spike in Meilisearch task queue depth (`kubectl exec -n meilisearch meilisearch-0 -c meilisearch -- curl -s localhost:7700/tasks?statuses=enqueued`) — should be flat-to-lower, not climbing

body:
## Summary

Drops the four-signal ensemble pipeline (which forced the lowest alternative to 0.00 via min-max normalisation) in favour of a user-selected single signal per LLM profile. Fixes a regression where clicking an alternative in the Run Detail review carousel hid the other alternatives from view.

### Pivot to a single active signal
- New ``LLMConfig.confidence_signal`` field — same tier of knobs as ``description_verbosity`` / ``n_alternatives``. Allowed values: ``logprob``, ``self_consistency``, ``self_decl``, ``judge``, ``none``. Default ``self_consistency`` (universal, zero extra token cost).
- ``ConfidenceConfig`` drops the four ``use_*`` booleans and keeps the master ``enabled`` switch plus the absolute band cut-offs. Legacy YAML still loads silently — unknown keys are dropped without crashing.
- ``amx/llm/confidence/scorer.py`` now dispatches to exactly one per-signal module; ``ensemble.py`` is replaced by a tiny ``band.py`` that maps raw 0-1 scores to HIGH / MED / LOW.
- ``AlternativeScore`` slims to ``{text, signal, score, band}``. JSON parser still accepts the legacy flat ``list[str]`` and the old ensemble payload, so existing ``history.db`` rows surface in Studio without a pill.

### Surfaces wired identically to ``description_verbosity``
- Studio LLM profile create / edit modal (``frontend/src/routes/Settings.tsx``)
- Studio New Run advanced LLM settings override (``frontend/src/routes/RunNew.tsx``)
- Pydantic per-run validator (``amx/web/routers/runs.py::LLMOverrides``)
- CLI ``/confidence-signal`` slash command + extra prompt in ``interactive_llm_block`` (``amx/cli_support/commands/profiles.py``)

### Badge
``ConfidenceBadge`` label reads ``SC: HIGH 0.78`` style so the user always knows which scorer drove the value (``LP`` / ``SC`` / ``SD`` / ``JU`` abbreviations). Popover shows signal + score + band only.

### Carousel regression fix
``amx/web/routers/pending.py::_serialize`` previously kept the cached single-entry alternatives list when a pending entry already had one, so the SPA dropped A / B / C from the carousel as soon as the user picked one of them. The guard is gone: fresh ``run_results.alternatives_json`` always wins, so the reviewer can switch back to a different alternative without re-running.

### Test plan
- [x] ``pytest -q`` — 2027 passed, 3 skipped (sentence-transformers env mismatch), no regressions.
- [x] ``ruff check`` / ``ruff format --check`` clean.
- [x] ``mypy`` on touched modules clean (pre-existing ``amx/storage/sqlite_store.py`` and ``amx/web/routers/runs.py`` integer-coercion warnings unchanged).
- [x] ``npx tsc -b --noEmit`` + ``npm run build`` clean.
- [ ] Remote Studio smoke test post-merge: confidence signal dropdown appears in profile edit + New Run advanced section; ``LP / SC / SD / JU: HIGH/MED/LOW 0.xx`` badge on each alternative; clicking one keeps the others visible.

## Summary

S3 ACT scaffold for `erdos-659-oq-01-oq-02` (d ≥ 3 extension of the
sharp-distance-bound result). Ships the structural skeleton for the
**axis-vs-plane** safety story of the lattice `L_{2, 5}`, derived from
three QR-descent sub-lemmas (one per equation A/B/C of S2b PREP §4).

The three sub-lemma bodies (`safe_A_holds`, `safe_B_holds`,
`safe_C_holds`) are deferred to **S4 ACT** as strategic sorries — same
isolation convention used in the gauss-wilson-non-cyclic-oq-01 Phase B
and Phase C scaffolds (PRs #18232 / #18652).

## What ships

| File | LOC | Sorries | Axioms |
|---|---|---|---|
| **NEW** `proofs/Proofs/Erdos659OQ01OQ02.lean` | 134 | 3 strategic | 0 |
| `proofs/Proofs.lean` | +1 | — | — |

The scaffold exposes:

- 3 predicates: `safe_A` (`5c² = a² + 2b²`), `safe_B` (`2b² = a² + 5c²`),
  `safe_C` (`a² = 2b² + 5c²`).
- 3 strategic-sorry theorems: `safe_A_holds`, `safe_B_holds`,
  `safe_C_holds` — each with a per-theorem discharge-plan docstring
  pointing at S2b PREP §4 + §5.
- 1 composite predicate: `SafePrimePair_AxisVsPlane (p q : ℕ) : Prop`.
- 1 named outer theorem: `safe_2_5_axis_vs_plane :
  SafePrimePair_AxisVsPlane 2 5` (derived from the three sub-lemmas).

## Scope and honesty

- **Axis-vs-plane only.** Full-rank safety (per S2c PREP §6.1
  recommendation) is deferred to a separate axiom in a future PR; this
  PR introduces **0 new axioms**, all gaps are theorem sorries.
- **Build pending.** Researcher worktree `proofs/.lake` is the

  will additionally need `Mathlib.NumberTheory.LegendreSymbol.QuadraticReciprocity`

S2b PREP §5 provides a Lean **template** for the safe_A descent body

## Summary

This is the documentation catch-up requested as part of the (a)→(b)→(c) plan. Implementation has been moving faster than the design docs since PR #45, so v0.2 here is the formal companion to the v1.3 requirements, written *from* the merged code so reviewers can trace any v1.3 requirement to a concrete module and test.

The doc is intentionally a single 496-line markdown file rather than a multi-doc design system — easier to keep in sync as the code evolves.

## What is captured

1. **Approval object** — full schema, plan_hash / pre_exec / post_exec semantics, `/modify` REPLAN sequence.
2. **Mode transition state machine** — `approval` ↔ `fullauto` with admin + `/confirm <token>` + `effective_until` + `auto_revert_to`.
3. **Telegram command surface** — every connected and read-only command, with the auth model (allowed user_id ∩ allowed chat_id ∩ role).
4. **Risk evaluator** — full Risk Level Matrix including the 3a/3b/3c/3d split. Order of `decideControlAction` checks documented so a future refactor can be reviewed against the same rules.
5. **Ralph state machine** — phases, transitions, the removed `WAITING_FOR_DIFF_APPROVAL`, and the new `escalateStuckOpenCodeRunning` guard.
6. **Hashing** — canonical JSON spec.
7. **LangGraph planning layer** — non-executing skeleton; dynamic re-planning is explicitly deferred.
8. **NemoClaw runtime status (honest)** — `nemoclaw` v0.0.38 + `openshell` v0.0.36 are installed on the dev host but `openclaw` is missing, so the mediated path currently times out and degrades via the fallback set. Production execution flows through `RALPH_DISPATCHER=opencode-kimi`. This is documented as a real Phase-0 implementation gap rather than papered over.
9. **OpenCode + Kimi K2.6 dispatcher contract (PR #45/#46)** — model selection, env scrubbing, worktree prompt rules (with the explicit "do not write a literal candidate.patch" rule), classify order, soft-timeout downgrade.
10. **Per-story worktree isolation** — `createStoryWorktree` / `diffStoryWorktree` / `destroyStoryWorktree` contract and the path excludes.
11. **Stuck-loop recovery** — the fallback failure set (in sync between two modules) and the attempts → ESCALATED guard.
12. **GitHub Issue supplier** — cadence, idempotency, default-off, redacted bounded summary.
13. **Secrets injection / failure escalation / explicit prohibitions** — same rules as v1.3 but with module/test pointers.
14. **Acceptance test mapping** — a per-requirement table pointing at the implementing module and the test that asserts it.
15. **Known limits** — what is NOT yet built at v0.2 (24h soak data, openclaw runtime, dynamic re-planning, Telegram `RESUME_AFTER_SECURITY_STOP` workflow).
16. **Versioning** — v1.0 → v1.3 → v0.2 history.

## What this PR does not change

- Zero behavior change. Only `docs/ralph-detailed-design-v0.2.md` is added.
- No code or tests modified.
- No CI surface changed.

## Test plan

- [ ] Reviewer cross-checks §16 acceptance test mapping against the actual test names; nothing should be missing.
- [ ] Reviewer confirms §8 (NemoClaw current status) matches their host install state, or amends if `openclaw` is now available.
- [ ] Reviewer confirms §9.2 (Kimi default model and override env vars) matches the dispatcher.
- [ ] Reviewer confirms §17 known-limits list matches what they expect to flag as v0.3 work.

## Summary
Six tool failures observed in live server logs are fixed with surgical edits:

- **awc-metar / fedreg-get-document**: empty required strings were sent to remote APIs (400/404). Added `min_length=1` on `AWCMetarParams.ids` and `FedRegGetDocumentParams.document_number` so Pydantic rejects them locally.

## Summary

Lifts the extension from the VS Code 1.94 baseline (Oct 2024) to 1.118 in three independently revertable layers, modernizes the manifest, and migrates the custom translation system to the stable `vscode.l10n` API.

Original target was 1.120 (latest stable at design time), bumped down to 1.118 because `@types/vscode 1.120` is not yet published on npm. `engines.vscode` and `@types/vscode` pinned in lockstep at `^1.118.0`.

### Layer 1 — engine + toolchain bump (`0a20adc`)
- `engines.vscode` + `@types/vscode`: `^1.94.0` → `^1.118.0`
- TypeScript 5.9, ESLint 9.39, esbuild 0.28, `@typescript-eslint/*` 8.59, `@vscode/test-cli` 0.0.12, `@vscode/test-electron` 2.5, Mocha 11.7
- CI matrix extended to Node 20 + Node 22

### Layer 2 — manifest cleanup (`a69f44a` + `689feef` + `de01d5f`)
- Drop the redundant `activationEvents` block (implicit activation since 1.74)
- Drop the unused `@vscode/extension-telemetry` runtime dep
- Drop the unregistered `journal.test` command
- Declare `capabilities.virtualWorkspaces: "limited"` and `capabilities.untrustedWorkspaces: "limited"` with `restrictedConfigurations: ["journal.base"]` (refined from spec's `false` to keep the extension usable in untrusted workspaces while still blocking workspace overrides of `journal.base`)

### Layer 3 — `vscode.l10n` migration (`3b46cf6` + `7f5baa4`)
- Replace `src/ext/messages.json` (299 lines) + `src/ext/translations.ts` (126 lines) with VS Code's stable `vscode.l10n` API (introduced 1.73)
- Manifest strings → `package.nls.json` + 10 locale overrides
- Runtime strings → `l10n/bundle.l10n.json` + 10 locale bundles (15 keys each)
- All 11 previously supported locales preserved (en, de, fr, es, it, pt, nl, ru, zh, ja, ar)
- Fixed a moment.js escape bug in the Spanish locale (`[desde] el` → `[desde el] ll`) carried over from `messages.json`
- Added `@vscode/l10n-dev` devDep and `npm run l10n:export` script
- Removed 7 `getInput*Translation` re-exports from `src/ext/index.ts`

author: mcgeedarion
body:
# Redox-Inspired Scheme VFS + Userspace Driver Framework

This PR implements the three highest-value ideas from Redox OS adapted to RustOS:

---

## 1. Scheme-Based VFS (`src/fs/scheme_table.rs`)

Adds a kernel-wide `SchemeTable` that maps URL prefixes to `Arc<dyn Scheme>` handlers.

- `open("net:eth0", flags)` → routed through `SCHEME_TABLE`
- `open("/etc/passwd", flags)` → falls back to existing POSIX VFS (zero breakage)
- `SCHEME_TABLE.register("blk", handler)` / `SCHEME_TABLE.unregister("blk")`
- `is_scheme_url(path)` helper distinguishes scheme URLs from classic paths
- `Scheme` trait: `open / read / write / ioctl / seek / close` — mirrors the fd interface

---

## 2. IPC Proxy Scheme (`src/fs/ipc_proxy_scheme.rs`)

`IpcProxyScheme` wraps an `IpcEndpoint` and implements `Scheme` by forwarding every call as a serialised `SchemeRequest` message to a userspace driver process and blocking for the `SchemeResponse`.

- Minimal tag-prefixed binary wire format (no external deps in kernel)
- Per-scheme `Mutex` serialises concurrent callers; ready for pipelined cookies later
- Registered automatically by `sys_scheme_register`

---

## 3. Driver + Scheme Syscalls

### `src/syscall/driver.rs`
| Syscall | Number | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `sys_driver_bind(bdf, flags)` | 400 | Claim PCI device, map BARs into caller's AS, return `DriverHandle` |
| `sys_dma_alloc(handle, size, align)` | 401 | Alloc contiguous DMA buffer, map into caller, return (virt, phys) |
| `sys_irq_subscribe(handle, irq, ep)` | 402 | Route IRQ as `IrqNotification` messages to `ep` instead of kernel ISR |

### `src/syscall/scheme.rs`
| Syscall | Number | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `sys_scheme_register(name, ep)` | 403 | Publish userspace driver as `name:` scheme handler |
| `sys_scheme_unregister(name)` | 404 | Remove scheme; auto-called on process exit |

---

## 4. Shared Types Crate (`crates/scheme-api/`)

`#![no_std]` crate shared between the kernel and all userspace drivers:
- `SchemeRequest` / `SchemeResponse` enums
- `SchemeError` with `.to_errno()` mapping
- `OpenFlags` (bitflags), `SeekWhence`, `IpcEndpoint`, `DriverHandle`, `SchemeFileId`
- `parse_scheme_url()` helper
- `IrqNotification` wire struct

---

## 5. Updated `sys_open` Dispatch (`src/syscall/fs.rs`)

`sys_open` now checks `is_scheme_url(path)` first:
- Scheme URL → `SCHEME_TABLE.open()` → `FdEntry::Scheme { handler, fid }`
- POSIX path → `vfs_ops::open()` → `FdEntry::Legacy(node)` (unchanged)

`sys_read/write/close/seek/ioctl` dispatch on the same `FdEntry` enum.

---

## 6. Virtio-Net Userspace Driver (`userspace/drivers/virtio_net/`)

The virtio-net NIC is now a **userspace process** — zero NIC code runs in ring 0:

1. `sys_driver_bind(BDF, 0)` — claims the PCI device
2. `sys_dma_alloc` × N — allocates RX/TX virtqueue descriptor rings + receive buffers
3. MMIO virtio device initialisation (spec §3.1) via volatile writes
4. `sys_irq_subscribe(handle, irq, ep)` — IRQs arrive as `IrqNotification` messages
5. `sys_scheme_register("net", ep)` — publishes `net:` scheme
6. Event loop: dispatches `IrqNotification` (drain RX virtqueue) vs `SchemeRequest` (read/write frames)

The TCP/IP stack opens `net:eth0` for raw Ethernet I/O — no change to the network stack interface.

---

## Integration Checklist

- [ ] Add syscall numbers 400–404 to the master `SyscallNumber` enum
- [ ] Wire `sys_driver_bind/dma_alloc/irq_subscribe/scheme_register/scheme_unregister` into the syscall dispatch table
- [ ] Add `FdEntry::Scheme` variant to the process fd table
- [ ] Implement `crate::drivers::pcie::find_device_by_bdf` + `try_claim`
- [ ] Implement `crate::kernel::irq::subscribe_userspace`
- [ ] Implement `crate::mm::dma_alloc_coherent`
- [ ] Add `crates/scheme-api` to workspace `Cargo.toml`
- [ ] Launch `virtio_net_drv` from init before the TCP stack starts
- [ ] Register in-kernel schemes (`tty:`, `proc:`, `file:`) in `kernel_main`

This PR updates [botocore](https://pypi.org/project/botocore) from **1.19.63** to **1.43.7**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 1.43.7
   ```
   ======

* api-change:``arc-region-switch``: Adds support for enabling and disabling Lambda event source mappings in Region switch plans.
* api-change:``batch``: Adds a billing callout to docs regarding using the CE Scale Down Delay feature
* api-change:``bedrock-agentcore-control``: Adds support for read-only summary APIs for Policy Engine, Policy, and Policy Generation resources, enabling metadata retrieval without KMS decryption for AWS Config integration.
* api-change:``billingconductor``: Add ConflictException to UpdateCustomLineItem operation.
* api-change:``connect``: This change added three new EventSourceName for schedule notification feature
* api-change:``connectcampaignsv2``: This release added support for Outbound Campaign timezone detection using all available contact methods
* api-change:``connectcases``: Amazon Connect Cases now supports SLA durations of up to 2 years (1,051,200 minutes), increased from the previous maximum of 90 days (129,600 minutes). This enables you to track long-running service level agreements for cases that require extended resolution timelines.
* api-change:``dsql``: Added support for Amazon Aurora DSQL change data capture (CDC) streams that deliver row-level database changes to Amazon Kinesis in JSON format. Includes CreateStream, GetStream, ListStreams, and DeleteStream operations.
* api-change:``ec2``: Include length limits in the SDK and documentation for text fields in Image (AMI) APIs such as the image name and description
* api-change:``endpoint-rules``: Update endpoint-rules client to latest version
* api-change:``es``: Adds support for AutomatedSnapshotPauseOptions.
* api-change:``glue``: AWS Glue now defaults the job timeout to 480 minutes for Glue version 5.0 and later when no timeout value is specified. The default remains 2,880 minutes for Glue version 4.0 and earlier.
* api-change:``lightsail``: Added OriginIpAddressTypeEnum (ipv4, ipv6, dualstack) and ipAddressType field to Origin and InputOrigin structures for Lightsail CDN distributions. Allows customers to specify how the distribution connects to origins, using IPv4, IPv6, or dualstack networking
* api-change:``opensearch``: Adds support for AutomatedSnapshotPauseOptions.
* api-change:``partnercentral-account``: Added ServiceQuotaExceededExceptions for Profile operations
* api-change:``pcs``: Add support for Amazon EC2 Interruptible-ODCR
* api-change:``quicksight``: Adds five new custom permission option for Quick Apps so that these capabilities can be controlled by public SDK and CLI.
* api-change:``redshift``: Added rg.xlarge and rg.4xlarge to valid NodeType values and updated documentation for CreateCluster, ModifyCluster, ResizeCluster, and RestoreFromClusterSnapshot APIs to reflect RG node type support.
* api-change:``rtbfabric``: Customers can now configure custom domain names for their RTB Fabric gateways. This enables partners to use their own branded domain for RTB traffic instead of the default rtbfabric endpoint
* api-change:``sagemaker``: Adds execution role session name mode to reflect user identity in Studio. Adds Flexible Training Plans on Studio apps. Adds restricted model packages to control access to proprietary model artifacts via IAM. Fixed instance type parity between inference endpoints and managed shadow tests.
* api-change:``securityagent``: Add support for code reviews, a new resource type that enables automated security-focused static analysis of source code repositories.
* api-change:``socialmessaging``: Adds parameters to call the GetWhatsAppMessageTemplate and UpdateWhatsAppMessageTemplate APIs with a template name and language code in place of the template ID. Linked WhatsApp accounts also describe whether the WABA is onboarded to Meta's Marketing Messages API.
* api-change:``stepfunctions``: Updated default SDK endpoints for AWS Step Functions in AWS GovCloud (US) regions. The default Dual-Stack endpoints now resolve to "states-fips" prefixed hostnames. There are no changes to service behavior. No customer action is required.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 1.43.6
   ```
   ======

* api-change:``bcm-data-exports``: With this release, customers can configure their data exports to generate additional integration artifacts for Athena and Redshift.
* api-change:``bedrock-agentcore``: Launching AgentCore payments - a capability that provides secure, instant microtransaction payments for AI agents to access paid APIs, MCP servers, and content. It handles payment processing for x402 protocol, payment limits, and 3P wallet integrations with Coinbase CDP and Stripe (Privy).
* api-change:``bedrock-agentcore-control``: Launching AgentCore payments - a capability that provides secure, instant microtransaction payments for AI agents to access paid APIs, MCP servers, and content. It handles payment processing for x402 protocol, payment limits, and 3P wallet integrations with Coinbase CDP and Stripe (Privy).
* api-change:``ec2``: DescribeInstanceTypes now accepts an IncludeUnsupportedInRegion parameter. When set, the response also lists instance types that are not available in the current Region. Each instance type includes a SupportedInRegion field indicating its regional availability.
* api-change:``guardduty``: This is a documentation update
* api-change:``invoicing``: Updated ListInvoiceSummaries API to add new ReceiverRole filter in Request and Response
* api-change:``route53resolver``: Adds supports for DNS64 on inbound endpoints and IPv6 forwarding through the internet gateway (IGW) on outbound endpoints, making it easier to manage hybrid DNS across IPv4 and IPv6 networks.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 1.43.5
   ```
   ======

* api-change:``bedrock-agentcore-control``: Adds support for bring-your-own file system in AgentCore Runtime. Developers can mount Amazon S3 Files and Amazon EFS access points directly into agent sessions using filesystemConfigurations.
* api-change:``endpoint-rules``: Update endpoint-rules client to latest version
* api-change:``glue``: Adds support for a CustomLogGroupPrefix parameter in StartDataQualityRulesetEvaluationRun to specify custom CloudWatch log group paths, and a RulesetName filter in ListDataQualityRulesetEvaluationRuns to filter evaluation runs by ruleset name.
* api-change:``imagebuilder``: The ImportDiskImage API now enforces a maximum character limit of 128 characters on the image name field.
* api-change:``lexv2-models``: Amazon Lex V2 introduces audio filler support for speech-to-speech bots. Configure melody or typing sounds that play during backend processing to reduce perceived latency and maintain a natural conversational experience for callers.
* api-change:``mwaa``: Amazon MWAA now supports a PublicAndPrivate webserver access mode. The Airflow web server is accessible over both public and private endpoints, enabling workers in VPCs without internet access to reach the Task API privately while retaining public access to the Airflow UI.
* api-change:``s3``: Validate outpost access point resource name
* api-change:``sagemaker``: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now returns ImageVersionStatus in DescribeCluster, DescribeClusterNode, and ListClusterNodes responses, indicating whether cluster instances are running the latest available image version.
* api-change:``securityhub``: Release GenerateRecommendedPolicyV2 and GetRecommendedPolicyV2 APIs. This supports generating and retrieving policy recommendations to remediate unused permissions findings that are now being supported on Security Hub.

## lunch-money A Go CLI for Lunch Money's official v2 OpenAPI — offline SQLite store, subscription detection, and bulk smart retag the web UI cannot do. **API:** lunch-money | **Category:** payments | **Press version:** 4.5.2 **Spec:** Official v2 OpenAPI `@lunch-money/v2-api-spec@2.11.0-preview.2` (11,733 lines, 59 operations, 16 resource tags) ### Publication Path New print — no merged CLI and no existing PR matched this slug. ### CLI Shape ``` Lunch Money CLI — A Go CLI for Lunch Money's official v2 OpenAPI — offline SQLite store, subscription detection, and bulk smart retag the… Highlights (not in the official API docs): • transactions subscriptions Find regular-cadence merchant charges that are not yet linked to a recurring item, so you can promote them before subscription creep sneaks past you. • recurring missing List recurring items whose next expected date falls in the requested month but have no matching transaction yet, so you can catch missed bills. • transactions duplicates Detect near-duplicate transactions in a window (same merchant, amount within tolerance, date within range) so you can group or delete them in bulk. • accounts stale Surface manual accounts and manual crypto whose balance has not been updated in N days, so net worth stays honest. • net-worth on Reconstruct net worth at any historical date by walking balance_history across every account type, with last-known-balance carry-forward where needed. • transactions retag Match transactions by regex on payee/notes via local FTS, preview the affected set, then bulk-apply tag/category changes via the API. • triage Pull all unreviewed transactions, compute a suggested category from prior categorizations of the same merchant, and optionally mass-apply the suggestion. • budgets burn For the current budget period, project end-of-month spend per category at the current linear rate and flag categories projected to overshoot. • changed List everything created or edited in the local store since a cutoff (e.g. --since 8h, --since 2026-05-01). Use at session start to orient before taking action. Agent mode: add --agent to any command for JSON output + non-interactive mode. Health check: run 'lunch-money-pp-cli doctor' to verify auth and connectivity. See README.md or the bundled SKILL.md for recipes. Usage: lunch-money-pp-cli [command] Available Commands: accounts Audit locally synced accounts agent-context Emit structured JSON describing this CLI for agents analytics Run analytics queries on locally synced data api Browse all API endpoints by interface name auth Manage authentication for Lunch Money budgets View settings and modify budget amounts.

Use the [/summary](#tag/summary) endpoint to view the budget details... changed List everything that changed since a cutoff time (local store) completion Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell doctor Check CLI health export Export data to JSONL or JSON for backup, migration, or analysis feedback Record feedback about this CLI (local by default; upstream opt-in) help Help about any command import Import data from JSONL file via API create/upsert calls me Get details about the user associated with the supplied authorization token. net-worth Reconstruct net worth from local balance history profile Named sets of flags saved for reuse recurring-items Work with recurring items search Full-text search across synced data or live API summary Retrieves a summary of the user's budget. Use this endpoint to access budget configuration details and performance... sync Sync API data to local SQLite for offline search and analysis tail Stream live changes by polling the API at regular intervals transactions Work with transactions triage Suggest categories for unreviewed local transactions version Print version which Find the command that implements a capability workflow Compound workflows that combine multiple API operations Flags: --agent Set all agent-friendly defaults (--json --compact --no-input --no-color --yes) --compact Return only key fields (id, name, status, timestamps) for minimal token usage --config string Config file path --csv Output as CSV (table and array responses) --data-source string Data source for read commands: auto (live with local fallback), live (API only), local (synced data only) (default "auto") --deliver string Route output to a sink: stdout (default), file:, webhook: --dry-run Show request without sending -h, --help help as a successful no-op --json Output as JSON --no-cache Bypass response cache --no-color Disable colored output --no-input Disable all interactive prompts (for CI/agents) --plain Output as plain tab-separated text --profile string Apply values from a saved profile (see 'lunch-money-pp-cli profile list') --quiet Bare output, one value per line --rate-limit float Max requests per second (0 to disable) --select string Comma-separated fields to include in output (e.g. --select id,name,status) --timeout duration Request timeout (default 30s) -v, --version version for lunch-money-pp-cli --yes ## Summary

Per UAT:
- Rename Nudge title \"Settlement Reminder\" → \"Debt Reminder\"
- Add inline deep-link button to nudge / settle DMs that opens the recipient's TMA on the People tab with the relevant CounterpartyBalanceSheet auto-opened
- Tree indent fix: leading 3-space indent under the last chat was collapsing in Telegram iOS pre-blocks; switched both indent paths to NBSP (U+00A0)

## Key changes

**New util:** \`packages/trpc/src/utils/counterpartyDeepLink.ts\`
- \`numericIdToUuid\` / \`uuidToNumericId\` round-trip — the existing v1 deep-link encoder only accepts UUID-shaped entity IDs, so we pad the Telegram userId hex to 32 chars and reverse on the TMA.
- \`buildCounterpartyDeepLinkPayload\` + \`buildMiniAppUrl\` helpers.
- 6 unit tests.

**Procedure changes** (\`settleAllWithUser\`, \`nudgeCounterparty\`):
- Bypass \`createBroadcast\` in favour of direct \`ctx.teleBot.sendMessage\` so we can pass \`reply_markup\`. Broadcast bookkeeping was overkill for these point-to-point operational DMs.
- \`sendDm\` signature gains optional \`InlineKb\` arg.
- New \`deps.getBotUsername\` (cached per request) so the URL uses the live bot username without an env var.

**Web side:**
- \`useStartParams\` and the v1 encoder \`entityType\` widened to include \`\"c\"\` (counterparty).
- \`chat.index.tsx\` new consumer branch for \`entity_type === \"c\"\` → navigates to \`/chat\` with \`selectedTab=groups\` + \`openCounterpartyId\`.
- \`UserBalancesTab\` new optional \`autoOpenCounterpartyId\` prop; sheet auto-opens once after the list loads (guarded by useRef so back-nav doesn't re-open).

**Smoke:** \`scripts/smoke-cross-group-dm.ts\` extended to send samples with the inline button so the deep link can be exercised end-to-end without going through the real settle/nudge flows.

## Test plan
- [x] Full trpc suite 188/188 (new counterpartyDeepLink.spec + updated nudge/settle/template specs)
- [x] Smoke samples sent to @bubuding0809 — tree indent renders correctly on iOS, inline buttons appear
- [ ] Tap \"💁 Open Balances\" on a real nudge DM → TMA opens, lands on People tab, CounterpartyBalanceSheet auto-opens for the nudge sender
- [ ] Tap \"📊 View Balances\" on a settle DM → same flow; if the counterparty is now zero-balance, sheet silently no-ops (correct empty state)

## Summary

Clears 14 `[unqualified]` warnings across 2 files by qualifying parent-element property access with the owning element's id.

### WirelessDetails.qml (10 lines)

Top-level is `DeviceDetails { id: root; readonly property var network: ... }`. Bare `network` accesses inside function bodies (`checkSavedProfile`, `updateDeviceDetails`, etc.) and the `device: network` binding all need `root.network`.

Token-protected the following so they were not double-qualified or otherwise corrupted:
- the declaration (`readonly property var network:`)
- the string literal `"...this network"` (line 68)
- existing `root.network` qualified accesses
- `session.network` references (different `network` from the `session` chain)

### LauncherPane.qml (3 lines)

The file contains two `displayedApp` properties in different scopes:

- Line 403: `property var displayedApp: null` on `rightLauncherPane` — bare references on lines 410, 421, 422 resolve to this and are NOT flagged.
- Line 515: `readonly property var displayedApp: ...` on `appDetailsLayout` (a nested ColumnLayout).

Lines 524/534/564 are inside `appDetailsLayout`'s children and qmllint flags their bare `displayedApp` access. Replaced with `appDetailsLayout.displayedApp` — matches the qualification pattern already used at lines 549/599/607/611/631/639/643 in the same scope.

## Scope

- [x] Fork-only change (lives in new files or clearly delimited blocks)
- [ ] Upstream-friendly change (should it be proposed to
  `caelestia-dots/shell` first? If not, justify below.)

Same as previous PRs in this series — `modules/controlcenter/` unchanged vs. upstream. Candidate for upstream after Phase 2.

## User-facing impact

- [x] No user-facing change.
- [ ] New behavior is opt-in via an additive key in `shell.json`; defaults preserve prior behavior.
- [ ] Breaking change to `shell.json`, IPC, or CLI surface.

QML id qualification doesn't change runtime resolution.

## Constitution checks (Principle II)

- [x] `qmlformat` clean on both modified files.
- [x] `clang-format` clean (no C++).
- [x] `qml-lint-conventions.py` clean.
- [ ] `cmake --build build` — not re-run; QML-only.
- [ ] CI workflows green — CI will verify.

## Testing

Verified pre-commit:
- 2 files changed, 13 insertions, 13 deletions (exact 1:1 rename).
- WirelessDetails preserved lines spot-checked: declaration (line 17), string literal (line 68), session.network references, all root.network unchanged.
- LauncherPane preserved lines spot-checked: rightLauncherPane scope (lines 403, 410, 421, 422), inner declaration (line 515), already-qualified access (line 549).

## CHANGELOG.md

- [ ] Will batch with other Phase 2 cleanup PRs.

## Rationale for divergence (if upstream-friendly but kept in fork)

Same as previous cleanup PRs.

## Related

- Fifth in the batch-mode `qmllint` cleanup series (after #7, #8, #9, #10).
- Together with #9 + #10, clears `rootPane` (86), `network` (9), and `displayedApp` (5) — 100 of 237 `[unqualified]` findings.
- Remaining `[unqualified]` work: `modelData` (101 — needs delegate ids), `itemMargin`/`itemRadius`/`isCurrent` (smaller groups, most need element ids added first), ComponentBehavior (4 — pragma fix).

author: tnptm
body:
This pull request introduces a comprehensive system for tracking and enforcing OpenSky API credit usage by implementing a multi-bucket credit tracker, updating configuration, and integrating credit enforcement into the main tracking workflow. The most important changes are grouped below:

**Credit Tracking System Implementation:**

* Added a new `CreditsTracker` class in `src/credits_tracker.py` to manage and enforce OpenSky's independent credit buckets (states, tracks, flights), including automatic window resets and blocking when limits are reached.

**Configuration Updates:**

* Added `OPENSKY_CREDITS` to `.env.example` and parsed it in `src/config.py` to allow configuration of daily credit limits per bucket. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a3046da0d15a27e89f2afe639b25748a7ad4d9290af3e7b1b6c1a5533c8f0a8cR21-R24) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-24a3fe5c783755412cb9de83238b4dfd0699345bf50dcadc3ec23c6749361592R23-R24)

**Integration into Tracker Workflow:**

* Updated `src/tracker.py` to instantiate and pass a `CreditsTracker` instance through the main loop and ghost processing logic, enforcing credit charges for both state polling and track fetching. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-229deb342c5697840c90530aa1cd46644b4ccacda0439f830d30cf93fd1301f5R19) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-229deb342c5697840c90530aa1cd46644b4ccacda0439f830d30cf93fd1301f5R102) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-229deb342c5697840c90530aa1cd46644b4ccacda0439f830d30cf93fd1301f5R143-R144) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-229deb342c5697840c90530aa1cd46644b4ccacda0439f830d30cf93fd1301f5R157) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-229deb342c5697840c90530aa1cd46644b4ccacda0439f830d30cf93fd1301f5L163-R180) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-229deb342c5697840c90530aa1cd46644b4ccacda0439f830d30cf93fd1301f5L200-R207)

**Documentation:**

* Added `src/docs/credit_rules.md` to clearly explain OpenSky's multi-bucket credit system, per-request costs, and practical usage math for users.
